01 · Context

A modular, consolidated model

The application brings workload, Health, resilience, investigation and fault-injection work into one workspace. The first phase establishes a common model and operation contract before implementing persistence, collectors, authorization, command dispatch, orchestration or a console UI.

This reference describes contract revision 2, based on main at 20650d3. It incorporates the explicit correction that all entities are versioned and all diagrams use Draw.io. The previous AWS analyses remain pinned independently to d926a81.

One entity, one version contract

Every entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. A material change appends the next immutable representation of the same identity. Owned values share their owner's version; no Version or Revision resource is introduced.

Exact history, explicit live navigation

EntityRef pins kind, id and version. EntityIdentity intentionally follows a continuing identity. Historical reads never substitute current content, and current authorization still applies.

Evidence has a clear owner

Source retains a scoped native representation. Observation records seeing it. Projection records a versioned interpretation with exact inputs and coverage. Snapshot closes a historical capture over exact entity versions.

Operations express intent

Closed request DTOs expose deliberate edits or commands. Server metadata, provider state and derived conclusions are not arbitrary writable fields. Provider dispatch, observed effects and local operator work retain separate meanings.

Contract and examples, not a running service.

All 108 operations are marked CONTRACT_ONLY. Examples are synthetic, independently valid situations with their own prior-head assumptions; they are not one chronological transaction log and no provider call was made to produce this document.

Source-backed design guidance is recorded in Design principles. This document uses repository evidence and the user’s explicit correction; it does not claim knowledge of inaccessible past conversations.

Consolidation path. Review the unified model and exact contracts first; implement retained reads and trusted ingestion (P2), durable commands and replay (P3), then workflow execution and its effect-reconciliation gates (P4). The application shell composes those verified capabilities. Implementation gates and acceptance evidence.

Coverage has been audited separately from name matching.

The earlier crosswalk records 174 rows and 340 aliases. Those are not entity counts or complete normalization proofs. The coverage audit distinguishes substantive source entities, diagram constructs, partial typed bindings and retained-only content. The mapping rules define when each representation is appropriate.

02 · Shared contract

How the model and API behave

ConcernShared rule
TransportPOST /; application/x-amz-json-1.1; PascalCase operation names and lowerCamelCase JSON members.
TargetX-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.<Operation>
SuccessHTTP 200 with the operation-specific output. For an asynchronous command, this means admission or receipt replay, not provider completion.
ScopeWorkspace and actor come from trusted authenticated context. Parent IDs and Connection references select scoped objects; they confer no authority.
VersionsGet<Entity>(version?) selects an exact immutable representation when supplied, or the current head once when omitted. ListEntityVersions returns exact references in descending version order.
ConcurrencyexpectedVersion guards the named entity, including owned values. Provider commands also require exact source context where declared. A conflict admits no new mutation.
ReplayEvery mutation requires a clientToken. Same scoped operation/token with identical intent replays its exact receipt before current-head checks. Changed intent with the same token conflicts.
ListsmaxResults is 1–100, default 20. Tokens bind the initial 15-minute publication, principal, query and selected parents. An empty page alone does not end traversal.
BoundsRequest body ≤ 1 MiB, response budget ≤ 8 MiB, plus each schema's field and collection bounds. Large content uses managed artifact references.
TimeFinite epoch seconds, maximum millisecond precision. Local publication, provider update, observation, derivation and capture times remain distinct.
PresenceOmitted, null, known empty, known zero, unavailable and not requested retain distinct meanings. clearFields is an explicit local clearing operation.
CompatibilityV2 is an explicit breaking correction of the proposed V1 contract. Reused operation names do not imply wire compatibility.

Authentication, authorization enforcement and SDK compatibility remain implementation work. The selector/media-type pattern is an AWS RPC style facade; catalog permissions are proposed console capabilities, not AWS IAM action names. Complete protocol and its primary references.

Write authority and effect

CategoryMeaning
READRead retained records, exact history or a documented current selector.
LOCAL_COMMANDChange application-owned state or create a capture/publication and durable receipt.
INGESTRecord collector-owned collection, source and observation facts.
DERIVECompute a projection from exact authorized inputs and trusted rule identity.
PROVIDER_COMMANDAdmit a narrow external intent; dispatch and reconciliation establish later outcomes.
EXECUTION_COMMANDAdmit or cancel an application Run; execution, acceptance and cleanup remain separate.

Reference and ownership rules

ValueUse
EntityRefExact kind/id/version for retained evidence, command results, admission bindings and snapshot members.
EntityIdentityExplicit live navigation or a continuing WorkItem target; never substitute it for a historical pin.
EvidenceRefExact Source, Observation, Projection or Snapshot reference, optionally with a typed locator.
Owned valueNo independent identity, version counter or CRUD endpoint. A change is a change to the containing entity.

Versioning does not create write access. Collector and workflow entities advance under their authority; sealed facts retain immutable history. A Source A → B → A content sequence publishes versions 1 → 2 → 3, while an unchanged consecutive poll may reuse the current Source version in a new Observation. A Run pins one PUBLISHED Scenario representation even when the current Scenario head is a later draft.

Snapshot members close over declared exact references. Structural parent identities do not silently pull current parent fields into history. Access to any historical evidence closure is re-authorized at read time.

03 · Use cases

Follow the work across modules

These illustrative journeys combine the declared operations. They describe the intended application behavior; provider dispatch and runtime guarantees still require the implementation gates above.

01 · Build the workload catalog without implying a provider edit

A platform owner registers a checkout system and its customer journey, then attaches a service to those local catalog identities.

Entities. System, UserJourney, Service, Resource, Command.

  1. Create the System and UserJourney with separate intent tokens; use returned canonical IDs.
  2. Create the Service with its owned membership set. Read before editing and guard the Service head with expectedVersion.
  3. Use the durable receipt and exact returned versions. A catalog edit does not rename or create a native AWS service.

Operations. CreateSystem, CreateUserJourney, CreateService, UpdateService, GetCommand.

Result. One local catalog writer owns service membership, while verified provider bindings preserve the distinction between application and native identities.

02 · Explain whether a Health impact is current, stale or unsupported

An operator needs a qualified impact view for a service after receiving an account-scoped Health event.

Entities. HealthEvent, EventContext, EntityImpact, Collection, ReadAttempt, Source, Observation, Projection.

  1. The trusted collector starts a fixed collection and records read-attempt settlement and observed source evidence.
  2. Complete the collection with independent pagination, detail, identity and claim-coverage dimensions; a quiet or empty response is not enough to establish absence.
  3. Navigate event → context → impacts, then inspect the service-status projection and its exact inputs. Preserve account/public/organization context instead of multiplying one event by delivery count.

Operations. StartCollection, RecordReadAttempt, IngestObservation, CompleteCollection, ListHealthEvents, ListEventContexts, ListEntityImpacts, GetServiceStatus, GetSource.

Result. The operator can trace a displayed impact to its native evidence and see what the collection actually established.

03 · Investigate a resilience finding and record remediation work

An assessment reveals a service-scoped finding; the operator needs the recommendation context and a separately owned work lifecycle.

Entities. Service, ResilienceAssessment, Finding, Recommendation, Snapshot, WorkItem, Command.

  1. Admit an assessment against the exact service/source context, then reconcile Command and collected assessment evidence.
  2. Read the finding under its Service parent and inspect recommendation and captured assessment context. Add estimates through Recommendation enrichment using the Recommendation version.
  3. Create a WorkItem for assignment and completion. Record verification with exact supporting evidence; technical assessment completion or local closure alone does not prove remediation.

Operations. StartResilienceAssessment, GetCommand, ListResilienceAssessments, ListFindings, ListRecommendations, GetSnapshot, UpdateRecommendationEnrichment, CreateWorkItem, RecordWorkItemVerification.

Result. Assessment posture, recommendation metadata and operator work state remain independently intelligible.

04 · Decide an investigation approval and resume deliberately

A DevOps execution pauses on a specific tool approval request while its task memberships and journal continue to be observed.

Entities. AgentSpace, Investigation, Execution, JournalRecord, ApprovalRequest, Command.

  1. Start the investigation in the selected AgentSpace and obtain its observed task/execution context from retained reads.
  2. Inspect the exact ApprovalRequest, source and action digest. Submit a deliberate decision with the relevant head and source preconditions.
  3. Resume only with the exact definitive successful decision Command version and matching approval context. Reconcile uncertain decision or resume effects instead of blindly resending.

Operations. StartInvestigation, ListInvestigations, ListExecutions, ListJournalRecords, GetApprovalRequest, DecideApproval, GetCommand, ResumeExecution.

Result. Approval intent, provider decision, resume and actual tool effects retain separate evidence and authority.

05 · Publish a scenario, run that version and inspect exact attempts

A reliability engineer authors a workflow that performs an experiment and evaluates explicit criteria.

Entities. Scenario, Run, StepRun, StepAttempt, Snapshot, Experiment, Projection.

  1. Edit a draft under Scenario.expectedVersion and publish it to resolve trusted operation/schema locks.
  2. Admit a Run with the exact PUBLISHED Scenario, subject and Connection versions. Inspect the atomic Run, Snapshot and StepRun response.
  3. Read children through the selected parent version. Preserve skipped zero-attempt steps and the admitted required-criterion denominator when interpreting evaluation.

Operations. CreateScenario, UpdateScenario, PublishScenario, StartRun, GetRun, ListRunSteps, ListStepAttempts, GetExperiment, GetProjection.

Result. Later scenario edits, child transitions or evaluator knowledge cannot silently change the historical admitted run.

06 · Cancel a run while an external experiment may still be active

An operator requests cancellation during execution and needs to distinguish the local fence from remote cessation and cleanup.

Entities. Run, StepRun, StepAttempt, Experiment, Command.

  1. Request cancellation against the Run head with a stable intent token. Replay the original receipt before considering a new intent.
  2. Inspect exact attempts and known external-effect references. Use the explicit StopExperiment contract only when authorized and its target/source preconditions are established.
  3. Observe terminal native state and required finalization independently. Non-creating reconciliation handles uncertain effects; cancellation cannot reissue a creating Start merely to discover a lost handle.

Operations. RequestRunCancellation, GetCommand, GetRun, ListRunSteps, ListStepAttempts, StopExperiment, GetExperiment.

Result. A cancellation request remains visible without being mistaken for completed remote cleanup or proven recovery.

07 · Reconstruct a past decision after the current state changes

An auditor wants the service, source and interpretation used for an earlier operational decision.

Entities. Service, Source, Observation, Projection, Snapshot, WorkItem.

  1. Capture a closed set of exact authorized members and their declared evidence closure at the chosen cutoff.
  2. Retrieve the Snapshot and resolve exact references through the normal typed getters, or enumerate an entity's history before selecting a specific version.
  3. Recheck current authority. Unknown or unavailable versions remain explicit outcomes; a getter never substitutes the current head for missing history.

Operations. CaptureSnapshot, GetSnapshot, ListEntityVersions, GetService, GetSource, GetObservation, GetProjection, GetWorkItem.

Result. The historical explanation remains tied to the representations available at the decision, with unavailable evidence made visible.

Foundation · entity

Workspace

#
Versioned entityAPPLICATION8 fields

The application authorization and configuration boundary for the consolidated console. It gives the seven modules one trusted scope without treating an AWS account, organization or DevOps AgentSpace as the product tenant.

Logical identity
workspaceId
Retained record
workspaceId + version
Owner / authority
The application owns its name, enabled module set and captured organization context. The authenticated server establishes workspace scope; a caller cannot grant access by supplying a workspaceId.
Lifecycle
Workspace versions record changes to this boundary and its configuration. Historical entities continue to belong to the same stable workspaceId, while access to retained versions is checked against current authorization. The current operation catalog exposes reads and version history; it does not imply a public Workspace creation or administration API.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Workspace

Use cases

One portfolio, several AWS scopes

Context. An operations team needs Health and Resilience information for resources in several accounts.

Use. Use one Workspace as the authorization boundary and separate Connection values for the authorized collection paths; retain account and organization context as scoped values.

Result. The team can navigate a consolidated portfolio without confusing tenancy with AWS resource ownership.

Enable a module deliberately

Context. A workspace adds investigation views alongside its existing workload catalog.

Use. Publish the permitted configuration as a new Workspace version with an updated enabledModules set.

Result. The same workspace identity acquires the module configuration while older representations remain interpretable.

Invariants and interpretation

  • Workspace is distinct from AgentSpace and from provider account/Region ownership.
  • Every entity, including Workspace, has a stable ID, version, createdAt and updatedAt.
  • A retained historical version does not preserve an obsolete permission grant.

Where it was defined and how it was used

trusted workspace, application IDs

Origin type: application-boundary.

Previous use. The workflow model scoped opaque application IDs and concurrency/authorization to a trusted workspace established by server context. It did not define a complete Workspace entity.

Consolidation decision. There is no one-to-one prior Workspace entity. Consolidation promotes that cross-module authorization boundary to a versioned entity.

aws/fis/analysis/workflow/model.md

Account, Organization, OrganizationMembership

Origin type: external-context.

Previous use. The Health model retained account, organization and membership validity as external context around event impact.

Consolidation decision. These contribute organization context owned by Workspace; none becomes the workspace identity or a new account entity.

Foundation · entity

Connection

#
Versioned entityAPPLICATION11 fields

A versioned reference to an authorized access path: provider, external credential reference, allowed scopes and authorization-context key. It tells collection how access was obtained without redefining the identity of the observed AWS object.

Logical identity
workspaceId + connectionId
Retained record
workspaceId + connectionId + version
Owner / authority
Application commands create and change Connection configuration. Credential material stays in a separate secret system; the model stores only credentialRef and scoped access metadata.
Lifecycle
CreateConnection admits a new configuration; UpdateConnection uses its expectedVersion. Observations and Collections pin the Connection version actually used. Disabling or rotating a connection changes later access behavior without making a second copy of every resource observed through it.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Connection

Use cases

Rotate the collection role

Context. The role used for reading one account is replaced.

Use. Update Connection under its version precondition and have subsequent Collections pin the new version.

Result. Old evidence still explains the access context used at collection time, while the canonical resource identity remains stable.

Compare two access paths

Context. Two authorized connections return the same native event or resource.

Use. Compare the fully scoped native identity independently of connectionId and keep each read occurrence with its own Connection and authorization context.

Result. The console avoids duplicate domain objects while retaining permission-sensitive provenance.

  • Changing a principal does not change native resource identity.
  • An allowed scope is an access constraint, not proof that an API read succeeded.

SourceConnection, OrganizationHealthAccess

Origin type: application-access-context.

Previous use. SourceConnection recorded caller, account/organization scope, capabilities and integration readiness so unavailable Health reads could be explained.

Consolidation decision. Connection consolidates the access path; observed organization access and capability evidence remain qualified context rather than credentials or native owner identity.

ConnectionContext, OwningScope

Origin type: application-access-context.

Previous use. ConnectionContext represented an authorization-sensitive access path separately from the partition/account/Region owning scope.

Consolidation decision. The distinction becomes common across every module, with exact Connection versions in collection and observation history.

Foundation · entity

Resource

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR11 fields

The canonical inventory identity for a sufficiently identified external resource. Resource carries scoped native identity, identity stability, selected observation and explicit matching evidence; it is not a universal wrapper around every provider object or selected target.

Logical identity
workspaceId + resourceId
Retained record
workspaceId + resourceId + version
Owner / authority
A trusted collector or normalizer publishes Resource representations. Local operators can inspect identity and matching provenance but cannot assert provider health or invent inventory existence by editing it.
Lifecycle
A stable resourceId survives new inventory observations and publishes later versions. A provisional or run-scoped identity remains qualified until matching evidence establishes its relationship to a stable resource; an alias match does not erase the original evidence.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Resource

Use cases

Resolve an affected database

Context. A Health entity contains a resource identifier that might identify the database in inventory.

Use. Use an evidenced ResourceMatch from EntityImpact to Resource and retain the Health identity independently.

Result. An operator can navigate from impact to inventory while seeing whether the match is confirmed or unresolved.

Preserve overlapping FIS selections

Context. Two experiment selectors include the same instance, while another selector returns a pod with only run-scoped identity.

Use. Deduplicate the established instance Resource but retain every selector membership; keep the pod identity qualified by its available scope and incarnation evidence.

Result. Resource counts remain distinct from membership counts and do not merge unrelated pod incarnations.

Fields

resourceIdRequiredId

Stable logical identity of this Resource; the entity version selects a retained representation.

workspaceIdRequiredId

Trusted application scope. Request bodies cannot select a tenant.

Maximum length: 4096

Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Invariants and interpretation

  • A provider name, DNS label or unqualified version is not a resource identity.
  • Resource identity and access Connection are independent.
  • Selected by FIS does not establish fault application; affected by Health does not establish global resource health.

Where it was defined and how it was used

InventoryResource, EntityResourceMatch

Origin type: external-resource.

Previous use. Health affected constructs could match zero, one or several inventory resources through an evidence-bearing bridge. Resource names, tags and owners came from external inventory.

Consolidation decision. Resource centralizes inventory identity while EntityImpact keeps its separate event-relative identity and owned matching values.

ResourceIdentity, ResolvedTarget

Origin type: external-resource.

Previous use. FIS targetInformation was retained in full; a resource-type adapter could normalize identity only when the returned information supported it.

Consolidation decision. The common Resource is optional. Experiment retains selector memberships even when no stable Resource can be established.

ServiceResource

Origin type: retained-provider-value.

Previous use. ServiceResource related a service-local resourceIdentifier to a descriptor and optional input source; global resolution required sufficient account, Region, type and identifier evidence.

Consolidation decision. The shared Resource replaces parallel global inventories without discarding service-local identifiers or unresolved references.

Foundation · entity

Collection

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR11 fields

One finite evidence-gathering pass over a fixed set of declared queries. Collection makes collection state, scope, times and qualified coverage first-class across all modules.

Logical identity
workspaceId + collectionId
Retained record
workspaceId + collectionId + version
Owner / authority
The trusted collector owns query execution and lifecycle publication. Each Collection pins its Connection version; queries and their fingerprints define the scope for the identity.
Lifecycle
StartCollection creates the pass. Lifecycle changes publish Collection versions, and CompleteCollection settles the requested pass with explicit coverage. Changing query definitions requires a new Collection identity, not an edit disguised as a lifecycle update.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Collection

Use cases

Hydrate findings after an assessment

Context. A new assessment triggers a paginated service finding list followed by detail reads.

Use. Retain one Collection with the list/detail query scopes, their ReadAttempts and independent pagination and hydration outcomes.

Result. A finished list can coexist with failed detail hydration without claiming complete recommendations.

Explain an empty target list

Context. FIS target enumeration returns no members.

Use. Combine the Collection query scope and page-chain outcome with separately retained resolution-ended evidence.

Result. The console distinguishes a scoped complete empty result from a premature or incomplete read.

Fields

Stable logical identity of this Collection; the entity version selects a retained representation.

workspaceIdRequiredId

endedAtRequiredAny of: Timestamp | nullUses the declared type and containing contract.
coverageRequiredArray of CoverageMaximum items: 1000

Invariants and interpretation

  • Fixed query definitions are part of Collection identity.
  • Completed pagination is not complete external history or an atomic multi-API snapshot.
  • Collection failures, detail gaps and identity resolution remain separate coverage dimensions.

Where it was defined and how it was used

CollectionPass, CoverageClaim

Origin type: application-collection.

Previous use. CollectionPass bounded an investigation reconciliation attempt; CoverageClaim stated what a query traversal had established and cited its read attempts.

Consolidation decision. Collection applies the same bounded-pass meaning to every module, with coverage retained as owned values and ordinary entity versions.

CollectionRun, CoverageAssessment

Origin type: application-collection.

Previous use. CollectionRun captured operation, filters, times, pagination and result state. CoverageAssessment explained stale or unavailable evidence.

Consolidation decision. Their shared collection mechanics become Collection without folding provider health into collection status.

FindingCapture

Origin type: application-collection.

Previous use. FindingCapture recorded service scope, filters, list pagination, detail hydration and optional qualified assessment correlation.

Consolidation decision. Collection retains those boundaries; neither the Collection nor Finding gains an unsupported assessment-ownership relationship.

Foundation · entity

ReadAttempt

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR19 fields

The durable record of one actual request attempt, including successful empty responses and failures. It preserves the exact request/response evidence and makes retry and pagination claims reviewable.

Logical identity
workspaceId + collectionId + readAttemptId
Retained record
workspaceId + readAttemptId + version
Owner / authority
The collector owns ReadAttempt under a Collection and queryKey. attemptNo describes retry order, not the entity version. The application retains provider request identifiers, errors and authorization context when supplied.
Lifecycle
RecordReadAttempt records the attempt and its request/response Sources. A running attempt can publish a settled representation under its own version. Once settled it is sealed; a retry is another attempt and later evidence does not reopen it.
Sealing rule
Lifecycle changes append versions. A settled/terminal record cannot be reopened; late reconciliation is new evidence and does not rewrite settled facts.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · ReadAttempt

Use cases

Retain a denied detail read

Context. The service summary was fetched but a subsequent detail request is denied.

Use. Record the failed ReadAttempt with query context, modeled error and retained request/response envelope when available.

Result. The missing detail is explained as unavailable rather than an empty successful result.

Audit a page traversal

Context. An operator asks whether every journal page was read.

Use. Inspect the sequence of attempts, opaque page tokens retained in Sources, returned counts and terminal page evidence.

Result. The coverage claim can be traced to actual requests, including retried pages.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Invariants and interpretation

  • No Observation is required for a request that returned no domain object.
  • EventBridge and stream receipts do not manufacture native ReadAttempts.
  • Settled attempts are immutable facts; failed is not equivalent to empty.

Where it was defined and how it was used

ReadAttempt

Origin type: application-collection-record.

Previous use. ReadAttempt represented one operation/page request even when no SourceObservation resulted; query fingerprints excluded the changing nextToken.

Consolidation decision. The same entity becomes shared infrastructure with universal versions and exact requestSource/responseSource references.

aws/devops-agent/analysis/annexes/Investigation_Data_Model.md

CollectionItemError, CollectionRun

Origin type: owned-error-and-collection.

Previous use. Health collections retained item-level failedSet errors, including errors inside a successful HTTP response.

Consolidation decision. ReadAttempt and its owned error/response evidence retain these outcomes without treating transport success as complete domain success.

Verified source coverage · 10 contributing constructs

These are source concepts contributing to this entity or its evidence. A target entity name does not establish complete normalization of every contributing concept.

Source conceptCoverageAssessment
health · CollectionItemErrorPARTIALRaw response evidence can preserve failedSet. ReadAttempt.error is one ReadError with code/message/retryable/request ID and has neither a collection of item errors nor event/account item identity.
health · CollectionRunNORMALIZEDCollection owns fixed typed queries and explicit coverage; ReadAttempt records individual request/response attempts including empty success and failure.
health · SourceObservationNORMALIZEDSource owns retained content versions and Observation owns the receipt occurrence with exact references and independent clocks. Repeated reads of identical content do not create a second logical domain entity.
resilience-hub · FindingCapturePARTIALCollection/ReadAttempt/Coverage normalize the query, attempts, intervals and list/detail dimensions. There is no explicit typed related-assessment plus correlationBasis value; using generic query filters or a generic subject alone would not preserve that qualified relation.
resilience-hub · FindingObservationNORMALIZEDSource representation/profile/operation identity and exact Observation/read-attempt links preserve the summary/detail distinction and capture provenance. Finding selects those exact records.
resilience-hub · TopologyEntityNORMALIZEDSnapshot(kind=TOPOLOGY) binds GraphContents and exact retained members with capture intervals/coverage. Collector completion remains distinct from an atomic provider snapshot; edge-property parity is assessed separately.
devops-agent · CollectionPassPARTIALCollection preserves stable identity, fixed query set, connection, lifecycle and time window. Its normalized record does not retain the prior explicitly required collector version or selection-policy identity.
devops-agent · ConnectionContextNORMALIZEDConnection and exact connection references preserve the access path, while attempts/observations retain the authorization-context key. Historical retrieval is checked against current authority.
devops-agent · ReadAttemptNORMALIZEDReadAttempt has typed identity, lifecycle, timestamps, provider request ID, counts/errors and exact request/nullable response Source references. Empty success and lost response remain distinct.
fis · TargetResolutionObservationNORMALIZEDExperiment.resolutionCoverage and Coverage explicitly separate resolution, pagination, detail, identity and claim dimensions; exact ReadAttempt refs retain request/response coverage evidence, and the named target-resolution profile retains source-specific details.

Foundation · entity

Source

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR18 fields

One logical retained source representation, identified independently of content digest or provider version. Source stores the original provider or adapter document so normalized entities and derived views can be explained and reprocessed.

Logical identity
workspaceId + sourceId
Retained record
workspaceId + sourceId + version
Logical key
workspaceId + identity + representation + profile + sourceOperation
Owner / authority
A trusted collector publishes Source representations under a registered identity/profile contract. Raw open JSON belongs here or in an exact artifact, not in writable extension bags on ordinary domain entities.
Lifecycle
Changed accepted content appends Source.version under the same sourceId; a repeated unchanged read creates another Observation of the current Source version. A content sequence A→B→A produces versions 1, 2 and 3. Native versions and content digests remain independent attributes.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Source

Use cases

Preserve a status reversal

Context. A Health impact is observed as PENDING, then RESOLVED, then PENDING again.

Use. Retain three Source versions and the Observations that selected them, even if the first and third payload bytes can share storage.

Result. History records the actual sequence rather than rewinding to an old digest.

Keep summary and detail honest

Context. A list response omits recommendation detail that was fetched earlier.

Use. Retain SUMMARY and DETAIL as distinct source representations with their own versions and observation clocks.

Result. The newer summary cannot erase or artificially refresh older detailed evidence.

Selects inline JSON or a managed artifact. INLINE may contain legitimate JSON null; ARTIFACT requires its artifact reference.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Conditional and cross-field schema rules 
{
  "allOf": [
    {
      "if": {
        "properties": {
          "payloadStorage": {
            "const": "ARTIFACT"
          }
        }
      },
      "then": {
        "properties": {
          "payload": {
            "type": "null"
          },
          "artifact": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ArtifactRef"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

Invariants and interpretation

  • Content digest, provider nativeVersion and sourceId answer different questions.
  • INLINE payload storage preserves a real JSON null; ARTIFACT explicitly selects an external payload reference.
  • Unknown provider fields remain retained and read tolerant; write inputs remain closed and typed.

Where it was defined and how it was used

SourceRevision, JournalRecordRevision

Origin type: retained-evidence.

Previous use. The investigation study separated distinct retained payload revisions from read occurrences, with hash/canonicalization metadata and native version retained as a fact.

Consolidation decision. The version-only SourceRevision class is removed. Source is the logical entity; each representation uses the common version contract.

aws/devops-agent/analysis/annexes/Investigation_Data_Model.md

SourceObservation, EventRevision, EntityRevision

Origin type: retained-evidence.

Previous use. The Health model retained raw messages/API responses and contextual event/entity evidence, separate from notification delivery.

Consolidation decision. Source holds retained content while Observation holds the occurrence, avoiding a different history mechanism for each Health entity.

aws/health/analysis/report.md

FindingObservation, SUMMARY, DETAIL

Origin type: retained-evidence.

Previous use. Finding observations retained distinct summary/detail payloads and field presence so failed hydration did not look like an empty recommendation array.

Consolidation decision. Registered Source representations preserve those meanings with shared exact version references.

Foundation · entity

Observation

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR15 fields

A genuine occurrence in which one exact Source version was read or received. Observation answers when and through which access/channel context evidence was seen; it does not create a new logical provider object on each poll.

Logical identity
workspaceId + observationId
Retained record
workspaceId + observationId + version
Owner / authority
The collector owns observations and their occurrence identity. API observations pin the actual ReadAttempt and Connection; event, stream and local receipts retain their real channel context without inventing a request.
Lifecycle
IngestObservation retains a new receipt with universal version metadata. Replaying the same ingestion intent returns its original receipt; a second genuine read or delivery is a new Observation even when it refers to unchanged source content. Source time, transport time, observedAt and expiry remain distinct.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Observation

Use cases

Record a fresh poll of unchanged content

Context. The same FIS experiment body is returned by a later successful read.

Use. Create another Observation of the same Source version and pin that later request and connection.

Result. The console knows the object was checked again without inventing new content or new experiments.

Retain redundant notification deliveries

Context. Primary and backup Health notifications deliver the same logical page.

Use. Keep each genuine delivery occurrence as Observation evidence while Communication groups the logical page.

Result. Delivery audit remains complete and event/impact counts do not multiply.

Invariants and interpretation

  • Observation occurrence is not Source identity and observedAt is not a provider update time.
  • An exact ingestion replay is different from a later legitimate receipt.
  • Current access is checked when retained evidence is read.

Where it was defined and how it was used

SourceObservation

Origin type: application-observation.

Previous use. SourceObservation recorded one occurrence of a retained revision, allowing repeated polls to cite the same revision and failed reads to have none.

Consolidation decision. The concept becomes the shared Observation entity and selects an exact Source version rather than a separate revision entity.

aws/devops-agent/analysis/annexes/Investigation_Data_Model.md

SourceObservation, MessageDelivery

Origin type: application-observation.

Previous use. Health distinguished API/source evidence from delivery records and preserved independent provider update clocks.

Consolidation decision. Observation supplies the common receipt mechanism; delivery provenance remains channel-specific owned content.

aws/health/analysis/report.md

ExecutionEvidence, StateObservation, MetricObservation

Origin type: retained-evidence.

Previous use. FIS required source identity/location, event and ingestion times, action/selector/account associations and coverage for execution and workload evidence.

Consolidation decision. Observation and Source consolidate those retention mechanics while provider-specific associations and telemetry shapes remain in registered source profiles.

Foundation · entity

Projection

#
Versioned entityDERIVATION15 fields

A named derived view with a stable projectionId, exact subject/input versions, a registered result profile and a rule digest. Projection explains what a rule concluded from particular evidence without presenting derived state as a native provider fact.

Logical identity
workspaceId + projectionId
Retained record
workspaceId + projectionId + version
Logical key
workspaceId + projectionKey + profile + subject identity set
Owner / authority
The trusted derivation service publishes the typed result and its coverage. Supported profiles are EVALUATION, LIFECYCLE_EXPOSURE, INVESTIGATION_RESULT, SERVICE_STATUS and WORKSPACE_SUMMARY; profile values are owned data, not new entity families.
Lifecycle
PublishProjection appends a version when selected inputs or rules change. Existing versions remain immutable and independently readable. Recomputing a conclusion cannot freshen its source evidence, rewrite a sealed Run or make an unavailable historical input resolve to current head.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Projection

Use cases

Explain service attention

Context. A service has healthy recent telemetry, an older resilience assessment and incomplete finding detail.

Use. Publish SERVICE_STATUS using exact selected observations, captured context, coverage and the named aggregation rule.

Result. The UI can explain each attention reason while keeping health, posture and collection quality separate.

Reevaluate lifecycle exposure

Context. A corrected matching rule is applied to the same retained database deployment and lifecycle catalog.

Use. Publish a later LIFECYCLE_EXPOSURE Projection version over the exact deployment/catalog inputs and new ruleDigest.

Result. The revised interpretation is reviewable beside the earlier result without changing the original inventory evidence.

Maximum length: 4096

Version of the registered profile/schema; separate from the containing entity's version.

Invariants and interpretation

  • A result must retain exact input and subject versions, rule identity, cutoff and coverage.
  • A passed acceptance result does not imply remote cleanup or provider recovery.
  • Missing evidence remains unknown; empty denominators cannot manufacture success.

Where it was defined and how it was used

CurrentProjection, Service status projection

Origin type: derived-view.

Previous use. The Resilience UI selected typed health/posture evidence into current status with freshness, coverage and computation time.

Consolidation decision. Projection consolidates this interpretation layer and replaces local projection counters with ordinary entity versioning.

aws/resilience-hub/analysis/report.md

LifecycleExposure

Origin type: derived-view.

Previous use. LifecycleExposure joined independently observed component deployments to catalog milestones with matching method, confidence, policy and assessment time.

Consolidation decision. Lifecycle exposure becomes a typed Projection profile, preserving exact inputs rather than an extra lifecycle entity.

aws/health/analysis/report.md

ResultDocument, DerivedRevision, Derivation

Origin type: derived-view.

Previous use. ResultDocument and derived items retained source fragments, parser versions, selection policy and phase; richer result schemas were explicitly application proposals.

Consolidation decision. Projection replaces separate revision entities and retains only validated typed result profiles; open native journal content stays in Source.

aws/devops-agent/analysis/annexes/Investigation_Data_Model.md

ResilienceAssessment, AssessmentEvidence

Origin type: derived-view.

Previous use. The FIS study modeled workload evaluation separately from experiment execution using explicit criteria and external evidence.

Consolidation decision. This application evaluation maps to EVALUATION Projection; it is not the native Resilience Hub ResilienceAssessment entity.

resilience-hub · EffectivePolicyEvidencePARTIALThe typed policy snapshot and exact references preserve the composition and historical context. The selected effective-target content remains opaque, so the former inline target values are not fully normalized.
resilience-hub · EntityRefPARTIALExact canonical EntityRef and native SourceIdentity now have clear separate roles. The former source visibilityState/tombstone meaning has no explicit typed field or deletion-state mapping in these reference values.
resilience-hub · HealthObservationPARTIALObservation supplies typed receipt and expiry metadata, and StateDimension supplies a result badge with evidence. The console.monitoring.health payload is opaque; signal identity, measured window and typed measurements are not a normalized evidence contract.
resilience-hub · PostureObservationPARTIALSource/Observation preserve native evidence and ServiceStatus provides a separate posture dimension. The source component-outcome record and AWS_SERVICE/DERIVED_ATTENTION payload shapes are not bound to a normalized posture-observation schema.
devops-agent · ArtifactReferencePARTIALArtifactRef supplies a managed durable locator, content version/digest and availability, while AssetFile and EvidenceRef supply related context. devops-agent · CoverageClaimPARTIALCoverage normalizes independent pagination/detail/resolution/identity/claim dimensions, exact attempts, scope/window, evaluation time and rationale. It does not carry an explicit evaluation-policy identity/version, particularly when owned by Collection or Snapshot.
devops-agent · DerivationPARTIALProjection retains profileVersion and ruleDigest, which identify the selected computation. The source contract’s explicit derivation kind/assertion origin and separate parser/model metadata are not a typed owned Derivation shape.
devops-agent · DerivedRevisionPARTIALOrdinary Projection versions normalize five result profiles. Other DevOps renditions are retained as application-origin Source documents; the generic prior item-kind/assertion-origin contract is not a normalized Projection variant.
devops-agent · Event notificationRETAINED_ONLYThe lifecycle-event profile retains the full envelope and Observation carries channel/time. InvestigationResult normalizes selected completion-pointer meaning, not the complete lifecycle-event DTO.
devops-agent · InvestigationNORMALIZEDThe aggregate is represented by Investigation plus explicitly referenced executions, journal evidence, result projections and snapshots. It is not claimed to be a native AWS Investigation response.
devops-agent · ProjectionSourceNORMALIZEDEvidenceRef pins kind/id/version and EvidenceLocator supplies JSON pointer, asset path or text-range attribution. Distinct locators remain distinct citations without another entity.
devops-agent · ResultDocumentNORMALIZEDINVESTIGATION_RESULT binds InvestigationResult: selected/candidate sources, expected summary identity, phase, completion observation, availability and selection basis. Projection version/profileVersion/ruleDigest retain interpretation history.
devops-agent · SnapshotProjectionNORMALIZEDExact Snapshot members pin Projection versions; imported legacy rendition content is pinned as Source versions. This replaces the old projectionRevisionId without creating a separate rendition entity.
fis · AssessmentCriterionPARTIALStepDefinition can mark a required criterion and its locked operation/input schema, while CheckResult pins predicateDigest and coverage. No concrete metric/recovery criterion profile specifies the old FIS timing/unit/missing-data contract, especially for evaluation without a Run.
fis · AssessmentEvidenceNORMALIZEDCheckResult.evidenceRefs and Evaluation inputSnapshot/evidenceCutoffAt preserve exact citation and cutoff as owned values; no extra relationship entity is required.
fis · ResilienceAssessmentNORMALIZEDProjection profile EVALUATION binds Evaluation with exact subject, input Snapshot, evidence cutoff, verdict/finality and criterion results. It can evaluate a native Experiment without creating a workflow Run.
workflow · CheckResultNORMALIZEDStepAttempt.checkResult binds CheckResult, and Evaluation.criteria binds CriterionResult. Verdict, predicate digest, exact evidence, cutoff, claim type and coverage are typed. Optional explanatory actual/expected values remain a profile/documentation discrepancy rather than a missing verdict entity.
workflow · CriterionDenominatorNORMALIZEDAdmission.requiredCriterionKeys and Evaluation.requiredCriterionKeys bind the preserved set; semantic checks compare it with enabled required criterion definitions.

Foundation · entity

Snapshot

#
Versioned entityAPPLICATION14 fields

A deliberate closed capture of exact entity versions and profile-specific contents. Snapshot supports reproducible admission, historical investigation views, policy context, topology and evaluation inputs; ordinary entity history remains the normal version mechanism.

Logical identity
workspaceId + snapshotId
Retained record
workspaceId + snapshotId + version
Owner / authority
The capture service validates and owns the manifest, capture interval, coverage and digest. Graph nodes, edges and capture-specific values belong to the Snapshot rather than creating independent CRUD roots.
Lifecycle
CaptureSnapshot creates a new capture identity at version 1. The model supports guarded later corrections as new Snapshot versions, but that correction writer is deferred. A distinct capture occurrence has a distinct identity. Retained members never fall back to latest records.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Snapshot

Use cases

Reopen an investigation as reviewed

Context. An investigation continues after an operator reviewed its earlier result.

Use. Read the prior Snapshot manifest containing exact task/execution/journal/source/projection and collection evidence versions.

Result. The earlier reviewed result stays reproducible while later live work is visible separately.

Freeze run admission inputs

Context. A published Scenario is admitted against the current workload and connections.

Use. Create a RUN_INPUT Snapshot containing validated inputs, resolved bindings, enabled steps and required criteria with exact supporting versions.

Result. Later inventory or definition drift cannot silently change what was admitted; future runtime facts are not inserted into that admission capture.

Invariants and interpretation

  • Snapshot is a business capture, not a replacement for versioning every entity.
  • Every historical input required to interpret its contents must resolve in the exact retained closure.
  • Capture completion means collection over an interval; it does not assert atomic AWS state.
  • A RUN_INPUT capture cannot contain future terminal outcomes.

Where it was defined and how it was used

InvestigationSnapshot, SnapshotSource, SnapshotProjection

Origin type: application-capture.

Previous use. An investigation snapshot froze source revisions, projections and collection/coverage evidence over a recorded capture interval, because completion was not a native immutable archive.

Consolidation decision. One Snapshot entity supplies that closure with exact EntityRefs; ReadAttempt records are referenced rather than copied.

aws/devops-agent/analysis/annexes/Investigation_Data_Model.md

TopologySnapshot, TopologyNode, TopologyEdge

Origin type: application-capture.

Previous use. Topology captures retained scoped nodes/edges, unresolved endpoints, collection intervals and query scope; no native atomic topology ID was assumed.

Consolidation decision. TOPOLOGY Snapshot content keeps graph values and endpoints within one captured scope.

aws/resilience-hub/analysis/report.md

PolicyContextCapture, EffectiveTargetObservation

Origin type: application-capture.

Previous use. Policy context retained observed target values, associations and policy evidence without claiming the provider had evaluated that exact revision.

Consolidation decision. POLICY_CONTEXT Snapshot keeps this qualified historical context distinct from an AWS revision guarantee.

aws/resilience-hub/analysis/report.md

AdmissionSnapshot

Origin type: owned-value.

Previous use. AdmissionSnapshot was a Run-owned value freezing validated inputs, resolved references, enabled steps and criterion denominator.

Consolidation decision. The consolidation promotes deliberate captures to shared Snapshot entities and has Run pin the exact capture version.

Foundation · entity

WorkItem

#
Versioned entityAPPLICATION16 fields

The sole owner of local operator assignment, priority, due dates, work state and verification over typed domain targets. It coordinates human or service follow-up without modifying native event, finding or experiment outcomes.

Logical identity
workspaceId + workItemId
Retained record
workspaceId + workItemId + version
Owner / authority
Application commands own WorkItem state. owner may identify a human, group or service; action audit actors identify the actual human or service. Targets are deliberately live EntityIdentity links, while resolution and verification evidence pin exact retained versions.
Lifecycle
CreateWorkItem establishes the task. UpdateWorkItem publishes changes under its expectedVersion, and RecordWorkItemVerification records qualified verification evidence. A completed local task can still await fresh AWS or inventory confirmation; its history is retained under one workItemId.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · WorkItem

Use cases

Track a maintenance campaign

Context. Several affected resources require coordinated upgrades for related Health contexts.

Use. Create a WorkItem with explicit targets, an owner and due-date rationale, then attach exact inventory/Health evidence during verification.

Result. Coordinated work is visible without inventing a provider incident-group identity or clearing PENDING impact.

Implement repeated suggestions once

Context. Several captured recommendations propose the same practical infrastructure change.

Use. Use one WorkItem to target those recommendation identities and track assignment and completion; keep each Recommendation suggestion and enrichment independently retained.

Result. Operators avoid duplicate task state without falsely merging provider-generated suggestions.

Invariants and interpretation

  • Closing a WorkItem does not establish Health resolution, finding remediation or workload recovery.
  • Live targets do not freeze target content; verification evidence must pin exact versions.
  • WorkItem owns operator workflow so Recommendation cannot maintain a competing assignment/state machine.

WorkItem, WorkItemTarget, OperatorAction

Origin type: application-workflow.

Previous use. WorkItem grouped context, impact or exposure targets with version-checked operator actions, ownership, priority and due-date evidence.

Consolidation decision. The same concept becomes the shared local workflow owner and uses common versions and typed targets.

aws/health/analysis/report.md

RecommendationEnrichment, RemediationTask

Origin type: application-enrichment.

Previous use. The Resilience analysis proposed enrichment or a separate remediation task for ownership, cost estimates and completion, because nested suggestions had no native lifecycle.

Consolidation decision. Assignment and work state move exclusively to WorkItem. Estimates and explanatory notes remain owned Recommendation enrichment under Recommendation.version.

Foundation · entity

Command

#
Versioned entityAPPLICATION17 fields

A durable record of admitted intent, dispatch and reconciliation. Command separates what an authorized actor requested from provider acceptance, remote effects and observed completion, using one common version and idempotency contract.

Logical identity
workspaceId + commandId
Retained record
workspaceId + commandId + version
Owner / authority
The command service admits validated intent; trusted dispatchers and reconcilers publish subsequent lifecycle versions. Operation-specific typed inputs determine what may change. Command attempts and effects are owned values.
Lifecycle
Admission retains operation, actor, clientToken, canonical requestDigest and relevant preconditions before dispatch. An exact replay is reauthorized and resolves to the original receipt before mutable head checks. Later versions retain attempts, effects, results or uncertainty; a lost response is reconciled without manufacturing success.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Command

Use cases

Recover a lost start response

Context. An assessment start request is accepted but the client loses the response.

Use. Replay the same scoped token and complete intent to obtain its existing Command receipt, then inspect reconciliation rather than creating a second start.

Result. The user can discover admitted work and uncertain effects without assuming exactly-once AWS execution.

Separate approval from continuation

Context. An operator approves a paused investigation action.

Use. Retain one decision Command and a distinct resume Command, each with its exact request context and observed result.

Result. Approval, resumed execution and verified operational recovery remain separately auditable facts.

Fields

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandIdRequiredId

Stable logical identity of this Command; the entity version selects a retained representation.

workspaceIdRequiredId

Trusted application scope. Request bodies cannot select a tenant.

versionRequiredVersion

createdAtRequiredTimestamp

updatedAtRequiredTimestamp

operationRequiredstringMinimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096
subjectRefsRequiredArray of EntityRefMaximum items: 100
actorRequiredActorRefUses the declared type and containing contract.
clientTokenRequiredstring

Opaque mutation-intent token. Exact replay requires the same operation, payload and preconditions.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096
requestDigestRequiredDigestUses the declared type and containing contract.
expectedVersionRequiredAny of: Version | null

Optimistic precondition on the named entity head; never a nested value's own clock.

acceptedAtRequiredTimestampUses the declared type and containing contract.
stateRequired"ACCEPTED" · "DISPATCHING" · "RECONCILING" · "SUCCEEDED" · "FAILED" · "CANCELED" · "OUTCOME_UNKNOWN"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
attemptsRequiredArray of CommandAttemptMaximum items: 1000
effectsRequiredArray of ExternalOperationRefMaximum items: 100
resultRefsRequiredArray of EntityRefMaximum items: 100
replayExpiresAtRequiredTimestampUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Invariants and interpretation

  • Local expectedVersion protects admission, not an atomic cross-service AWS transaction.
  • Idempotency compares the complete canonical intent, including preconditions, within trusted workspace/principal/operation scope.
  • An accepted command, an accepted stop and a permission grant are not proof of remote completion.
  • An unresolved effect cannot justify a blind creating retry.

Where it was defined and how it was used

local command, clientToken, reconciliation state

Origin type: application-command.

Previous use. The Resilience analysis required a local command ID, input, actor, submission time, request result and reconciliation state; asynchronous acceptance could not establish completion.

Consolidation decision. There was no complete one-to-one shared Command schema. Consolidation makes this cross-module intent/receipt record explicit and versioned.

aws/resilience-hub/analysis/report.md

ApprovalRequest, DecisionAttempt, ResumeAttempt

Origin type: application-control-audit.

Previous use. The investigation UI contract retained distinct observed approval request, decision attempt and resume attempt records, with actual responses and ambiguous outcomes.

Consolidation decision. DecisionAttempt and ResumeAttempt become instances of the shared Command entity; ApprovalRequest retains the observed provider request context.

aws/devops-agent/analysis/annexes/Investigation_UI_Contract.md

dispatch intent, CancellationIntent, ExternalOperationRef

Origin type: owned-control-values.

Previous use. Workflow attempts persisted a dispatch key before provider calls, reconciled ambiguous effects, and retained cancellation intent independently from remote stopping.

Consolidation decision. Command unifies public mutation admission and receipt behavior; workflow StepAttempt still owns execution-attempt facts and its effects.

Systems, journeys, services and dependency context.

Workload · entity

System

#
Versioned entityAPPLICATION8 fields

A local business-system catalog entry that groups workload context for the operator. It retains verified provider bindings so the console can relate its catalog to earlier Resilience system definitions without making every local change an AWS configuration command.

Logical identity
workspaceId + systemId
Retained record
workspaceId + systemId + version
Owner / authority
Application commands own System name, description and provider bindings. Service.memberships is the sole writable source of system/service membership; reverse service lists and counts are derived.
Lifecycle
CreateSystem creates the stable systemId and first version. UpdateSystem compares the owning System version and publishes a successor. Historical projections and captures pin the System representation they used; a business rename does not alter those earlier views.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · System

Use cases

Describe the commerce boundary

Context. An operator defines the commerce system containing purchase and fulfillment journeys.

Use. Create a System with local business metadata and retain any verified Resilience system association in providerBindings.

Result. All modules can present the same business context without assuming local catalog creation provisioned a native system.

Count a shared service once

Context. One service participates in two journeys within the same system.

Use. Derive the system service set from distinct Service.memberships rather than adding journey counts.

Result. System-level counts reflect unique services and preserve the evidence behind their status.

Fields

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
systemIdRequiredId

Stable logical identity of this System; the entity version selects a retained representation.

workspaceIdRequiredId

Trusted application scope. Request bodies cannot select a tenant.

versionRequiredVersion

Positive server-assigned version of this immutable entity representation.

createdAtRequiredTimestamp

Local creation time of the logical entity; constant across its entity versions.

updatedAtRequiredTimestamp

Local publication time of this entity representation; nondecreasing across versions.

nameRequiredstringMinimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096
descriptionRequiredstringMaximum length: 16384
providerBindingsRequiredArray of ProviderBindingMaximum items: 100

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Invariants and interpretation

  • Names are display fields, not identity joins.
  • System has no invented directly assigned native policy field.
  • Journey membership does not supply execution order, redundancy or critical-path weighting.

Where it was defined and how it was used

SystemEntity, System, SystemService

Origin type: native-resource-and-local-membership.

Previous use. The earlier Resilience model normalized native System fields and Service.associatedSystems into a system catalog and local join records. A system could contain journeys and directly associated services.

Consolidation decision. The consolidated System is the application business catalog. Native aliases are explicit provider bindings; Service owns local membership and AWS writes have separate command boundaries.

Workload · entity

UserJourney

#
Versioned entityAPPLICATION9 fields

A named local user journey within exactly one System. It provides business context for participating services, without claiming that membership alone defines an executable workflow or measured end-to-end availability.

Logical identity
workspaceId + userJourneyId
Retained record
workspaceId + userJourneyId + version
Owner / authority
Application commands own the journey metadata and verified provider bindings. Its parent systemId is ownership context. Service.memberships owns the service association; UserJourney does not keep a competing writable service list.
Lifecycle
CreateUserJourney creates a system-scoped identity and UpdateUserJourney publishes later metadata versions under expectedVersion. An exact historical view pins the appropriate journey and membership evidence instead of joining to the latest catalog.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · UserJourney

Use cases

Define the purchase journey

Context. A team wants to examine checkout and payment as the services supporting a customer purchase.

Use. Create UserJourney under the commerce System and associate the services through their memberships.

Result. Operators gain a business navigation view while retaining each service as an independently observed workload.

Explain qualified journey posture

Context. One shared service misses its effective resilience target.

Use. Use the journey membership and captured policy context in a Projection rather than assigning a native success/failure field to the journey.

Result. The view shows which member and requirement need attention without asserting unmeasured journey compliance.

Maximum length: 4096

Invariants and interpretation

  • A UserJourney belongs to one System, and journey membership must agree with that system.
  • Do not derive ordering or redundancy from membership.
  • Local journey edits do not mutate native policy assignments.

Where it was defined and how it was used

UserJourneyEntity, UserJourney, JourneyService

Origin type: native-resource-and-local-membership.

Previous use. The prior model scoped userJourneyId by System, preserved a native policy reference and normalized service participation from Service.associatedSystems. The journey body had no embedded service list.

Consolidation decision. UserJourney becomes a local catalog entity with explicit provider bindings; the consolidated model retains one membership writer on Service.

journey policy assignment, effectivePolicyValues

Origin type: provider-configuration-context.

Previous use. The analysis distinguished journey policy applicability from service-level effective targets and warned that a strict combined target did not prove each looser journey requirement failed.

Consolidation decision. Those provider facts remain retained Source and policy-context Snapshot evidence rather than local writable journey status.

Workload · entity

Service

#
Versioned entityAPPLICATION10 fields

The business workload boundary reused by Health, Resilience, investigations and workflow context. Service is distinct from an AWS service family such as EC2 and from a DevOps RegisteredService integration.

Logical identity
workspaceId + serviceId
Retained record
workspaceId + serviceId + version
Owner / authority
Application commands own Service catalog metadata, resource links, provider bindings and memberships. Memberships is the only writable system/journey association in the consolidated catalog; native Resilience configuration remains separately observed and separately commanded.
Lifecycle
CreateService and UpdateService publish local catalog versions under expectedVersion. Provider-observed changes retain Source/Observation evidence and may invalidate derived context without rewriting prior Service snapshots. UpdateResilienceServiceConfiguration is a distinct native mutation boundary.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Service

Use cases

Connect a workload to observed resources

Context. The checkout workload uses worker instances and a database.

Use. Retain the local Service, qualified resourceIds and explicit providerBindings, then associate domain observations through their scoped identities.

Result. The operator sees a common workload page without treating incomplete resource discovery as a complete architecture.

Move a service into a journey

Context. A service becomes part of the purchase journey in the commerce system.

Use. Replace the allowed membership value through UpdateService using its current version; derive reverse system/journey views.

Result. There is one membership authority, and historical captures preserve the earlier associations.

Fields

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
serviceIdRequiredId

Stable logical identity of this Service; the entity version selects a retained representation.

workspaceIdRequiredId

Trusted application scope. Request bodies cannot select a tenant.

versionRequiredVersion

Positive server-assigned version of this immutable entity representation.

createdAtRequiredTimestamp

Local creation time of the logical entity; constant across its entity versions.

updatedAtRequiredTimestamp

Local publication time of this entity representation; nondecreasing across versions.

Maximum length: 4096
descriptionRequiredstringMaximum length: 16384
membershipsRequiredArray of ServiceMembershipMaximum items: 100
resourceIdsRequiredArray of IdMaximum items: 10000
providerBindingsRequiredArray of ProviderBindingMaximum items: 100

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Invariants and interpretation

  • One writer owns memberships; reverse lists are derived.
  • A local catalog edit cannot assert that AWS configuration changed.
  • Provider permission configuration is not application authorization.
  • Distinct service identities, not summed memberships, are the rollup population.

Where it was defined and how it was used

ServiceEntity, Service.associatedSystems, SystemService, JourneyService

Origin type: native-resource-and-local-membership.

Previous use. The earlier model retained native Service metadata and normalized associatedSystems into constrained system/journey joins; services could be shared across several systems.

Consolidation decision. Service is now the common local workload catalog with one memberships owner. Native ARNs and configuration remain explicit bindings and source evidence.

aws/resilience-hub/analysis/report.md

ServiceResource, InputSourceEntity, PermissionModel

Origin type: provider-configuration-context.

Previous use. Service resource descriptors, input sources and permission configuration supported discovery and native execution; partial read shapes were not valid create requests.

Consolidation decision. The local Service exposes catalog resource links while those native configuration objects remain registered retained DTOs, avoiding a writable universal configuration blob.

Workload · entity

Dependency

#
Versioned entityMIXED12 fields

A service-scoped observed dependency with optional evidenced Resource or Service resolution and a small local governance value. It keeps native classification and local allow/deny reasoning distinct without creating a second entity or version clock.

Logical identity
workspaceId + serviceId + dependencyId
Retained record
workspaceId + dependencyId + version
Owner / authority
Mixed field authority shares one Dependency.version: the collector owns native identity, observation and rawClassification; the application owns governance through UpdateDependencyGovernance. UpdateDependencyClassification is the separate provider command boundary.
Lifecycle
New provider evidence and permitted governance edits both append versions of the same dependencyId. Governance has no independent version. A provider refresh can make a local expectedVersion stale, preserving the conservative conflict instead of overwriting new evidence.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Field authorities
governance: APPLICATION; observed fields: COLLECTOR
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Dependency

Field authority is partitioned, but the containing entity has one version. Owned governance or enrichment values have no independent version counter.

Use cases

Review a discovered DNS dependency

Context. Checkout discovers a database DNS name with HARD native criticality.

Use. Inspect the observed Dependency and its evidence; attach governance rationale using UpdateDependencyGovernance while preserving rawClassification.

Result. The local decision is auditable without implying network permissions or native criticality changed.

Resolve a dependency carefully

Context. A DNS name appears to identify a cataloged service.

Use. Set or retain a qualified targetServiceId or targetResourceId only when matching evidence supports the relationship.

Result. An operator can navigate the dependency without treating a display-name coincidence as an AWS foreign key.

Fields

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
dependencyIdRequiredId

Stable logical identity of this Dependency; the entity version selects a retained representation.

workspaceIdRequiredId

Trusted application scope. Request bodies cannot select a tenant.

versionRequiredVersion

Positive server-assigned version of this immutable entity representation.

createdAtRequiredTimestamp

Local creation time of the logical entity; constant across its entity versions.

updatedAtRequiredTimestamp

Local publication time of this entity representation; nondecreasing across versions.

serviceIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
identityRequiredSourceIdentityUses the declared type and containing contract.
targetResourceIdRequiredAny of: Id | nullUses the declared type and containing contract.
targetServiceIdRequiredAny of: Id | nullUses the declared type and containing contract.
rawClassificationRequiredAny of: string | nullMinimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096
selectedObservationRequiredAny of: EntityRef (kind = "Observation") | null

Exact observation selected for this representation; historical reads do not retarget it.

governanceRequiredLocalDecisionUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Invariants and interpretation

  • Governance shares Dependency.version; it has no separate counter.
  • Native classification describes dependency criticality, not current availability.
  • DNS query counts do not establish request success or latency.
  • An allowed-status decision does not change network permissions.

Where it was defined and how it was used

DependencyEntity, DependencyGovernance, DNS queryRange

Origin type: native-resource-and-local-overlay.

Previous use. DependencyEntity retained service-scoped DNS evidence, usage windows and criticality. DependencyGovernance was a separately versioned local allowed-status overlay with rationale; DNS counts were not health metrics.

Consolidation decision. The concept stays service-scoped, but governance is now an owned value under the single Dependency version. Native classification and local governance retain separate writers and operation contracts.

Health · entity

HealthEvent

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR11 fields

The shared identity of one AWS Health event, preserving the complete event ARN and indexed event classification. Context-specific status, affected constructs and delivery occurrences remain separate so one event is not multiplied by accounts or notifications.

Logical identity
workspaceId + healthEventId
Retained record
workspaceId + healthEventId + version
Owner / authority
A trusted Health collector normalizes the provider identity and selected exact Source. Operators cannot create, acknowledge or close the native event through this entity; local follow-up belongs to WorkItem.
Lifecycle
The same healthEventId publishes versions as accepted provider evidence changes. EventContext partitions account/public/organization evidence, and independently observed entity impacts keep their own update clocks. Missing newer source access does not erase retained history.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · HealthEvent

Use cases

Unify cross-account views of one event

Context. Organization and account reads reference the same full Health event ARN.

Use. Resolve them to one HealthEvent and keep their evidence in distinct EventContexts.

Result. Event totals remain stable while each account view preserves its own status and impact evidence.

Retain an updated event description

Context. Hydration supplies a newer event representation after an EventBridge notification.

Use. Retain its Source and update the selected versioned event representation without discarding the original notification.

Result. Operators can inspect what changed and which source supported the displayed event.
