Health · entity

EventContext

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR12 fields

An application evidence partition for one Health event: PUBLIC, ACCOUNT or ORG_SUMMARY. It carries the context key, selected observation and contextual provider status so information from one account or access scope cannot overwrite another.

Logical identity
workspaceId + healthEventId + kind + contextKey
Retained record
workspaceId + eventContextId + version
Owner / authority
The trusted normalizer derives context from actual provider request/response scope. PUBLIC has no affected-account or organization owner; ACCOUNT has one account; ORG_SUMMARY has organization scope and cannot own EntityImpact children.
Lifecycle
A context has stable uniqueness within Workspace by event identity, kind and non-null contextKey. Later selected observations publish context versions. Notification recipients are retained as communication provenance and do not create additional affected-account contexts.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · EventContext

Use cases

Keep public recipient metadata separate

Context. A public Health notification is delivered to several accounts.

Use. Resolve all copies to the shared PUBLIC EventContext and keep recipient details with Communication/Observation.

Result. Delivery count does not become affected-account count.

Hydrate one organization account

Context. An organization summary identifies an affected account requiring detail hydration.

Use. Create or resolve its ACCOUNT context and record the account-scoped detail/impact observations there.

Result. Partial organization summary evidence remains separate from actual account detail.

Where it was defined and how it was used

EventContext, PUBLIC, ACCOUNT, ORG_SUMMARY

Origin type: application-aggregate.

Previous use. The earlier Health design introduced non-null context keys because account detail is addressed by event/account while public events have no affected-account owner. ORG_SUMMARY could not contain entity impacts.

Consolidation decision. The same local abstraction is retained as a universally versioned entity; its values remain application context kinds rather than invented AWS eventScopeCode values.

EntityImpact

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR11 fields

The participation of an affected construct in one Health EventContext. It retains the Health entity identity/value, independently observed event-relative state and optional inventory matches; it is not a globally healthy or unhealthy Resource.

Logical identity
workspaceId + eventContextId + scoped provider entity key
Retained record
workspaceId + entityImpactId + version
Owner / authority
The Health collector owns the native impact representation and selected observation. Resource matching uses explicit method/evidence and may resolve zero, one or several inventory resources.
Lifecycle
The stable impact identity is context-scoped. Later provider observations publish versions even when the parent event timestamp does not change. An entityValue-only receipt can remain provisionally identified until supported reconciliation establishes its identity.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · EntityImpact

Use cases

Track maintenance action on a database

Context. The event-relative database state changes from PENDING to RESOLVED.

Use. Retain the independent impact observations and publish the next EntityImpact version.

Result. The UI shows the provider transition while preserving local WorkItem verification as a separate fact.

Keep a broad affected construct visible

Context. Health reports a resource group or an unresolved value rather than one identifiable inventory object.

Use. Retain EntityImpact without forcing a one-to-one Resource link and expose its unresolved or multiple resourceMatches.

Result. Valid impact evidence survives even when inventory matching is incomplete.

Maximum length: 4096

Invariants and interpretation

  • Entity state is relative to this event context, not a global health verdict.
  • entityValue is not globally unique.
  • A selected impact observation retains its own provider clock.
  • Local completion cannot rewrite provider PENDING or RESOLVED state.

Communication

#
Versioned entityDERIVATION11 fields

A validated logical grouping of Health notification pages. It brings together page candidates and delivery observations without confusing a logical message/page with a native Health event or affected entity.

Logical identity
workspaceId + communicationId
Retained record
workspaceId + communicationId + version
Owner / authority
A trusted derivation process owns groupingRuleDigest, validatedBaseId, assembly state and owned pages. Raw communication identifiers and contradictory candidates remain retained evidence; grouping is an explicit application interpretation.
Lifecycle
As pages or conflicting candidates arrive, new Communication versions preserve the evolving assembly. Repeated genuine deliveries remain separate Observations. Completion is asserted only when the expected pages and validated grouping evidence support it.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Communication

Use cases

Assemble a paginated notification

Context. Three pages arrive out of order and page two is delivered twice.

Use. Group validated logical page identities in Communication and retain both page-two receipt observations.

Result. The message can become complete without counting duplicates as additional impact.

Expose conflicting page content

Context. Two deliveries claim the same page identity but their payloads disagree.

Use. Retain both candidates and publish a qualified assembly state instead of silently choosing the last arrival.

Result. Operators can inspect the conflict and avoid treating an incomplete or disputed resource list as a total.

assemblyStateRequired"COMPLETE" · "PARTIAL" · "CONFLICTED" · "UNKNOWN"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
pagesRequiredArray of CommunicationPageMaximum items: 1000

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Invariants and interpretation

  • Raw provider communicationId and local communicationId are different identities.
  • Grouping must retain its validated rule and notification-account context.
  • Delivery region and recipient do not redefine logical event identity.
  • Incomplete pages cannot support a complete affected-resource count.

LifecycleEntry

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR12 fields

One retained lifecycle catalog entry describing a component version and its milestones. It carries local identity and exact catalog capture/source provenance because the examined provider catalog does not establish a stable entry ID.

Logical identity
workspaceId + lifecycleEntryId
Retained record
workspaceId + lifecycleEntryId + version
Owner / authority
The collector owns the returned catalog values. Milestones are owned values under LifecycleEntry.version; versionLabel and recommendedVersion are provider content, not entity-version counters.
Lifecycle
Observed catalog changes are retained as versions under an evidenced local identity, with catalogSnapshot and Source references. Distinct entries are not merged solely because serviceCode and versionLabel match. Changes in title, dates or milestone content remain historically inspectable.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · LifecycleEntry

Use cases

Review an upcoming support milestone

Context. A catalog entry lists an end-of-support date for an engine version.

Use. Inspect the LifecycleEntry, its retained milestones and source catalog Snapshot; use a Projection to assess actual deployed components.

Result. Operators see the catalog fact separately from any claim that a resource is affected.

Preserve a revised milestone date

Context. A later catalog capture changes a previously observed milestone date.

Use. Retain both exact source/capture contexts and publish the accepted new LifecycleEntry representation.

Result. A prior lifecycle assessment remains traceable to the date it actually used.

  • Do not treat service plus versionLabel as a provider-guaranteed unique key.

  • An unresolved recommendedVersion remains the provider-supplied value.

ComponentDeployment

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR9 fields

An observed installed component and version on a Resource. It supplies the inventory side of lifecycle assessment, separately from catalog entries and from any later interpretation of support or applicability.

Logical identity
workspaceId + componentDeploymentId
Retained record
workspaceId + componentDeploymentId + version
Owner / authority
The inventory collector owns componentKind, versionLabel and the exact supporting Observation. The resource link identifies where this deployment was observed; application publication time does not replace the inventory observation time.
Lifecycle
Fresh installed-version evidence publishes ComponentDeployment versions under a stable identity. Lifecycle Projections pin the exact deployment version and its observation, so later upgrades cannot rewrite an earlier exposure result.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · ComponentDeployment

Use cases

Assess the database engine actually installed

Context. A database resource has a documented engine-version observation.

Use. Retain ComponentDeployment and evaluate it against a captured LifecycleEntry using the registered matching rule.

Result. The exposure result has an explicit inventory basis rather than a guessed match from a service name.

Verify an upgrade after local completion

Context. An operator completes an upgrade WorkItem.

Use. Collect a new deployment observation and compare the new ComponentDeployment version with the evidence used by the old exposure.

Result. Verification depends on fresh installed-version evidence; completing the task alone does not clear exposure.

Resilience · entity

ResiliencePolicy

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR10 fields

The normalized provider-observed Resilience policy with typed optional components and exact source evidence. It preserves configured objectives without inventing unsupported native performance targets or claiming which revision an assessment evaluated.

Logical identity
workspaceId + resiliencePolicyId
Retained record
workspaceId + resiliencePolicyId + version
Owner / authority
The collector publishes observed policy representations. UpdateResiliencePolicyConfiguration admits a separate narrow provider command and reconciliation supplies observed state. Components are owned values under the one policy version.
Lifecycle
New accepted provider observations append ResiliencePolicy versions, retaining providerUpdatedAt when supplied. Policy changes can invalidate current context, but earlier policy-context Snapshots remain unchanged. Native creation/update times are distinct from local version publication.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · ResiliencePolicy

Use cases

Compare configured recovery objectives

Context. A policy defines multi-AZ recovery targets but leaves multi-Region recovery unconfigured.

Use. Read the typed components and retain absence rather than filling missing metrics with zero.

Result. The assessment view can distinguish configured objectives from unsupported or unconfigured dimensions.

Review a policy change safely

Context. An authorized operator changes a supported native target.

Use. Submit UpdateResiliencePolicyConfiguration with its source precondition and inspect the Command and later selected Observation.

Result. The console separates admitted intent from observed configuration and preserves earlier captured context.

Resilience · entity

ResilienceAssessment

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR11 fields

One native service-scoped Resilience assessment execution. It records observed execution state and optional selected posture/context evidence while keeping successful execution, achieved objectives and live workload health independent.

Logical identity
workspaceId + serviceId + resilienceAssessmentId
Retained record
workspaceId + resilienceAssessmentId + version
Owner / authority
A trusted collector owns provider assessment representations. StartResilienceAssessment admits an asynchronous provider command; it does not immediately create a successful assessed outcome. Any policy-context or finding association must be supported and qualified.
Lifecycle
The same native scoped assessment identity acquires later observed versions as it progresses. A failed new assessment does not erase the previous successful posture retained for the Service. Exact policyContextSnapshot and selectedPostureProjection references explain the selected interpretation when available.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · ResilienceAssessment

Use cases

Track a newly requested assessment

Context. An operator starts another assessment after a service change.

Use. Follow its Command and observed ResilienceAssessment state separately from the service’s retained last-known posture.

Result. Queued or running work is visible without prematurely marking the service assessed.

Explain failure without losing history

Context. The newest assessment fails while yesterday’s completed assessment has retained findings/context.

Use. Retain the failed execution and continue qualifying the older posture by age, coverage and context.

Result. Operators see both the execution failure and the limited evidence that remains available.

Resilience · entity

Finding

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR14 fields

A native service-scoped resilience finding with independently selected summary and detail evidence. Finding preserves current disposition and severity while recording whether recommendation content was actually observed.

Logical identity
workspaceId + serviceId + findingId
Retained record
workspaceId + findingId + version
Owner / authority
The collector owns provider fields and selected observations. UpdateFindingDisposition is a provider command with narrow inputs; local task assignment, completion and verification belong to WorkItem.
Lifecycle
A stable service/finding identity publishes later representations as native evidence changes. currentCaptureCollection qualifies the current observation attempt. A newer incomplete summary or failed detail fetch cannot erase earlier detail or turn unknown recommendations into an empty array.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Finding

Use cases

Show incomplete detail honestly

Context. The finding list is complete but a detail request fails.

Use. Retain selectedSummaryObservation, the prior selectedDetailObservation if available and the current Collection’s qualified coverage.

Result. The operator sees observed counts and detail uncertainty instead of a fabricated zero-suggestion result.

Track a claimed remediation

Context. An operator sets the native finding disposition to RESOLVED after implementing a change.

Use. Retain the disposition Command and later provider observation, and use separate WorkItem verification evidence for confirmed remediation.

Result. A status edit is not presented as an independently verified repair.

Invariants and interpretation

  • A finding belongs to a Service, not an invented immutable assessment result set.
  • Detail unavailable, omitted suggestion fields and known empty suggestions are different states.
  • RESOLVED or IRRELEVANT disposition does not itself prove remediation.
  • Do not invent resource ARNs when the provider supplies service-function references.

Consolidation decision. Collection, Source and Observation consolidate those mechanisms. Finding selects them without acquiring separate revision-only entities.

Resilience · entity

Recommendation

#
Versioned entityMIXED13 fields

One captured Resilience finding suggestion, preserving its source grouping and text plus narrowly owned local enrichment. It is not the separate AWS DevOps prevention Recommendation resource, which remains a retained provider DTO.

Logical identity
workspaceId + serviceId + findingId + exact source reference + groupKey + ordinal (unless a stable native key is available)
Retained record
workspaceId + recommendationId + version
Owner / authority
Mixed field authority shares one Recommendation.version: the collector owns the captured suggestion and exact source/detail observation; the application owns estimates and explanatory enrichment. WorkItem exclusively owns assignment and work state.
Lifecycle
Where the source provides no stable suggestion key, identity is scoped by Finding, exact Source version, groupKey and ordinal. Repeated observations of that same Source reuse the recommendation identity. A changed Source does not establish continuity merely because ordinal or text matches. Enrichment edits append ordinary Recommendation versions.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Field authorities
enrichment: APPLICATION; observed fields: COLLECTOR
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Recommendation

Field authority is partitioned, but the containing entity has one version. Owned governance or enrichment values have no independent version counter.

Use cases

Estimate a suggested architecture change

Context. A detailed finding suggests adding another node.

Use. Retain the captured suggestion and add an estimate with provenance, currency/units, basis and confidence through UpdateRecommendationEnrichment.

Result. The operator can assess the proposal without presenting application estimates as native AWS recommendation fields.

Avoid duplicates from repeated polling

Context. The same detailed finding payload is read again.

Use. Reuse the Recommendation tied to the exact Source version and retain the later Observation separately.

Result. Polling does not create duplicate suggestions, while genuinely changed captures remain distinct and traceable.

Invariants and interpretation

  • Recommendation has no independent enrichment version counter.
  • Ordinal and content equality do not prove native continuity across changed source versions.
  • Group identity is the source array, not Finding.failureCategory.
  • A local estimate or completed WorkItem is not native recommendation status.

Where it was defined and how it was used

RecommendationEntity, RecommendationEnrichment, RemediationTask

Origin type: native-owned-value-and-local-enrichment.

Previous use. Native detail contained grouped infrastructure/code, observability and testing suggestedChanges arrays without a standalone recommendation ID or lifecycle. The study proposed observation-scoped normalization and separate enrichment/task support.

Consolidation decision. The captured suggestion becomes a versioned application Recommendation. Estimates/notes inherit its version; task ownership and state move to WorkItem.

The native AWS DevOps Agent workspace resource observed inside the application Workspace. It supplies provider scope for tasks, executions, journals and assets and retains observed integration associations.

workspaceId + agentSpaceId

Owner / authority
The collector owns AgentSpace identity, name, selected observation and association values. A RegisteredService association is provider integration context, distinct from the local business Service and from the application Connection used to read it.

Use cases

Browse investigations in one native space

Context. An operator selects a DevOps AgentSpace within the consolidated console.

Use. Use its scoped native identity to list retained Investigation, Execution and Asset entities under the same application Workspace.

Result. The user has a coherent native scope without confusing it with the product authorization boundary.

Explain available integrations at capture time

Context. A historical investigation refers to repository access that has since changed.

Use. Inspect the captured AgentSpace representation and associated source evidence rather than the latest associations.

Result. The view explains observed historical configuration without claiming that configured access was successfully consumed.

AgentSpace, RegisteredService, Association

Origin type: native-resource-and-configuration.

Investigation · entity

Investigation

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR15 fields

An application aggregate over a native DevOps Task whose taskType is INVESTIGATION. It brings together the task identity and selected observation, explicitly observed execution memberships, external references and phase-specific result views.

Logical identity
workspaceId + agentSpaceId + native taskId
Retained record
workspaceId + investigationId + version
Owner / authority
The collector owns the normalized task representation and memberships. StartInvestigation is the consolidated facade command over the supported native task boundary; the model does not invent an AWS Investigation resource or native GetInvestigation operation.
Lifecycle
Provider Task changes publish Investigation versions, with nativeTaskVersion retained separately from the application version. Completion does not seal all future provider activity: an investigation can continue. Deliberate Snapshot captures preserve earlier reviewed results while current observations advance.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Investigation

Use cases

Open a completed case whose summary is unavailable

Context. The Task is completed but the completion event points to a journal record that has not been retrieved.

Use. Read the Investigation alongside its INVESTIGATION_RESULT Projection, exact completion evidence and collection status.

Result. Task completion remains visible while the result is correctly labeled pending or unavailable.

Preserve a case before further work

Context. An operator reviews an investigation and later continues the native task.

Use. Capture the earlier Investigation and its exact evidence/membership closure in Snapshot, then retain subsequent task versions.

Result. The earlier review remains reproducible rather than being overwritten by the continued case.

Invariants and interpretation

  • GetInvestigation is an application API, not a claimed native AWS operation.
  • The optional Task execution pointer is not guaranteed to identify the latest, root or only execution.

  • Completion and authoritative summary availability are independent.

Where it was defined and how it was used

Investigation, Task, TaskExecutionMembership

Origin type: application-aggregate-over-native-task.

Previous use. The earlier model explicitly composed an Investigation from Task, observed memberships, executions, journals, notifications, results and historical snapshots. It stated that this was not an AWS response payload.

Consolidation decision. The composition remains, but Investigation itself now uses the universal identity/version contract; Task nativeVersion and exact evidence remain separate facts.

Task.status, Execution.executionStatus, result availability

Origin type: independent-provider-and-application-state.

Previous use. Task status, execution status, chat completion, investigation/mitigation milestones and result readiness were kept independent. A completed investigation could continue.

Consolidation decision. The consolidated aggregate preserves rawTaskStatus without folding these dimensions into a single done flag; result interpretation belongs to Projection.

Execution

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR11 fields

A native DevOps execution scoped by AgentSpace, retaining its own status, optional parent execution identity, agent subtask and selected observation. Its relation to investigations is an observed membership, not a fictional single mandatory parent.

Logical identity
workspaceId + agentSpaceId + native executionId
Retained record
workspaceId + executionId + version
Owner / authority
The collector owns the native execution representation. Investigation retains memberships established through actual task-scoped reads; parentExecutionIdentity is the separately observed native execution hierarchy.
Lifecycle
Successive native observations publish Execution versions. ResumeExecution is a command boundary whose acceptance/stream activity is retained independently from later observed execution state. Provider status changes do not rewrite previously captured execution versions.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Execution

Use cases

Display an observed execution tree

Context. Several executions are returned for an investigation, including a child whose parent detail has not yet been loaded.

Use. Retain each Execution with its native parent identity and preserve unresolved hierarchy context.

Result. The tree can explain partial coverage without deleting the child or fabricating a parent state.

Associate an execution with multiple tasks

Context. Task-scoped reads establish memberships involving the same native execution identity.

Use. Keep one AgentSpace-scoped Execution and retain the separate Investigation membership evidence.

Result. The model avoids duplicating runtime history or enforcing an unsupported single-task foreign key.

Invariants and interpretation

  • Execution scope includes AgentSpace.
  • Observed task membership and execution parentage are different relations.
  • STOPPED alone does not prove success, mitigation or recovery.

JournalRecord

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR11 fields

A stable native journal envelope identified within AgentSpace and Execution. JournalRecord preserves recordType and exact selected Source/Observation references while leaving content as arbitrary retained JSON.

Logical identity
workspaceId + agentSpaceId + executionId + native recordId
Retained record
workspaceId + journalRecordId + version
Owner / authority
The collector owns the envelope representation. Known content profiles may be interpreted by registered derivations, but unsupported record types and unexpected content forms remain available as source evidence instead of being discarded or coerced.
Lifecycle
Later accepted representations publish JournalRecord versions under the same scoped record identity. Each selected source and occurrence is pinned. Summary selection follows exact phase-specific completion references when supplied; selection and availability are derived concerns, not writable journal status.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · JournalRecord

Use cases

Retrieve the exact investigation summary

Context. A completion event identifies a specific summary_record_id.

Use. Find that JournalRecord in the correct space/execution and use its exact source version for the INVESTIGATION_RESULT Projection.

Result. Another summary with a later timestamp cannot silently replace the referenced result.

Inspect an unfamiliar record type

Context. A provider returns a new recordType or content that is not a Markdown string.

JournalRecord, JournalRecordRevision

Origin type: native-envelope-and-retained-evidence.

Previous use. The prior model relied on required space/execution/record/type/time/content fields and emphasized that content was arbitrary JSON with no universal root-cause, evidence or sequence schema.

Consolidation decision. JournalRecord is uniformly versioned; retained payload history uses Source versions rather than separate JournalRecordRevision entities.

Origin type: documented-content-profile.

Previous use. The analysis selected exact completion-referenced records by phase and kept missing pointers, unresolved pointers and ambiguous candidates distinct. The _md type did not change the content wire type.

ApprovalRequest

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR14 fields

A retained application record of an observed DevOps approval request context, including its native approval identity, execution, exact request evidence and action digest. It is a control/audit entity, not evidence that a tool ran successfully.

Logical identity
workspaceId + approvalRequestId
Retained record
workspaceId + approvalRequestId + version
Owner / authority
The collector owns request content and observed rawState. DecideApproval and ResumeExecution admit separate Commands under current authorization and exact request context; local clients cannot set provider approval state directly.
Lifecycle
Observed request/state changes publish ApprovalRequest versions. Decision and resume Command identities are retained independently, allowing partial success or an ambiguous response to remain visible. Neither decision acceptance nor resumption proves the intended operational result.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · ApprovalRequest

Use cases

Approve a precisely observed action

Context. An execution pauses with a validated approval request.

Use. Review its exact actionDigest and request Source, then submit DecideApproval against that context.

Result. The accepted decision is auditable without broadening its scope or assuming action execution.

Recover decision success with failed resume

Context. The approval call succeeds but the resume response is lost or fails.

Use. Keep decisionCommandIds and resumeCommandIds distinct and inspect their reconciled outcomes before any new action.

Result. The UI preserves partial success and uncertainty rather than showing a false completed action.

Invariants and interpretation

  • Preserve actual native approval, interrupt and tool-use context; a button label is not identity.
  • A successful rejection is different from a failed API request.
  • Approval redemption or decision acceptance does not prove successful tool execution.
  • Lost approval/resume responses require a verified recovery path, not blind mutating replay.

Where it was defined and how it was used

ApprovalRequest, DecisionAttempt, ResumeAttempt

Origin type: application-control-audit.

Previous use. The earlier UI contract modeled an observed request context around native approval values, then separate UpdateApprovalAction decision and SendMessage resumption stages. Space-scoped approvalId was separate from interrupt/tool/execution context.

Consolidation decision. ApprovalRequest remains the observed request entity. DecisionAttempt and ResumeAttempt consolidate into Command, with ordinary entity versions and no implied single-execution limit on reusable native approval identity.

Asset

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR12 fields

A native DevOps asset root with ordinary entity versions. Each retained Asset representation selects an exact nativeVersion, Source and owned file descriptors, allowing historical content to be addressed without a separate AssetVersion entity.

Logical identity
workspaceId + assetId
Retained record
workspaceId + assetId + version
Owner / authority
The collector owns the observed metadata, native version and file evidence. assetType is open provider content; documented metadata profiles remain qualified source interpretation rather than arbitrary writable fields on the canonical entity.
Lifecycle
Observed native metadata/content versions publish Asset versions under the same assetId. The application version and nativeVersion are separate. A historical read uses exact file/artifact references and reports unavailable content rather than substituting the provider’s latest alias.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Asset

Use cases

Reopen an attached checklist

Context. An investigation references a skill or attachment that has since changed.

Use. Use the captured Asset version and exact nativeVersion/file evidence retained for that historical context.

Result. The original reviewed content is reproducible if retained and authorized, instead of being replaced by current files.

Separate available context from consumed inputs

Context. The AgentSpace contains skills and memories while an execution runs.

Use. Retain asset availability/configuration with provenance and record actual consumption only when source evidence supports it.

Result. The UI does not claim that every available current asset was used by the historical execution.

Where it was defined and how it was used

Asset, AssetVersion, AssetFileVersion, ArtifactReference

Origin type: native-resource-and-versioned-content.

Previous use. The earlier model kept native assets/files distinct from journal content and A2A artifacts and required a specific assetVersion for reproducible historical reads.

Consolidation decision. AssetVersion is no longer an independent entity or nested independent history array. Asset uses the same identity/version contract as all entities, with nativeVersion and files as fields of the selected representation.

Workflow · 4 entities

Scenario authoring, publication, admitted runs and execution history.

Workflow · entity

Scenario

#
Versioned entityAPPLICATION11 fields

One application-authored workflow definition with a stable identity and DRAFT, PUBLISHED or ARCHIVED representations. A Scenario owns step definitions, operation locks, checks and publication metadata; versions express publication history without a separate ScenarioRevision entity.

Logical identity
workspaceId + scenarioId
Retained record
workspaceId + scenarioId + version
Owner / authority
Application authoring commands own the definition. PublishScenario validates and freezes the complete executable contract, schemas, expression/reducer rules and immutable operation locks under the Scenario version. Owned step definitions have no independent CRUD lifecycle.
Lifecycle
CreateScenario begins a draft; UpdateScenario appends a draft representation; PublishScenario appends a PUBLISHED representation with its digest. Editing a published or archived definition creates a later DRAFT without changing old publications. ArchiveScenario appends an ARCHIVED head that blocks new admissions, while exact replay of an already admitted Run preserves its receipt.
Sealing rule
Published version content and locks are immutable. Editing opens a later DRAFT version; publishing or archiving appends another version. History is never reopened.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Scenario

Use cases

Publish a repeatable fault exercise

Context. An author defines a fault action, workload checks and finalizers.

Use. Publish the Scenario so every operation alias resolves to an exact retained implementation/schema lock and the check definitions are frozen.

Result. A Run can select a reproducible program rather than whichever implementation an alias points to later.

Revise without changing earlier runs

Context. The author adjusts the error-budget check after one run has finished.

Use. Create a later DRAFT and then publish another Scenario version; earlier Runs keep their exact PUBLISHED reference.

Result. Definition evolution does not rewrite the criteria or behavior of an admitted run.

Invariants and interpretation

  • A published Scenario version is immutable.
  • New drafts do not invalidate explicit selection of an older PUBLISHED version; a current ARCHIVED head blocks new admission.
  • A FIS ExperimentTemplate is provider configuration, not automatically a Scenario.
  • A digest establishes declared content integrity, not external cloud immutability or permission.

Where it was defined and how it was used

Scenario, ScenarioRevision, StepDefinition, OperationLock

Origin type: application-authoring-aggregate.

Previous use. The earlier workflow split mutable Scenario catalog metadata from immutable ScenarioRevision configuration, with definitions and complete dependency locks owned by each revision.

Consolidation decision. ScenarioRevision is folded into Scenario. Draft editing, publication and archival now append ordinary Scenario versions under one identity; owned values inherit that version.

aws/fis/analysis/workflow/model.md

publication, operation lock, revision digest

Origin type: application-execution-contract.

Previous use. Publication resolved aliases and retained implementation/schema contracts; admission rejected missing or revoked pinned artifacts rather than silently substituting current aliases.

Consolidation decision. Those invariants remain, with Run selecting EntityRef(Scenario,id,version) instead of a separate revision ID.

Workflow · entity

Run

#
Versioned entityWORKFLOW19 fields

An admitted execution of one exact published Scenario version, with a frozen input Snapshot and an explicitly selected history of StepRuns. Run keeps orchestration, acceptance, finalization and external-effect state separate.

Logical identity
workspaceId + runId
Retained record
workspaceId + runId + version
Owner / authority
The workflow runtime owns Run lifecycle publications. StartRun performs trusted admission; RequestRunCancellation records monotonic control intent. Clients cannot set executionOutcome, assessmentVerdict or runtime status through a generic update.
Lifecycle
Admission pins the PUBLISHED Scenario, resolved bindings, enabled steps and required criterion denominator before dispatch. State transitions append Run versions. Cancellation fences new main dispatch while existing effects are reconciled. Terminal Run facts are sealed; later observations or new evaluation Projections do not rewrite the admitted execution.
Sealing rule
Lifecycle changes append versions. A settled/terminal record cannot be reopened; late reconciliation is new evidence and does not rewrite settled facts.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Run

Use cases

Execute a published checkout exercise

Context. An operator starts a known Scenario version against captured workload bindings.

Use. Read the Run’s exact scenario, inputSnapshot and pinned StepRun references as its runtime progresses.

Result. The console can explain what was admitted and which exact child representations produced a displayed result.

Cancel while the remote effect is uncertain

Context. A fault-start request may have reached AWS but its response was lost.

Use. Record cancellation intent, reconcile the originating dispatch and use finalization/effect dimensions to retain unresolved remote work.

Result. The Run can terminate with an indeterminate effect state rather than falsely reporting that cancellation restored the workload.

Invariants and interpretation

  • Run pins an exact PUBLISHED Scenario and RUN_INPUT Snapshot.
  • Runtime skipping or cancellation cannot shrink the admitted required-criterion denominator.
  • No required criteria means NOT_EVALUATED, not automatic success.
  • A finished Run or passed verdict does not establish remote cleanup.
  • Run.steps references exact StepRun versions; historical reads cannot join current child heads.

Where it was defined and how it was used

Run, AdmissionSnapshot

Origin type: application-execution-aggregate.

Previous use. The earlier Run owned admission context, cancellation, steps and attempts and pinned one ScenarioRevision. Its final result was sealed.

Consolidation decision. Run now has an ordinary entity version, pins a Scenario version and a shared Snapshot, and records exact child versions rather than latest-only child IDs.

aws/fis/analysis/workflow/model.md

execution phase, assessment verdict, finalization, remoteDisposition

Origin type: application-execution-state.

Previous use. The workflow model separated technical outcome, required-check verdict, finalization and unknown remote effects. An empty required set was not automatically passed.

Consolidation decision. The same dimensions remain explicit on Run; independent projectionVersion counters are removed in favor of Run.version.

aws/fis/analysis/workflow/model.md

CancellationIntent, finalizers, unresolvedEffects

Origin type: owned-control-values.

Previous use. Cancellation fenced further main dispatch, cleanup had a separate finite budget and unresolved effects remained indeterminate rather than hidden as normal cancellation.

Consolidation decision. These remain Run-owned control and state semantics with versioned command receipts and retained effect evidence.

Workflow · entity

StepRun

#
Versioned entityWORKFLOW12 fields

The Run-owned lifecycle of one named Scenario step, including a step that never executes. It provides the scheduling outcome, explicit attempt selection and exact retry history without becoming an independently editable workflow definition.

Logical identity
workspaceId + runId + stepKey
Retained record
workspaceId + stepRunId + version
Owner / authority
The workflow runtime owns StepRun. Its uniqueness includes runId and stepKey; Scenario owns the corresponding StepDefinition value. There is no independent retry, status-edit or step-authoring command for StepRun.
Lifecycle
Runtime transitions publish StepRun versions. attempts retains exact StepAttempt references and selectedAttempt states which result drives the step’s interpretation. A skipped step can validly have zero attempts, with a reason retained. The parent Run selects the exact StepRun versions used by that representation.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · StepRun

Use cases

Explain a zero-attempt skipped check

Context. A required check cannot run because an upstream action failed.

Use. Retain its StepRun with skipReason and zero attempts rather than deleting it.

Result. The required criterion remains visible and cannot disappear from the Run denominator.

Inspect a permitted retry

Context. A read-only query is retried under the published bounded retry policy.

Use. Keep both attempt references and explicitly select the attempt used by the step result.

Result. The UI can explain retry history without confusing transport polling with a new workflow step.

workspaceIdRequiredId

stepKeyRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.

Maximum length: 4096

outcomeRequiredAny of: "SUCCEEDED" · "FAILED" · "CANCELED" · "BLOCKED" · "TIMED_OUT" · "INDETERMINATE" · "SKIPPED" | nullUses the declared type and containing contract.
selectedAttemptRequiredAny of: EntityRef (kind = "StepAttempt") | nullUses the declared type and containing contract.
attemptsRequiredArray of EntityRef (kind = "StepAttempt")

Exact known attempt representations selected by this StepRun version, one per attempt identity.

Maximum items: 100

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Invariants and interpretation

  • StepRun is runtime state, not the authored StepDefinition.
  • One Run/stepKey identifies the step; retries are StepAttempts.
  • Zero attempts is valid for a skipped step.
  • Selecting an attempt does not discard earlier attempts or unresolved effects.

Where it was defined and how it was used

StepRun

Origin type: application-owned-runtime-entity.

Previous use. The prior workflow had exactly one StepRun for every compiled main/finalizer step, even if never attempted, with no independent retry/status mutation API.

Consolidation decision. The entity is retained and uniformly versioned. attempts and selectedAttempt pin exact child representations rather than implicit current records.

Workflow · entity

StepAttempt

#
Versioned entityWORKFLOW15 fields

One durable execution attempt of a StepRun, with a stable dispatch identity, observed external effects, exact evidence and optional check result. It is the record that makes retry and uncertain-effect handling concrete.

Logical identity
workspaceId + runId + stepRunId + attemptNo
Retained record
workspaceId + stepAttemptId + version
Owner / authority
The workflow runtime owns attempt facts. attemptNo counts deliberate retries and is distinct from StepAttempt.version. ExternalOperationRef and CheckResult are owned values; their provenance and remote disposition remain explicit.
Lifecycle
The dispatch key is persisted before any provider call. Polling, transport recovery and checkpoint resume stay within the same attempt; a permitted deliberate retry creates another attempt only after the previous effect is reconciled. Lifecycle versions accumulate until settlement, after which attempt facts are sealed. Late reconciliation adds new evidence rather than rewriting the settled attempt.
Sealing rule
Lifecycle changes append versions. A settled/terminal record cannot be reopened; late reconciliation is new evidence and does not rewrite settled facts.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · StepAttempt

Use cases

Reconcile a lost FIS start response

Context. A worker loses contact after dispatching the FIS start request.

Use. Use the retained dispatchKey and external-operation intent to investigate the existing effect through a supported non-creating recovery path.

Result. The engine avoids launching a second fault merely to discover whether the first exists.

Retain a conclusive check result

Context. A workload query supplies sufficient evidence for a required assertion.

Use. Store the result with evaluator/predicate identity, cutoff and exact evidence references on the settled attempt.

Result. The result can be audited without treating later samples or a new evaluator as part of the original check.

Fields

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
stepAttemptIdRequiredId

Stable logical identity of this StepAttempt; the entity version selects a retained representation.

workspaceIdRequiredId

Trusted application scope. Request bodies cannot select a tenant.

versionRequiredVersion

updatedAtRequiredTimestamp

Local publication time of this entity representation; nondecreasing across versions.

runIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
stepRunIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
attemptNoRequiredPositiveIntegerUses the declared type and containing contract.
dispatchKeyRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
outcomeRequired"PENDING" · "RUNNING" · "SUCCEEDED" · "FAILED" · "CANCELED" · "TIMED_OUT" · "INDETERMINATE"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
startedAtRequiredTimestampUses the declared type and containing contract.
settledAtRequiredAny of: Timestamp | nullUses the declared type and containing contract.
checkResultRequiredAny of: CheckResult | nullUses the declared type and containing contract.
externalOperationsRequiredArray of ExternalOperationRefMaximum items: 100
evidenceRefsRequiredArray of EvidenceRefMaximum items: 1000

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Invariants and interpretation

  • Persist dispatch intent before the external call.
  • A timeout or lost handle does not establish that the remote effect did not happen.
  • A new mutating attempt is forbidden while the earlier effect is unresolved.
  • A false assertion is not a retryable technical error.
  • Sealed facts remain unchanged; later reconciliation is separately retained evidence.

Where it was defined and how it was used

StepAttempt

Origin type: application-owned-runtime-entity.

Previous use. The earlier attempt was scoped by Run, step and attempt number, appended dispatch/checkpoint/effect facts during execution and sealed terminal facts.

Consolidation decision. StepAttempt retains its own identity and common version metadata; attemptNo remains an execution-order fact.

aws/fis/analysis/workflow/model.md

dispatchKey, ExternalOperationRef, remoteDisposition

Origin type: owned-effect-values.

Previous use. The workflow required persisted dispatch intent before calls, reconciliation before mutating retry and explicit indeterminate outcomes for unresolved effects.

Consolidation decision. Those safeguards remain with exact entity/evidence references and no exception to universal versioning.

aws/fis/analysis/workflow/model.md

CheckResult, Evidence, evaluation cutoff

Origin type: owned-evaluation-and-evidence.

Previous use. Assertions froze evidence IDs, evaluator contracts and cutoff; unavailable or insufficient evidence could not establish conclusive absence, and later data could not silently rewrite a sealed result.

Consolidation decision. Shared Source/Observation/Projection evidence replaces a separate generic Evidence entity while settled attempt facts stay sealed.

FIS · entity

Experiment

#
Versioned entityCOLLECTOR13 fields

One native AWS FIS experiment, independently observable whether or not the console launched it. It retains runtime configuration/evidence, named action values, selected target memberships, resolution coverage and report state.

Logical identity
workspaceId + experimentId
Retained record
workspaceId + experimentId + version
Owner / authority
The FIS collector owns observed experiment representations. Native actions, dependencies, selector bindings, target accounts and reports remain provider-owned values under Experiment rather than independent console StepRuns or controllable action entities.
Lifecycle
Accepted provider observations publish Experiment versions under the scoped native identity. The historical run is interpreted from its retained runtime configuration and template provenance, never from current mutable template contents. StopExperiment records asynchronous intent; subsequent observed status and independent workload/effect evidence establish what followed.
Sealing rule
Every stored version is immutable. Authorized changes append the next version of the same entity; provider state changes do not rewrite prior versions.
Authoritative contract
model/schema.json · Experiment

Use cases

Inspect a workflow-launched fault

Context. A StepAttempt starts FIS and retains its external experiment identity.

Use. Follow that evidence to Experiment while keeping the console Run/StepRun graph separate from native named actions.

Result. The operator sees both orchestration and provider execution without fabricating independent action controls.

Compare selected scope with observed recovery

Context. An experiment completes and its report later becomes available.

Use. Inspect targetMemberships, resolutionCoverage, actions and report independently, then evaluate workload telemetry through Projection.

Result. Selected targets, action completion, report readiness and workload recovery remain separate evidence-backed claims.

Invariants and interpretation

  • No individual native action stop, retry or pause operation is invented.
  • Named action identity is experiment plus action name, not catalog actionId.
  • Selected membership does not prove a per-resource fault occurred.
  • A stopped experiment does not prove workload recovery.
  • Report availability is independent of experiment outcome and acceptance verdict.

Where it was defined and how it was used

ExperimentRun, Experiment, ActionExecution, ActionDependency

Origin type: native-resource-and-owned-runtime-values.

Previous use. The FIS analysis centered on the native experiment and named action map keys, preserving same-experiment dependency/binding scope and the runtime configuration snapshot.

Consolidation decision. Experiment remains the native entity. Named action/runtime members are owned values, and universal Experiment versions replace any special state-history classes.

aws/fis/analysis/report.md

TargetSelection, ResolvedTargetMembership, ExperimentTargetAccount, TargetResolutionObservation

Origin type: provider-owned-values-and-collection-evidence.

Previous use. The prior model retained every selector membership, complete targetInformation and separate resolution-ended versus page-traversal evidence; configured target accounts were not child experiments or per-account results.

Consolidation decision. Experiment retains memberships and qualified coverage; optional canonical Resource resolution is evidence-based, and shared Collection/Source/Observation retain the collection mechanics.

aws/fis/analysis/report.md

Experiment, ExternalOperationRef, named FIS action, FIS report

Origin type: provider-execution-boundary.

Previous use. The generalized workflow treated an experiment as an external execution of a StepAttempt and native action detail as provider-owned, while reports and checks had independent lifecycles.

Consolidation decision. That boundary is preserved: Run can refer to zero, one or several Experiment identities, and workload acceptance remains a Projection rather than a native experiment field.

Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Orient an operator in the correct scope

Actor. Console user

Context. An operator opens the console before reviewing a checkout service and needs the selected workspace name and enabled modules.

When to use. At application entry or when auditing the exact workspace representation retained by another record.

Intended result. The interface identifies the selected application workspace without accepting a tenant selector in JSON.

  1. Read the authenticated workspace head, or pass an exact retained version for an audit.
  2. Use its configuration to explain the visible module scope; enforce current permissions independently.

Preconditions

  • Authentication must already establish the workspace; a version does not select a different workspace.

Request · GetWorkspaceRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
versionOptionalVersion

Immutable representation number. In a getter request, omission selects the current head once.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · GetWorkspaceResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
workspaceRequiredWorkspaceUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Workspace comes exclusively from authenticated context; the request cannot select a tenant.
  • version selects an exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head; current authorization is always enforced, including historical reads.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Workspace is the application authorization boundary. AgentSpace is a separate native DevOps resource.
  • Historical workspace configuration cannot restore access that has since been revoked.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Use case

Compare a service before and after a membership edit

Actor. Reviewer

Context. A service has changed since a topology review. The reviewer needs the retained versions under the same serviceId rather than a separate revision object.

When to use. When finding a known entity’s historical representations before reading an exact version.

Intended result. The reviewer can compare exact representations while preserving ordinary entity identity and domain authorization.

  1. Supply its EntityIdentity and traverse the returned references in descending version order.
  2. Resolve selected references through the normal typed getter with the returned version.

Preconditions

  • The caller needs both history permission and the entity’s normal read permission; a Workspace identity must match authenticated scope.

Operation semantics

  • Enumerates immutable exact references for one logical entity, ordered by descending version in a fixed traversal. References are values, not separately managed Version resources.
  • Resolve each reference with that entity's Get operation and the returned version. Historical versions are never silently replaced by current heads.
  • The current caller must hold both history capability and the entity's normal domain-read permission; each returned version must authorize its full retained closure.
  • A Workspace identity must equal the already authenticated workspace. This operation cannot select another tenant or bypass domain parent/scope checks.
  • The cursor binds entity kind/id, authenticated scope and the traversal's retained version set. It exposes no hidden version count.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Returned values are EntityRef values, not independently managed Version resources.
  • Missing or inaccessible historical content must never be replaced with the current head. Pagination reveals no hidden version count.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, PaginationTokenExpiredException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Review the connection pinned to a command

Actor. Operator

Context. A command names a Connection version. An operator checks which provider scope and credential binding were admitted.

When to use. Before a scoped action, or to explain a recorded access path.

Intended result. The operator understands the configured access path and can choose an authorized binding.

  1. Read the exact Connection reference from the command when reviewing history.
  2. For a new action, inspect current configuration and the proposed binding scope.

Preconditions

  • The Connection must be visible within the authenticated workspace.

Request · GetConnectionRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
connectionIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
versionOptionalVersion

Immutable representation number. In a getter request, omission selects the current head once.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · GetConnectionResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
connectionRequiredConnectionUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • A Connection reference conveys no permission by itself; current authority is rechecked for dispatch.
  • Historical configuration does not reveal secrets or reinstate a disabled access path.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Use case

Choose a connection for a scoped collection

Actor. Collector administrator

Context. A team needs a configured connection for collecting evidence about a service in its account and Region.

When to use. When selecting an existing access path before admitting collection or provider intent.

Intended result. A suitable configured connection can be selected without passing raw credentials.

  1. List enabled connections and traverse all required pages.
  2. Inspect the chosen connection’s scopes and exact version before including it in the request.

Preconditions

  • The caller must have connection-read permission in the authenticated workspace.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.

Interpretation and recovery

  • enabled=true is a configuration filter, not proof of current provider access or successful authentication.
  • A complete local list does not establish complete AWS inventory.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, PaginationTokenExpiredException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Use case

Register an approved evidence-collection access path

Actor. Workspace administrator

Context. An approved identity binding exists for a test account, and the team needs a named connection with bounded allowed scopes.

When to use. After the credential binding is registered and its usable scope is known.

Intended result. A versioned local Connection exists for subsequent scoped operations.

  1. Provide the binding ID, provider, name and allowed scopes with a clientToken.
  2. Review the returned Connection and Command before using the connection in collection.

Preconditions

  • The binding must already exist; requested scopes must fit both caller grants and binding capabilities.

Operation semantics

  • Binds an already registered secret/identity reference after authorization; accepts no credential bytes.
  • Requested scopes are checked against the caller's grant and the binding's capabilities; references do not grant access.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The request accepts a binding reference, never credential bytes.
  • Reusing the same token with a different scope or binding is a conflicting intent, not an edit.

When to use. When changing or disabling configured access rather than rewriting evidence history.

Preconditions

Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Resolve the database referenced by a finding

Actor. Responder

Context. A service review identifies a database Resource. The responder needs its observed identity and provenance before relating it to a lifecycle exposure.

When to use. When moving from a canonical resource reference to inventory evidence.

Intended result. The resource identity can be examined without assuming a display name is a stable provider key.

  1. Read the exact Resource version retained in the review, or select the current head for live navigation.
  2. Follow selectedObservation and evaluate matching provenance before treating a provider identifier as equivalent.

Preconditions

  • The Resource must be visible; retained evidence must be authorized.

Request · GetResourceRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
resourceIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
versionOptionalVersion

Immutable representation number. In a getter request, omission selects the current head once.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · GetResourceResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
resourceRequiredResourceUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • A Resource is inventory identity, not every possible provider object.
  • Run-scoped or provisional identity needs its explicit boundary; matching names alone cannot prove continuity.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Inventory the resources attached to checkout

Actor. Service owner

Context. The owner is preparing a service review and wants the known database resources associated with checkout.

When to use. When assembling a current local inventory view.

Intended result. The owner sees the retained service inventory with explicit evidence to assess coverage.

  1. Filter by serviceId and resourceType as needed and follow nextToken.
  2. Inspect individual resources and the collections that supplied their observations.

Preconditions

  • The service filter must refer to an authorized local service.

itemsRequiredArray of Resource

The operation's typed result collection. Parent/version and ordering semantics are specified below.

Minimum items: 0
Maximum items: 100
pageRequiredPage

Publication metadata for the selected traversal; it is not a domain Snapshot.

nextTokenOptionalstring

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.

Interpretation and recovery

  • An empty local page is not proof that the provider has no resources.
  • Resource identity matching and collection coverage remain separate from service membership.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, PaginationTokenExpiredException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Use case

Explain an incomplete topology review

Actor. Reviewer

Context. A topology view has a gap. The reviewer checks whether dependency detail reads failed or whether list pagination remains open.

When to use. When judging how far a collection’s evidence supports a conclusion.

Intended result. The reviewer can distinguish collected objects from justified completeness claims.

  1. Read the Collection version referenced by the view or capture.
  2. Inspect each coverage dimension and follow the referenced ReadAttempts.

Preconditions

  • The selected Collection and its retained reference closure must be readable.

  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Successful completion of a collection is not an atomic AWS snapshot.
  • Pagination, hydration, identity resolution and claim sufficiency are independent facts.

Foundation · operation

ListCollections

#
READCONTRACT_ONLYP2_READ_AND_INGEST

Locate finite collections by connection or exact subject for evidence review and operational diagnosis.

Wire target
POST /
X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.ListCollections
Media type
application/x-amz-json-1.1
Permission
console:Read · proposed application capability
Entity scope
Collection
Scope members
connectionId, subject
Effect
Read-only selection of retained data; no implicit fresh provider collection.
Provider dispatch
No direct native dispatch declared by this operation.
Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Find the collection behind a stale service view

Actor. Collector operator

Context. A service status view appears stale and the operator wants to inspect collections associated with that subject.

When to use. When locating collection records before inspecting individual query outcomes.

Intended result. The operator can identify the retained collection that explains the available evidence.

  1. List collections for the relevant subject or connection.
  2. Read candidate collections and compare their coverage and source timing.

Preconditions

  • Filters must use authorized references and preserve their exact meaning throughout pagination.

Request · ListCollectionsRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
connectionIdOptionalIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
subjectOptionalEntityRefUses the declared type and containing contract.
maxResultsOptionalinteger

Requested page bound; default 20, maximum 100. A response may contain fewer rows.

Minimum: 1
Maximum: 100
nextTokenOptionalstring

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · ListCollectionsResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
itemsRequiredArray of Collection

The operation's typed result collection. Parent/version and ordering semantics are specified below.

Minimum items: 0
Maximum items: 100
pageRequiredPage

Publication metadata for the selected traversal; it is not a domain Snapshot.

nextTokenOptionalstring

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Collection updatedAt is local publication time; it is not proof that upstream evidence is fresh.
  • This list does not silently start another collection.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, PaginationTokenExpiredException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Foundation · operation

GetReadAttempt

#
READCONTRACT_ONLYP2_READ_AND_INGEST

Read the retained facts for one actual provider read attempt, including failures, empty results and request/response references.

Wire target
POST /
X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.GetReadAttempt
Media type
application/x-amz-json-1.1
Permission
console:Read · proposed application capability
Entity scope
ReadAttempt
Scope members
collectionId, readAttemptId
Effect
Read-only selection of retained data; no implicit fresh provider collection.
Provider dispatch
No direct native dispatch declared by this operation.
Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Investigate a read that returned no usable evidence

Actor. Collector operator

Context. A dependency query has no objects and the operator must distinguish a known empty response from a lost response or failed call.

When to use. When explaining a collection gap or auditing a specific dispatched read.

Intended result. An empty successful result can be distinguished from absent response content.

  1. Supply the owning collectionId and the exact attempt version referenced by the coverage record.
  2. Inspect state, error, returnedCount and exact requestSource/responseSource references.

Preconditions

  • The readAttemptId must belong to the supplied collection; current evidence access applies.

Request · GetReadAttemptRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
collectionIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
readAttemptIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
versionOptionalVersion

Response · GetReadAttemptResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
readAttemptRequiredReadAttemptUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • A null responseSource after response loss is not an empty successful response.
  • A receipt that pins STARTED does not automatically retarget to a later settled version.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

ListReadAttempts

#
READCONTRACT_ONLYP2_READ_AND_INGEST

Enumerate the read attempts retained for a collection, including calls that failed or returned zero objects.

Wire target
POST /
X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.ListReadAttempts
Media type
application/x-amz-json-1.1
Permission
console:Read · proposed application capability
Entity scope
ReadAttempt
Scope members
collectionId
Effect
Read-only selection of retained data; no implicit fresh provider collection.
Provider dispatch
No direct native dispatch declared by this operation.
Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Audit why a collection cannot support an absence claim

Actor. Reviewer

Context. The object list is empty, but the reviewer needs to see every recorded read and its settlement before accepting an absence conclusion.

When to use. When reviewing collector behavior independently of returned object rows.

Intended result. Failed and empty reads remain visible as evidence of how collection proceeded.

  1. Traverse the attempts for the collection.
  2. Read the relevant exact attempts and compare their facts with the collection’s coverage rationale.

Preconditions

  • The collection must be authorized and pagination must retain the same scope.

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.
  • Includes failed and empty reads; their absence from returned object rows must not erase collection evidence.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The list returns retained attempt heads, not a replacement for the exact versions referenced by historical coverage.
  • A completed traversal does not itself establish sufficient upstream claim coverage.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, PaginationTokenExpiredException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.
