Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Inspect the raw detail supporting a recommendation

Actor. Analyst

Context. A recommendation cites a finding-detail Source version. The analyst needs that exact content, including preserved provider fields.

When to use. When verifying a canonical interpretation or following an EvidenceRef of kind Source.

Intended result. The evidence remains tied to the provider representation actually cited.

  1. Use the sourceId and version from the referring record.
  2. Inspect the registered profile, representation, field presence and retained payload or authorized artifact reference.

Preconditions

  • The source and any retained artifact content must be currently authorized and available.

Request · GetSourceRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
sourceIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
versionOptionalVersion

Immutable representation number. In a getter request, omission selects the current head once.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · GetSourceResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
sourceRequiredSourceUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • An omitted version selects the current head and can show different content from the cited evidence.
  • Matching payload digests do not merge source identities, and INLINE null is a legitimate payload value.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Use case

Explain why identical content was seen twice

Actor. Collector analyst

Context. Two polls returned the same provider document. The analyst needs to distinguish separate observations from a change in the provider representation.

When to use. When reasoning about receipt chronology, freshness or collection provenance.

Intended result. Separate receipts can be understood without manufacturing new logical provider objects.

  1. Read the Observation version referenced by the domain entity or projection.
  2. Follow its exact Source and, for API reads, its retained ReadAttempt reference.

Preconditions

  • Referenced evidence and connection provenance must be within the caller’s current visibility.

observationRequiredObservationUses the declared type and containing contract.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • observedAt is receipt time, not provider event order.
  • A repeated observation may point to the same Source version; source version and observation identity serve different purposes.

Use case

Reproduce a previous service-status explanation

Actor. Reviewer

Context. A past review cites Projection version 2 even though a later derivation is now selected. The reviewer needs the earlier result and rationale.

When to use. For exact historical interpretations or when inspecting derivation provenance.

Intended result. The prior interpretation remains reviewable alongside the precise evidence that supported it.

  1. Request the exact projectionId and version cited by the review.
  2. Inspect subjectRefs, inputRefs, ruleDigest, asOf and coverage before interpreting value.

Preconditions

  • The caller must be authorized for the full retained projection closure.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • A new generatedAt does not make old inputs fresh.
  • A projection records a qualified interpretation; it does not mutate the source subjects or rewrite a sealed Run.

Use case

Prepare a remediation handoff

Actor. Service owner

Context. A recommendation has an associated work item. The incoming owner needs the current assignment, resolution notes and evidence used for verification.

When to use. When examining operator work around a finding, event or recommendation.

Intended result. The handoff can describe what people did and what has been independently verified.

  1. Read the WorkItem head for current coordination, or an exact version for an audit.
  2. Inspect target identities, action history, resolutionEvidence and verificationState separately.

Preconditions

  • The work item and any referenced target evidence must be currently authorized.

Use case

Recover from a timed-out mutation request

Actor. Operator or client recovery handler

Context. A provider-facing request timed out after admission. The caller needs to discover whether the intent was accepted and what outcome is now known.

When to use. After receiving a command receipt or when resuming observation of an admitted intent.

Intended result. The caller can recover through the durable receipt without inventing a new mutation.

  1. Read the command head for current progress, retaining exact versions that matter to later actions.
  2. Inspect state, attempts, effects and resultRefs before following the reconciled entity.

Preconditions

  • The command must belong to the authorized workspace and caller-visible scope.

Request · GetCommandRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • HTTP 200 or ACCEPTED is not evidence that an AWS effect occurred.
  • OUTCOME_UNKNOWN requires safe reconciliation. A succeeded command means its documented intent succeeded, not that the workload is healthy.

Use case

Find a retained FIS template without a new domain entity

Actor. Workflow author

Context. An author needs to inspect a retained FIS template profile before choosing a published workflow input.

When to use. When locating native peripheral resources or raw representations behind canonical entities.

Intended result. Native detail remains accessible through a typed source profile.

  1. Filter by the registered profile, scoped identity or representation.
  2. Read the selected exact Source version and inspect its provider scope and retained content.

Preconditions

  • Filters and returned content must be within current source-read authority.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.
  • Native peripheral resources are retained typed profiles, including FIS templates/catalogs and DevOps registrations/triggers/goals.
  • Representation and source identity are explicit; matching hashes do not merge different logical source records.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Equal hashes or display names are not identity joins.
  • This list does not imply that a retained template is currently usable or that an operation is authorized to execute it.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, PaginationTokenExpiredException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Earlier operations and consolidation

Resilience ListInputSources maps to typed source discovery. The prior ListEvents and workflow ListRunEvidence also decompose into source, observation and projection queries according to evidence kind.

Earlier operation / packageDispositionCurrent operations / meaning
ListSystems
aws/resilience-hub/analysis/api		CANONICAL_READ_WITH_NATIVE_FACETListSystems, ListSources

Canonical catalog list plus typed native source profiles; unresolved native references are not silently discarded.

ListUserJourneys
aws/resilience-hub/analysis/api		CANONICAL_READ_WITH_NATIVE_FACETListUserJourneys, ListSources

Canonical catalog list plus typed native source profiles; unresolved native references are not silently discarded.

ListServices
aws/resilience-hub/analysis/api		CANONICAL_READ_WITH_NATIVE_FACETListServices, ListSources

Canonical catalog list plus typed native source profiles; unresolved native references are not silently discarded.

ListInputSources
aws/resilience-hub/analysis/api		RETAINED_TYPED_PROFILEListSources, GetSource

Use aws.resilience-hub.input-source/v1 and exact service-scoped source identity.

ListEvents
aws/resilience-hub/analysis/api		SHARED_EVIDENCE_READListObservations, ListSources

Filter exact subjects/profile/channel evidence; delivery ID never becomes a HealthEvent ID.

ListRunEvidence
aws/fis/analysis/workflow		SHARED_TYPED_EVIDENCEListObservations, ListSources, ListProjections

Filter the exact Run subject/producer references; raw source, receipt and derived evidence types stay explicit.

ListSourceRevisions
consolidated-operations-console/api@db142c84bcfd691d5c71071681731cac81a52c7b		BREAKING_CONTRACT_V2ListSources, ListEntityVersions

List current Source heads; enumerate a Source identity's versions through the common history operation.

Related next operations. GetSource, StartCollection.

Foundation · operation

ListObservations

#
READCONTRACT_ONLYP2_READ_AND_INGEST

Find retained receipts by exact Source, collection or subject without collapsing repeated receipt events.

Wire target
POST /
X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.ListObservations
Media type
application/x-amz-json-1.1
Permission
console:Read · proposed application capability
Entity scope
Observation
Scope members
source, collectionId, subject
Effect
Read-only selection of retained data; no implicit fresh provider collection.
Provider dispatch
No direct native dispatch declared by this operation.
Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Trace the observations supporting a service review

Actor. Evidence analyst

Context. A reviewer wants to know which receipts were associated with a service and whether they came from an API collection or another channel.

When to use. When exploring receipt chronology before resolving individual evidence references.

Intended result. The evidence trail preserves timing and access provenance distinct from provider content identity.

  1. Filter by the relevant subject, source or collection and traverse the bounded pages.
  2. Read selected observations and follow their exact sources and read attempts.

Preconditions

  • The caller must have current access to each complete returned observation.

Request · ListObservationsRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
sourceOptionalEntityRef kind = "Source"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
collectionIdOptionalIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
subjectOptionalEntityRefUses the declared type and containing contract.
maxResultsOptionalinteger

Requested page bound; default 20, maximum 100. A response may contain fewer rows.

Minimum: 1
Maximum: 100
nextTokenOptionalstring

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · ListObservationsResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
itemsRequiredArray of Observation

The operation's typed result collection. Parent/version and ordering semantics are specified below.

Minimum items: 0
Maximum items: 100
pageRequiredPage

Publication metadata for the selected traversal; it is not a domain Snapshot.

nextTokenOptionalstring

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The fixed list order is receipt chronology, not authoritative provider event order.
  • An event delivery is an Observation; its delivery ID does not become a HealthEvent identity.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, PaginationTokenExpiredException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Foundation · operation

ListProjections

#
READCONTRACT_ONLYP2_READ_AND_INGEST

Locate named derived views for a subject or profile while returning one selected head per logical projection.

Wire target
POST /
X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.ListProjections
Media type
application/x-amz-json-1.1
Permission
console:Read · proposed application capability
Entity scope
Projection
Scope members
subject
Effect
Read-only selection of retained data; no implicit fresh provider collection.
Provider dispatch
No direct native dispatch declared by this operation.
Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Find service-status and lifecycle interpretations

Actor. Analyst

Context. An analyst reviewing a workload wants the retained derived views relevant to its status and lifecycle exposure.

When to use. When selecting among available interpretations before reading their exact provenance.

Intended result. Distinct named views remain discoverable without introducing separate revision resources.

  1. Filter by exact subject or registered projection profile.
  2. Inspect the returned projection head and enumerate its history if a prior derivation is needed.

Preconditions

  • The caller must be authorized for each complete projection closure.

Request · ListProjectionsRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
subjectOptionalEntityRefUses the declared type and containing contract.
profileOptional"EVALUATION" · "LIFECYCLE_EXPOSURE" · "INVESTIGATION_RESULT" · "SERVICE_STATUS" · "WORKSPACE_SUMMARY"

Registered profile selecting the source or interpretation contract for this record.

maxResultsOptionalinteger

Requested page bound; default 20, maximum 100. A response may contain fewer rows.

Minimum: 1
Maximum: 100
nextTokenOptionalstring

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · ListProjectionsResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
itemsRequiredArray of Projection

The operation's typed result collection. Parent/version and ordering semantics are specified below.

Minimum items: 0
Maximum items: 100
pageRequiredPage

Publication metadata for the selected traversal; it is not a domain Snapshot.

nextTokenOptionalstring

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.
  • Returns current Projection heads. Each logical projection has ordinary entity versions; exact prior derivations remain readable without a ProjectionRevision entity.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Ordinary listing returns current heads within the fixed traversal, not all historical derivations.
  • A derived result is qualified by its inputs, rule and coverage, not by its publication date alone.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, PaginationTokenExpiredException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Use case

Find topology captures for a service review

Actor. Service reviewer

Context. Two topology reviews were captured at different times. The reviewer needs to locate the captures before comparing their exact members.

When to use. When browsing retained business captures rather than ordinary entity changes.

Intended result. The reviewer can compare two explicit captures without substituting current resource state.

  1. Filter by the service subject and kind=TOPOLOGY.
  2. Read each selected Snapshot and compare its captured members and evidence windows.

Preconditions

  • The subject reference and complete capture closure must be authorized.

Request · ListSnapshotsRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
subjectOptionalEntityRefUses the declared type and containing contract.
kindOptional"INVESTIGATION" · "TOPOLOGY" · "POLICY_CONTEXT" · "LIFECYCLE_CATALOG" · "RUN_INPUT" · "EVALUATION_INPUT"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
maxResultsOptionalinteger

Requested page bound; default 20, maximum 100. A response may contain fewer rows.

Minimum: 1
Maximum: 100
nextTokenOptionalstring

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · ListSnapshotsResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
itemsRequiredArray of Snapshot

The operation's typed result collection. Parent/version and ordering semantics are specified below.

Minimum items: 0
Maximum items: 100
pageRequiredPage

Publication metadata for the selected traversal; it is not a domain Snapshot.

nextTokenOptionalstring

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.

Interpretation and recovery

  • A list of captures does not prove any capture has complete upstream coverage.
  • Capture kind is meaningful; a topology capture cannot replace a Run’s input snapshot.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, PaginationTokenExpiredException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Synthetic request example 
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: console.example.invalid
Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.1
X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.ListSnapshots

{
  "maxResults": 20
}

Find local operator work by continuing target identity and work state.

Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Review outstanding work for a recommendation

Actor. Team lead

Context. A recommendation needs follow-up, and the team lead checks whether work already exists before creating a second assignment.

When to use. When coordinating local work around a domain target.

Intended result. Existing work can be reused and its current coordination state understood.

  1. Filter by the target identity and, when useful, state.
  2. Read matching work items to inspect owner, priority, actions and verification.

Preconditions

  • The target must be visible within the authenticated workspace.

Request · ListWorkItemsRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
targetOptionalEntityIdentityUses the declared type and containing contract.
stateOptional"OPEN" · "ACKNOWLEDGED" · "IN_PROGRESS" · "RESOLVED" · "DISMISSED"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
maxResultsOptionalinteger

Requested page bound; default 20, maximum 100. A response may contain fewer rows.

Minimum: 1
Maximum: 100
nextTokenOptionalstring

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · ListWorkItemsResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
itemsRequiredArray of WorkItem

The operation's typed result collection. Parent/version and ordering semantics are specified below.

Minimum items: 0
Maximum items: 100
pageRequiredPage

Publication metadata for the selected traversal; it is not a domain Snapshot.

nextTokenOptionalstring

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Work state does not replace native disposition or assessment verdict.
  • A current work list is not a historical evidence snapshot of the target.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, PaginationTokenExpiredException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Investigate unresolved provider requests

Actor. Operations supervisor

Context. Several operations have been admitted for a service, and a supervisor needs to find those whose provider outcomes remain uncertain.

When to use. When auditing command progress or recovering a known intent through its receipt.

Intended result. Uncertain external outcomes can be surfaced independently from domain status.

  1. Use subject, operation or state filters and retain the same query during pagination.
  2. Inspect each command’s current state and exact effects before deciding the next action.

Preconditions

  • The caller must be authorized for each command and its scope.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Command state is not workload health or remediation verification.
  • A new token creates a new intent; listing an uncertain command is not permission to resend a remote mutation.

Foundation · operation

StartCollection

#
INGESTCONTRACT_ONLYP2_READ_AND_INGEST

Admit a finite registered set of read-only provider queries under an exact Connection version.

Wire target
POST /
X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.StartCollection
Media type
application/x-amz-json-1.1
Permission
console:Collect · proposed application capability
Entity scope
Collection, Command
Scope members
connection
Effect
Mutating intent; a durable Command receipt is returned.
Provider dispatch
No direct native dispatch declared by this operation.
Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Collect evidence for a topology review

Actor. Trusted collector

Context. A service review needs inventory, dependency and policy evidence from a defined account and Region.

When to use. When initiating a bounded collection whose scope and queries can be reviewed in advance.

Intended result. The collection has an explicit scope against which attempts and later coverage can be recorded.

  1. Resolve the authorized Connection version and registered query definitions with canonical request digests.
  2. Submit the immutable query set with a clientToken, then inspect the admitted Collection.

Preconditions

  • Queries must exist in the registered read-only adapter catalog, have unique queryKeys and fit authorized scope.

Request · StartCollectionRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
connectionRequiredEntityRef kind = "Connection"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
queriesRequiredArray of CollectionQueryMinimum items: 1
Maximum items: 100
clientTokenRequiredstring

Opaque mutation-intent token. Exact replay requires the same operation, payload and preconditions.

Minimum length: 16
Maximum length: 128
Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · StartCollectionResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

collectionRequiredCollectionUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Admits a finite exact query set from the registered read-only adapter catalog; unknown operations or unauthorized scope fail admission.
  • queryKey uniqueness, canonical requestDigest, filter types and operation-specific bounds are validated against that registered adapter.
  • Completion, pagination, hydration, resolution and claim coverage remain independent facts.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Admission does not prove any provider read has finished.
  • Changing query definitions requires a new Collection identity; coverage cannot be inferred from the intent alone.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Example admission preconditions 
{
  "currentHeads": [],
  "notes": [
    "Independent design illustration, not a command to execute against the final model fixture heads."
  ]
}

Foundation · operation

RecordReadAttempt

#
INGESTCONTRACT_ONLYP2_READ_AND_INGEST

Settle an already recorded STARTED read attempt with exact request/response evidence and qualified result facts.

Wire target
POST /
X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.RecordReadAttempt
Media type
application/x-amz-json-1.1
Permission
console:IngestEvidence · proposed application capability
Entity scope
ReadAttempt, Command
Scope members
collectionId, readAttemptId, providerRequestId
Effect
Mutating intent; a durable Command receipt is returned.
Provider dispatch
No direct native dispatch declared by this operation.
Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Preserve an empty provider response

Actor. Trusted collector

Context. A real list request returns zero objects. The collector must retain the response rather than leaving a gap indistinguishable from a failed call.

When to use. After the dispatched read has a known settlement or an explicitly recorded lost-response failure.

Intended result. The same ReadAttempt receives its settled version, preserving the earlier STARTED representation.

  1. Use the existing attempt identity, expectedVersion and exact requestSource recorded before dispatch.
  2. Retain the response when available and submit settlement facts, including returnedCount, token presence or error.

Preconditions

  • The attempt must still be STARTED and its requestSource must match the retained dispatched request.

Response · RecordReadAttemptResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

readAttemptRequiredReadAttemptUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Settles the same existing STARTED ReadAttempt created by the trusted collector dispatch transaction before the actual read; does not append a second attempt or fabricate a pre-call record after the fact.
  • Trusted context assigns authorizationContextKey; a caller cannot forge its acting principal or provenance.
  • expectedVersion guards the existing STARTED ReadAttempt head. Settlement creates the next version of that same identity; prior STARTED representations remain intact.
  • requestSource must equal the exact already retained request envelope for this attempt. Response references must belong to this exact request and scope, including empty responses.
  • IngestObservation may retain response/object observations while the attempt is STARTED; settlement then references those revisions. A response-lost failure has an explicit null response reference, not a fabricated empty response.
  • A settled attempt is immutable. Exact replay returns the original result; conflicting terminal facts reject. Query identity, attemptNo, requestDigest, startedAt and authorization provenance are server-owned.

Interpretation and recovery

  • This operation cannot fabricate a pre-call record after dispatch or create a second logical attempt.
  • A lost response uses null responseSource and an error; it must not be recorded as a successful empty result.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Context. A second inventory poll returns unchanged database content. The adapter must record a new receipt while preserving the existing Source version.

When to use. When accepting validated API, event, stream or local source evidence under a registered profile.

Intended result. Unchanged content reuses its current Source version and still receives a new observation when the receipt is distinct.

  1. Supply the scoped source representation, exact connection and receipt facts with the appropriate channel/readAttempt context.
  2. Inspect the returned Source and Observation references for later canonical mapping or derivation.

Preconditions

  • The registered profile must validate identity, known fields, representation and digest; evidence scope must be authorized.

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Atomically resolves the stable Source identity independently of content digest, retains a new Source version when its accepted representation changes, and records a distinct Observation with an exact Source reference.
  • An unchanged consecutive receipt reuses the current Source version. A→B→A publishes versions 1→2→3; byte deduplication cannot relabel the last observation as the old version 1.
  • The registered versioned profile validates typed known members, source identity, representation and digest; raw unknown provider output remains retained evidence.
  • payload is the intentionally opaque provider document, bounded by the body cap and adapter schema; it cannot patch canonical state or set a verdict.
  • The adapter reconciles canonical entity indexes through verified mappings. Digest equality alone is not event identity; receipt dedupe includes the authenticated channel/scope.

Interpretation and recovery

  • A→B→A content creates Source versions 1→2→3, not a return to version 1.
  • Opaque provider payload cannot patch canonical state or assert a derived verdict. Receipt deduplication is distinct from byte deduplication.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Earlier operations and consolidation

The earlier PutHealthObservation separates into evidence ingestion and derived SERVICE_STATUS publication. IngestEvent also becomes retained channel evidence plus explicit collection admission.

Earlier operation / packageDispositionCurrent operations / meaning
PutHealthObservation
aws/resilience-hub/analysis/api		SHARED_TRUSTED_INGESTIngestObservation, PublishProjection

Retain runtime-health source evidence then derive SERVICE_STATUS. This is distinct from AWS Health Event ingestion.

IngestEvent
aws/resilience-hub/analysis/api		SHARED_TRUSTED_INGESTIngestObservation, StartCollection

Retains raw channel evidence and schedules authorized read collection; event body cannot patch authoritative state.

IngestObservation
consolidated-operations-console/api@db142c84bcfd691d5c71071681731cac81a52c7b		BREAKING_CONTRACT_V2IngestObservation

Use the V2 namespace and revised DTO: every entity has version/createdAt/updatedAt; evidence and historical context use exact references. Existing operation names do not imply wire compatibility.

Related next operations. GetObservation, PublishProjection.

CompleteCollection

#
INGESTCONTRACT_ONLYP2_READ_AND_INGEST

Publish the Collection’s next version with sealed, separately qualified coverage for its declared queries.

Mutating intent; a durable Command receipt is returned.

No direct native dispatch declared by this operation.
Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Close a collection with a documented detail gap

Actor. Trusted collector

Context. All declared queries have settled, but one detail hydration failed. The collector needs to finish the collection without claiming complete evidence.

When to use. After every declared query has a settled or explicitly unresolved outcome.

Intended result. The completed collection records what is known, missing and sufficient for each supported claim.

  1. Assemble coverage from attempts belonging to this Collection under registered collector rules.
  2. Submit coverage with the current Collection expectedVersion and retain the returned version.

Preconditions

  • Every coverage reference must belong to the collection; expectedVersion must guard its current head.

Request · CompleteCollectionRequest

coverageRequiredArray of CoverageMinimum items: 1
Maximum items: 100

Opaque mutation-intent token. Exact replay requires the same operation, payload and preconditions.

Minimum length: 16
Maximum length: 128
Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$

Optimistic precondition on the named entity head; never a nested value's own clock.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · CompleteCollectionResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

collectionRequiredCollectionUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Seals collection coverage after every declared query has a settled or explicitly unresolved outcome; referenced attempts must belong to this collection.
  • A coverage conclusion must be justified by registered collector rules. Successful or exhausted pages cannot alone claim source sufficiency.
  • expectedVersion guards the Collection head; completion publishes its next ordinary entity version. There is no second projectionVersion clock.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Exhausted pagination alone does not establish detail completeness or claim sufficiency.
  • Completion must preserve failed and empty reads rather than treating missing rows as proof of absence.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Foundation · operation

PublishProjection

#
DERIVECONTRACT_ONLYP2_READ_AND_INGEST

Run a registered derivation over exact evidence and publish a new immutable version of a named Projection.

Wire target
POST /
X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.PublishProjection
Media type
application/x-amz-json-1.1
Permission
console:PublishProjection · proposed application capability
Entity scope
Projection, Command
Scope members
subjectRefs
Effect
Mutating intent; a durable Command receipt is returned.
Provider dispatch
No direct native dispatch declared by this operation.
Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Refresh the qualified service-status view

Actor. Authorized projector

Context. Fresh evidence changes the status explanation for checkout. The projector must retain the earlier derivation while publishing the new one.

When to use. When an authorized rule should interpret a selected evidence set.

Intended result. A versioned derived view records the rule, inputs, coverage and computed value.

  1. Select exact subjects and input references, the registered profile and ruleDigest.
  2. Use expectedVersion=null for first publication or the current Projection version for an update, then inspect the result.

Preconditions

  • All exact inputs must be authorized and available; the rule must be registered and executable by the projector.

Request · PublishProjectionRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
projectionKeyRequiredstringMinimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096
profileRequired"EVALUATION" · "LIFECYCLE_EXPOSURE" · "INVESTIGATION_RESULT" · "SERVICE_STATUS" · "WORKSPACE_SUMMARY"

Registered profile selecting the source or interpretation contract for this record.

profileVersionRequiredstring

Version of the registered profile/schema; separate from the containing entity's version.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096
subjectRefsRequiredArray of EntityRefMaximum items: 1000

Maximum items: 10000

asOfRequiredTimestampUses the declared type and containing contract.

Optimistic precondition on the named entity head; never a nested value's own clock.

clientTokenRequiredstring

Opaque mutation-intent token. Exact replay requires the same operation, payload and preconditions.

Minimum length: 16
Maximum length: 128
Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · PublishProjectionResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

projectionRequiredProjectionUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Executes an authorized registered rule over exact entity-version inputs and publishes the next version of the same logical Projection.
  • expectedVersion=null requires that the named projection identity does not exist; a positive value guards its current head. The first publication is version 1. Concurrent incompatible publication returns VersionConflictException.
  • The request cannot supply value, generatedAt, coverage or a desired verdict. The trusted projector derives them from the selected evidence.
  • Every reference must be authorized, same-workspace and available. Missing evidence produces a qualified result or explicit failure; it never becomes success.
  • A new projection version does not change its source subjects or any earlier entity representation. Current-view selection never rewrites a sealed Run.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The request cannot provide a desired value, verdict, generatedAt or coverage.
  • Publishing does not change subject entities, freshen source evidence or rewrite a sealed workflow result.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

CaptureSnapshot

#
LOCAL_COMMANDCONTRACT_ONLYP3_DURABLE_COMMANDS

Create a deliberate closed capture of existing exact subjects and retained evidence.

Wire target
POST /
X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.CaptureSnapshot
Media type
application/x-amz-json-1.1
Permission
console:CaptureEvidence · proposed application capability
Entity scope
Snapshot, Command
Scope members
subjectRefs, members
Effect
Mutating intent; a durable Command receipt is returned.
Provider dispatch
No direct native dispatch declared by this operation.
Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Preserve topology at a review boundary

Actor. Service reviewer

Context. Before accepting a dependency governance decision, the reviewer captures the topology and supporting read evidence available at that moment.

When to use. When a review needs a stable evidence set with a declared capture kind.

Intended result. A new Snapshot identity at version 1 preserves a reviewable evidence boundary.

  1. Select exact subjects and initial members, including relevant failed or empty reads where applicable.
  2. Submit the capture and inspect the server-closed manifest and coverage.

Preconditions

  • Every selected version and the closed reference graph must be available and authorized.

Request · CaptureSnapshotRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
kindRequired"INVESTIGATION" · "TOPOLOGY" · "POLICY_CONTEXT" · "LIFECYCLE_CATALOG" · "EVALUATION_INPUT"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
subjectRefsRequiredArray of EntityRefMinimum items: 1
Maximum items: 100
membersRequiredArray of EntityRefMinimum items: 1
Maximum items: 1000
Unique items: True
clientTokenRequiredstring

Opaque mutation-intent token. Exact replay requires the same operation, payload and preconditions.

Minimum length: 16
Maximum length: 128
Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · CaptureSnapshotResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

snapshotRequiredSnapshotUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Builds a closed immutable manifest and typed contents from existing retained evidence, including failed/empty read attempts and coverage.
  • All selected subjects and members use exact (kind,id,version) references. The server closes the authorized retained reference graph without resolving any member to latest; unavailable versions reject capture.
  • The manifest does not consult mutable current fields after capture. capturedAt does not renew source timestamps or make paginated AWS reads atomic.
  • RUN_INPUT snapshots are created only during StartRun admission; clients cannot replace a Run's inputs by creating a similarly named snapshot.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Capture does not consult later entity heads or create an atomic provider view.
  • RUN_INPUT is reserved for StartRun admission; a caller-created capture cannot replace Run inputs.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

CreateWorkItem

#
LOCAL_COMMANDCONTRACT_ONLYP3_DURABLE_COMMANDS

Create local operator work with continuing typed targets, optional assignment and scheduling metadata.

Wire target
POST /
X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.CreateWorkItem
Media type
application/x-amz-json-1.1
Permission
console:ManageWork · proposed application capability
Entity scope
WorkItem, Command
Scope members
assigneeSubjectId
Effect
Mutating intent; a durable Command receipt is returned.
Provider dispatch
No direct native dispatch declared by this operation.
Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Assign follow-up for a resilience recommendation

Actor. Team lead

Context. A recommendation requires engineering analysis and the team needs one place for ownership and follow-up.

When to use. When the need is coordination, assignment or tracking work around retained domain entities.

Intended result. Operator workflow is centralized in WorkItem rather than duplicated inside each target entity.

  1. Select the target identities and provide a concrete title, plus optional priority, due date and authorized assignee.
  2. Create the work item with a clientToken and inspect its assigned local state.

Preconditions

  • The trusted workspace directory must resolve any assignee under assignment policy; the actor is server-attributed.

Request · CreateWorkItemRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
titleRequiredstringMinimum length: 1
Maximum length: 256
targetsRequiredArray of EntityIdentityMinimum items: 1
Maximum items: 100
priorityOptional"CRITICAL" · "HIGH" · "MEDIUM" · "LOW"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
dueAtOptionalTimestampUses the declared type and containing contract.
assigneeSubjectIdOptionalIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
clientTokenRequiredstring

Opaque mutation-intent token. Exact replay requires the same operation, payload and preconditions.

Minimum length: 16
Maximum length: 128
Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · CreateWorkItemResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

workItemRequiredWorkItemUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Creates local operator work; no provider state or operational conclusion is implied.
  • assigneeSubjectId resolves through the trusted workspace directory and assignment policy; it selects a work owner, never the acting principal.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Creating work does not change provider state or accept a recommendation’s conclusion as proven.
  • Targets are continuing identities; cite exact evidence separately when resolving or verifying the work.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

UpdateWorkItem

#
LOCAL_COMMANDCONTRACT_ONLYP3_DURABLE_COMMANDS

Record a server-attributed local work action and publish the WorkItem’s next version.

Wire target

Provider dispatch

Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Resolve a coordination task with supporting evidence

Actor. Assigned operator

Context. Engineering work has been completed and the operator wants to record the resolution evidence while preserving the previous work history.

When to use. When changing assignment, work state, scheduling or local notes.

Intended result. A new WorkItem version records the local action and its actor without changing target provider records.

  1. Read the current WorkItem and decide the specific fields or allowed clearFields to change.
  2. Submit the update under expectedVersion with exact resolution evidence when appropriate.

Preconditions

  • The current WorkItem version must match; evidence and any new assignee must be authorized.

Request · UpdateWorkItemRequest

Maximum length: 256

priorityOptional"CRITICAL" · "HIGH" · "MEDIUM" · "LOW"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
dueAtOptionalTimestampUses the declared type and containing contract.
assigneeSubjectIdOptionalIdUses the declared type and containing contract.

Maximum length: 16384

Maximum items: 3

Maximum length: 128

Use case

Verify that a resolved remediation has independent support

Actor. Verifier

Context. A task was marked resolved, and a verifier now has independent target-scoped evidence to assess the claimed remediation.

When to use. When evaluating the result of work after distinguishing it from the resolution action.

Intended result. verificationState and verificationEvidence advance on the WorkItem while its work state remains independently meaningful.

  1. Read the current WorkItem and select evidence that applies to its targets.
  2. Submit the qualified verification result and rationale with expectedVersion and exact evidence references.

Preconditions

  • VERIFIED requires independent supporting evidence under the registered verification policy and separate authorization.

Operation semantics

  • Records a separately authorized, qualified local verification judgment and an immutable server-attributed action under the WorkItem version.
  • All evidence must resolve to this work's target scope. VERIFIED requires independent supporting evidence under the registered verification policy; the same operator resolution action or assessment completion alone is insufficient.
  • The result updates verificationState/verificationEvidence, not WorkItem.state or any provider status, posture or historical source record.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The same resolution action or a completed assessment alone is insufficient proof.
  • This judgment does not rewrite provider status, posture or historical source records.

Introduce the commerce system into the catalog

Actor. Catalog maintainer

When to use. When adding an application-owned workload grouping.

Use case

Explain the system referenced in an older review

Actor. Architect

Context. A captured workload review names a System version. The architect wants its historical description and the provider bindings retained then.

When to use. When inspecting a system as a canonical catalog object or resolving an exact reference.

Intended result. The local system and its provider aliases can be explained without conflating their authorities.

  1. Read the specified version for the review, or omit version for current catalog navigation.
  2. Inspect providerBindings explicitly before following native evidence.

Preconditions

  • The System and its retained evidence must be authorized.

systemIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
versionOptionalVersion

Immutable representation number. In a getter request, omission selects the current head once.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · GetSystemResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
systemRequiredSystemUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • This read does not synchronously call the native system API.
  • A historical system representation does not implicitly load current journey names or service membership.

When to use. When discovering local workload groupings before drilling into journeys and services.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.

  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.

Interpretation and recovery

  • A canonical list is not a complete native provider-system inventory; unresolved native profiles may remain source evidence.
  • An empty page with a continuation token does not end the traversal.

Use case

Clarify a business-system description

Actor. Catalog maintainer

Context. The commerce system description no longer reflects its business scope. The maintainer needs to correct it without changing provider configuration.

When to use. When editing local name or description.

Intended result. The same systemId receives a new immutable representation while old references remain readable.

  1. Read the current System version and prepare only the intended metadata fields.
  2. Submit expectedVersion and a clientToken, preserving omitted values.

Preconditions

  • expectedVersion must match the current System head.

Request · UpdateSystemRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
systemIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.

Maximum length: 256
descriptionOptionalstringMinimum length: 0
Maximum length: 16384
clientTokenRequiredstring

Opaque mutation-intent token. Exact replay requires the same operation, payload and preconditions.

Minimum length: 16
Maximum length: 128
Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$
expectedVersionRequiredVersion

Optimistic precondition on the named entity head; never a nested value's own clock.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Conditional and cross-field schema rules

      ]

  ]
}

Response · UpdateSystemResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

systemRequiredSystemUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Updates the named entity under its one expectedVersion and publishes the next immutable representation, including owned values. There is no separate configuration or overlay clock.
  • Changes to separate Source, Observation or Projection identities do not change this entity. A material change to its own fields or verified bindings does advance its version.
  • Omitted fields are unchanged; an empty description is a known empty value; supplied arrays replace their complete owned membership set.
  • Service is the sole membership writer. Every journey must belong to its paired system; a journey update cannot set a second service list.

Interpretation and recovery

  • This operation does not update native sharing, policies or provider-owned system metadata.
  • System does not become a second writable owner of service membership.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Use case

Review the purpose of a critical user flow

Actor. Service reviewer

Context. A service participates in the purchase journey, and the reviewer needs to understand the business flow represented by that membership.

When to use. When following a journey identity from service membership or a capture.

Intended result. The business journey remains distinct from the operational behavior of its participating services.

  1. Provide both systemId and userJourneyId, with version for an exact historical read.
  2. Use service listing to inspect current participation when the task is live navigation.

Preconditions

  • The supplied System parent must match the stored UserJourney ownership.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.

Rename a journey after a product terminology change

Actor. Catalog maintainer

When to use. When local journey metadata changes without reparenting or provider mutation.

Preconditions

Operation semantics

  • Updates the named entity under its one expectedVersion and publishes the next immutable representation, including owned values. There is no separate configuration or overlay clock.
  • Changes to separate Source, Observation or Projection identities do not change this entity. A material change to its own fields or verified bindings does advance its version.
  • Omitted fields are unchanged; an empty description is a known empty value; supplied arrays replace their complete owned membership set.
  • Service is the sole membership writer. Every journey must belong to its paired system; a journey update cannot set a second service list.

Interpretation and recovery

  • This request cannot move the journey to another system or create a competing service list.
  • The local edit does not rename the native provider journey.

Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Inspect the service version used at run admission

Actor. Workflow reviewer

Context. A Run pins Service version 2 while the current catalog has changed. The reviewer needs the exact admitted workload representation.

When to use. When opening a live service page or resolving an exact historical Service reference.

Intended result. The service used by the review or run remains distinguishable from the current catalog head.

  1. Use the reference’s version for historical review; omit it only for a deliberate current-head read.
  2. Follow exact retained evidence for historical details and inspect provider bindings explicitly.

Preconditions

  • The service and retained reference closure must be currently authorized.

Request · GetServiceRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
serviceIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
versionOptionalVersion

Immutable representation number. In a getter request, omission selects the current head once.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · GetServiceResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
serviceRequiredServiceUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The getter does not infer runtime health; current qualified status has its own selector.
  • Reading a historical service never silently replaces its members with current versions.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Use case

Identify shared services in the purchase journey

Actor. Architect

Context. The purchase journey uses checkout and a shared data service. The architect needs the deduplicated workload set.

When to use. When navigating local workload participation.

Intended result. One canonical service identity appears once even when it has several memberships.

  1. Filter by systemId and userJourneyId where needed and traverse the fixed publication.
  2. Inspect selected services and their independent status projections.

Preconditions

  • Membership filters must refer to valid authorized catalog identities.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.
  • Service membership is many-to-many and deduplicated by canonical serviceId; it does not establish journey execution order or end-to-end compliance.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Membership does not establish journey execution order or end-to-end resilience compliance.
  • The list is a retained local view; it does not prove native inventory completeness.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, PaginationTokenExpiredException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Add checkout to another business journey

Actor. Catalog maintainer

Context. Checkout now also supports a returns journey. The catalog needs the additional membership while preserving its existing memberships.

When to use. When changing canonical name, description, membership or resource references.

Intended result. Service remains the single writable source of catalog membership.

  1. Read the current Service and assemble the complete intended memberships array.
  2. Submit the replacement array with expectedVersion and inspect the next Service version.

Preconditions

  • Every journey must belong to its paired System; expectedVersion guards the whole Service.

Maximum items: 100

Maximum items: 1000
Unique items: True

Maximum length: 128

Response · UpdateServiceResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

serviceRequiredServiceUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Updates the named entity under its one expectedVersion and publishes the next immutable representation, including owned values. There is no separate configuration or overlay clock.
  • Changes to separate Source, Observation or Projection identities do not change this entity. A material change to its own fields or verified bindings does advance its version.
  • Omitted fields are unchanged; an empty description is a known empty value; supplied arrays replace their complete owned membership set.
  • Service is the sole membership writer. Every journey must belong to its paired system; a journey update cannot set a second service list.

Interpretation and recovery

  • A supplied array replaces the complete owned set, so sending only the new member would omit existing ones.
  • Provider configuration belongs to UpdateResilienceServiceConfiguration; local editing does not mutate AWS.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Use case

Explain a service that is operationally degraded despite a completed assessment

Actor. Operator

Context. Checkout has an assessment execution marked successful while runtime evidence reports degradation. The operator needs both dimensions and their provenance.

When to use. When presenting the currently selected service interpretation.

Intended result. The view gives an evidence-qualified explanation without collapsing distinct meanings into one status.

  1. Request the service’s current status projection.
  2. Inspect runtime health, resilience posture, assessment execution, discovery and coverage independently, then follow exact evidence.

Preconditions

  • A current authorized projection must be available for the service; otherwise PROJECTION_NOT_AVAILABLE is explicit.

Operation semantics

  • Returns the currently selected SERVICE_STATUS projection under its named rule, including evidence/freshness/coverage. Clients do not infer current state from newest receipt time.
  • No current selected projection returns ResourceNotFoundException with code PROJECTION_NOT_AVAILABLE, never an invented healthy/default object.
  • Runtime health, native assessed posture, collection quality and operator workflow remain distinct dimensions.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The newest receipt time does not select authoritative status by itself.
  • Historical status uses GetProjection with the exact returned version; this selector has no historical version parameter.

Use case

Review portfolio coverage with a defensible denominator

Actor. Workspace reviewer

Context. A reviewer wants a portfolio-level view and needs to know which distinct services contribute and which evidence is usable.

When to use. When presenting the current authorized workspace summary.

Intended result. The aggregate is interpretable within the caller’s actual visible workload scope.

  1. Read the selected summary and inspect its contributor identities, denominator and rule.
  2. Drill into service-status projections to explain individual contributions or coverage gaps.

Preconditions

  • The complete returned summary must match current authorization; a broader cached summary cannot be exposed unchanged.

Request · GetWorkspaceSummaryRequest

Operation semantics

  • Returns the current qualified WORKSPACE_SUMMARY for the trusted caller's authorized workload scope, including exact distinct contributor identities, denominator and rule.
  • An empty authorized scope has null percentages. Retained historical evidence is separate from current usable coverage; no end-to-end journey compliance is inferred.
  • A cached broader summary must be recomputed/selected for the authorized scope; hidden records cannot leak through counts.

Interpretation and recovery

  • An empty authorized scope has null percentages rather than a misleading zero or full success.
  • Aggregate service results do not establish end-to-end journey compliance, and hidden records must not leak through counts.

Use case

Examine an unexpected outbound dependency

Actor. Security reviewer

Context. Checkout is observed depending on another resource. The reviewer needs the observed identity and local allow/deny decision before discussing an exception.

When to use. When reviewing one service-scoped dependency or its exact historical representation.

Intended result. The reviewer can explain both what was observed and what local policy says about it.

  1. Supply the owning serviceId and dependencyId, using version when following captured evidence.
  2. Inspect selectedObservation, rawClassification and governance as separate authorities.

Preconditions

  • The dependency must belong to the supplied Service and its evidence must be readable.

Request · GetDependencyRequest

dependencyRequiredDependencyUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • A local governance decision is not a network-control result.
  • Changing native criticality and changing local allowed/denied governance require different commands.

Actor. Service owner

Context. The owner is reviewing the dependencies known for checkout before evaluating resilience and governance decisions.

When to use. When exploring a service’s observed dependency set.

Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Document an approved dependency exception

Actor. Governance reviewer

Context. A dependency to a shared service is acceptable under a local policy exception, and the reviewer needs to record the decision.

When to use. When expressing local governance independently of provider criticality.

Intended result. The Dependency gains a new version containing the local governance decision.

  1. Read the current Dependency and inspect its observed identity.
  2. Submit the decision and reason with Dependency.expectedVersion and a clientToken.

Preconditions

  • The dependency must belong to the supplied service and the caller must have governance-write authority.

Request · UpdateDependencyGovernanceRequest

dependencyIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.

reasonRequiredstringMinimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096
clientTokenRequiredstring

Opaque mutation-intent token. Exact replay requires the same operation, payload and preconditions.

Minimum length: 16
Maximum length: 128
Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$
expectedVersionRequiredVersion

Optimistic precondition on the named entity head; never a nested value's own clock.

dependencyRequiredDependencyUses the declared type and containing contract.

Operation semantics

  • expectedVersion addresses Dependency.version. The governance value has no independent version or CRUD lifecycle; changing it publishes the next Dependency representation.
  • An allowed/denied decision is local governance. It neither changes DNS evidence nor grants/revokes network access.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The governance value has no independent identity or version clock.
  • Allowed/denied does not change DNS evidence, grant or revoke network access, or update native criticality.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Use case

Identify the regional event behind several notifications

Actor. Responder

Context. Notifications from multiple contexts refer to the same regional event. The responder needs the event identity before reviewing account impact.

When to use. When resolving the provider event itself before choosing an evidence context.

Intended result. One shared event identity can support several explicitly separated context views.

  1. Read the HealthEvent and inspect eventArn, serviceCode, impactedRegion and selectedSource.
  2. List its contexts to choose the account, public or organization-summary evidence relevant to the question.

Preconditions

  • The event and its selected source must be within current read scope.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • An EventBridge envelope ID is not the HealthEvent identity.
  • A public event does not by itself prove that an account or resource is affected.

Use case

Validate whether a database is an affected entity

Actor. Responder

Context. An account-context impact record looks like a database resource. The responder must examine its match provenance before linking it to inventory.

When to use. When drilling into one provider-identified affected entity.

Intended result. Event-relative impact remains distinct from canonical inventory and global resource health.

  1. Supply the complete HealthEvent/EventContext ownership chain and the desired impact version.
  2. Inspect native entity identity, status, selectedObservation and resourceMatches.

Preconditions

  • Both parent IDs must match stored ownership; an organization-summary context cannot own EntityImpact records.

Use case

Inspect a partially assembled notification

Actor. Responder

Context. An event notification arrived in several pages, and the visible wording may be incomplete or contradictory.

When to use. When understanding a communication’s assembly state and original delivered content.

Intended result. The responder can distinguish a complete logical communication from partial or conflicting delivery evidence.

  1. Read the communication under its HealthEvent and EventContext parents.
  2. Inspect assemblyState, grouping provenance and the retained pages before using its text.

Preconditions

  • The communication must belong to both supplied parents and its content must be currently authorized.
