Use case

Review a database engine support milestone

Actor. Platform engineer

Context. A deployed database engine appears to approach a lifecycle milestone. The engineer needs the exact catalog entry used by the exposure calculation.

When to use. When verifying a lifecycle projection’s catalog input.

Intended result. The engineer can explain the catalog fact used to evaluate the deployed component.

  1. Read the exact LifecycleEntry version cited by the projection or snapshot.
  2. Inspect catalogSnapshot, source, version labels and milestones, preserving matching provenance.

Preconditions

  • The entry’s exact source and catalog capture must be authorized and available.

lifecycleEntryRequiredLifecycleEntryUses the declared type and containing contract.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • A title or version label is not an established stable native entry ID.
  • A later catalog publication must not silently replace the entry referenced by an older exposure calculation.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The list must select through the supplied manifest, not a later snapshot head.
  • Matching titles or equal version labels alone cannot establish continuity across catalog captures.

Use case

Review the exact suggestion selected for engineering work

Actor. Engineer

Context. A work item targets a recommendation captured from finding detail. The engineer needs its source text and the estimate recorded on that recommendation.

When to use. When examining a specific suggestion or resolving its exact historical version.

Intended result. The engineer sees the captured provider suggestion and clearly separate local planning information.

  1. Provide serviceId, findingId and recommendationId, adding version for a historical reference.
  2. Inspect source, groupKey, ordinal, suggestion and enrichment before consulting the associated WorkItem.

Preconditions

  • The complete parent chain must match stored ownership and the source evidence must be readable.

findingIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
recommendationIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.

recommendationRequiredRecommendationUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Without a stable native key, equal text or the same ordinal in changed detail content does not prove continuity.
  • Local enrichment does not carry assignment, work state or verification; those belong to WorkItem.

Use case

Assess checkout after an approved configuration change

Actor. Resilience operator

Context. Configuration work is complete and the operator wants a new native assessment against the service’s current admitted configuration.

When to use. When a fresh assessment execution is required and the caller has provider-command authority.

Intended result. A durable intent can be tracked separately from the created assessment and its eventual posture evidence.

  1. Read the current Service and choose an exact authorized Connection version.
  2. Submit the Service expectedVersion and clientToken, then follow the Command until an assessment identity is reconciled.

Preconditions

  • Service and Connection versions must satisfy admission; native binding and current provider scope must be verified.

Request · StartResilienceAssessmentRequest

serviceIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
connectionRequiredEntityRef kind = "Connection"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
clientTokenRequiredstring

Minimum length: 16
Maximum length: 128
Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$
expectedVersionRequiredVersion

Optimistic precondition on the named entity head; never a nested value's own clock.

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Pins the local Service version and Connection at admission, then requests native StartFailureModeAssessment. expectedVersion is a Service precondition, not an AWS conditional-write token.
  • GetCommand exposes the created assessment identity after readback. SUCCESS of assessment execution does not imply achievable posture or verified remediation.
  • Findings remain service-scoped and independent of a particular run.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The operation maps to native StartFailureModeAssessment; it does not synchronously produce a verdict.
  • A successful assessment execution does not prove resilience or remediation, and the local version check is not AWS compare-and-swap.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

Use case

Enable native dependency discovery for a service

Actor. Resilience operator

Context. Checkout has an established native profile and the team wants to enable dependency discovery through the authorized provider access path.

When to use. When the intent concerns supported provider configuration rather than canonical catalog metadata.

Intended result. The provider request is tracked separately from observed discovery state and local service membership.

  1. Read the Service head and suitable exact native Source evidence.
  2. Submit the desired discovery setting or other supported changes with expectedVersion, expectedSource and Connection, then inspect command/readback.

Preconditions

  • The Service must have a verified native binding; connection scope and source representation must match the native object.

Request · UpdateResilienceServiceConfigurationRequest

connectionRequiredEntityRef kind = "Connection"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
expectedSourceRequiredEntityRef kind = "Source"Uses the declared type and containing contract.

Maximum length: 128

Response · UpdateResilienceServiceConfigurationResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Admits a durable command and returns its receipt. Provider dispatch and authoritative observation reconciliation occur later.
  • expectedVersion guards the named entity head. expectedSource pins the exact source evidence for the native precondition; neither creates an AWS compare-and-swap guarantee.
  • The adapter resolves verified native aliases and enforces connection scope. An ambiguous provider response becomes OUTCOME_UNKNOWN until safe reconciliation.
  • The source precondition must belong to this exact native object and an appropriate configuration/detail representation. A different object's version or a stale unrelated summary is rejected even in the same workspace.
  • The exact Connection version is recorded at admission; current permissions, revocation and material provider preconditions are checked again at dispatch.
  • Changes the verified Resilience Hub service profile only. Local UpdateService remains the canonical catalog/membership command.
  • This initial write subset covers description, Regions, direct policy attachment and desired discovery state. Native creation/deletion, association replacement, permissions, report configuration and clearing remain deferred adapter commands.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Desired discovery state is not evidence that discovery has completed.
  • Creation, deletion, association replacement, permissions, report configuration and unsupported clearing remain outside this initial command.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Operation semantics

  • expectedVersion refers to Recommendation.version. Enrichment is an owned value without a second version clock; the complete Recommendation receives the next version.
  • Estimate amount/currency/basis/complexity/source/time/confidence are typed local information, separate from native assessment execution cost.
  • Assignment, work state, completion and verification belong exclusively to a WorkItem targeting this recommendation. This operation cannot maintain a competing recommendation workflow.
  • Local estimates do not establish provider remediation or recommendation identity across changed source versions.

Interpretation and recovery

  • An estimate is distinct from native assessment execution cost and does not prove remediation.
  • Assignment, completion and verification belong to WorkItem; enrichment has no separate version clock or workflow.

Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Check the native investigation scope

Actor. Investigation operator

Context. The operator is preparing to inspect investigations and needs the retained native workspace identity and associations.

When to use. When selecting or auditing the native scope used by DevOps operations.

Intended result. The native DevOps scope is explicit without confusing it with application tenancy.

  1. Read the AgentSpace head for navigation, or the exact version pinned by a command.
  2. Inspect identity and selectedObservation before selecting a compatible Connection.

Preconditions

  • The AgentSpace and its source evidence must be currently authorized.

Request · GetAgentSpaceRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
agentSpaceIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
versionOptionalVersion

Immutable representation number. In a getter request, omission selects the current head once.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · GetAgentSpaceResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
agentSpaceRequiredAgentSpaceUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • AgentSpace is not Workspace and cannot select another application tenant.
  • A retained association is evidence, not a substitute for current dispatch authority.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Use case

Choose the investigation workspace for checkout

Actor. Investigation operator

Context. Several native DevOps spaces are represented, and the operator must choose the one associated with the intended workload.

When to use. When navigating retained native workspace scope before opening tasks or executions.

Intended result. The operator can choose a clearly scoped native workspace.

  1. Traverse the visible AgentSpace list.
  2. Inspect the selected space’s identity, associations and evidence before proceeding.

Preconditions

  • Current read permission applies to each returned AgentSpace.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The operation does not provision or switch the application Workspace.
  • A local list does not prove complete native workspace discovery or grant execution permission.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, PaginationTokenExpiredException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Use case

Understand the investigation linked from an incident

Actor. Responder

Context. An incident review links an Investigation. The responder needs its native task state and the executions actually associated with it.

When to use. When examining one investigation task in its AgentSpace.

Intended result. The task and its execution relationships remain explicit and evidence-based.

  1. Provide agentSpaceId and investigationId, choosing an exact version for a review citation.
  2. Inspect the task observation, execution pointer and membership evidence before opening executions.

Preconditions

  • The Investigation must belong to the supplied AgentSpace and its retained evidence must be readable.

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Investigation is a canonical projection of a native task, not a claim that a native GetInvestigation API exists.
  • A task pointer or task state alone does not prove an execution result.

Actor. Investigation lead

When to use. When navigating investigations after establishing AgentSpace scope.

  2. Open selected tasks and inspect their execution membership and evidence.

Use case

Actor. Investigation reviewer

Context. A review cites an asset version containing an investigation report. The reviewer needs exactly those files, even if later native asset content exists.

When to use. When following an asset citation or inspecting its current retained representation.

Intended result. The cited asset content remains reproducible through the ordinary entity version contract.

  1. Request the cited Asset version within its AgentSpace.
  2. Inspect nativeVersion, source and exact files, applying current access checks to artifact content.

Preconditions

  • The asset must belong to the AgentSpace; retained file access must be currently authorized and available.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.

Interpretation and recovery

  • nativeVersion is provider metadata, not a substitute for Asset.version.
  • There is no nested versions collection or separate AssetVersion resource; unavailable exact files never fall back to newer ones.

Actor. Investigation operator

Context. Checkout has qualified degradation evidence and the operator wants a native investigation task with a clear title, priority and context.

When to use. When intentionally creating a new native investigation task.

Intended result. The creation intent and later reconciled Investigation identity can be reviewed separately from execution progress.

  1. Read the AgentSpace head and select an exact authorized Connection.
  2. Submit title, priority and optional description under the AgentSpace expectedVersion, then follow the durable Command.

Preconditions

  • expectedVersion guards the AgentSpace head used for admission. The Connection version is pinned and current authority rechecked before dispatch.
  • A task creation receipt does not prove execution started. Native task, execution and result observations are reconciled separately.
  • The adapter maps the durable console intent to a stable provider token within native bounds; no raw tenant/actor is accepted.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The native operation is CreateBacklogTask, not a native API called StartInvestigation.
  • A task creation receipt does not prove that an execution began or that a result was produced.

Use case

Approve a reviewed single-use action

Actor. Approver

Context. An approver has inspected a concrete requested action and decides to allow that exact scope once.

When to use. Only when the complete authenticated approval context and action digest are available for review.

Intended result. The decision has a durable receipt bound to the reviewed action scope.

  1. Read the current ApprovalRequest and its exact requestSource/actionDigest.
  2. Submit APPROVED with singleUse=true, expectedVersion, exact connection and a clientToken; inspect the decision Command before any resume.

Preconditions

  • The request, source and digest must match; the first release supports exact observed scope and single use only.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • First-release decision supports exact observed scope and single use only; reusable grants and pattern editing are explicitly deferred.
  • expectedVersion guards ApprovalRequest; expectedRequestSource selects its exact retained request content. A version from another request or source object is rejected.
  • APPROVED requires singleUse=true. REJECTED omits singleUse; the adapter also omits native pattern and TTL fields for rejection.
  • Validates a complete authenticated chat request context and exact action digest, then invokes UpdateApprovalAction. It neither resumes the execution nor claims the tool ran.
  • Native UpdateApprovalAction has no modeled idempotency token. A lost response is OUTCOME_UNKNOWN; local replay returns the receipt and must not repeat the remote mutation blindly.
  • A successful rejection is a successful decision command, not a provider API failure.

Interpretation and recovery

  • REJECTED omits singleUse and native pattern/TTL fields; a successful rejection is a successful decision command.
  • UpdateApprovalAction has no modeled native idempotency token. A lost response is OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and local replay must not blindly repeat it.
  • Decision does not resume execution or prove that the tool ran.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Use case

Continue an execution after a recorded decision

Actor. Investigation operator

Context. The approval decision has reconciled successfully. The operator now needs to submit the corresponding resume context without changing the approved scope.

When to use. After a matching decision Command has an exact SUCCEEDED representation and the retained execution context is still valid.

Intended result. Resume submission remains separately observable from decision, credential use and actual tool outcome.

  1. Read the current Execution and pin the validated ApprovalRequest and the successful decision Command version.
  2. Submit ResumeExecution under the Execution expectedVersion and follow the new Command, stream evidence and execution observations.

Preconditions

  • The supplied decisionCommand must be the exact successful representation for this request; current authorization and validated interrupt/tool context are required.

commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Requires a definitively successful matching decision Command, valid current authorization and a validated approval/interrupt/tool-use context.
  • expectedVersion guards Execution; approvalRequest and decisionCommand are exact retained representations. An ACCEPTED decision version is insufficient even if a later command version has succeeded.
  • Constructs the native SendMessage APPROVAL_ACTION context from that retained request; the caller cannot substitute interrupt/tool IDs or widen approved scope.
  • Decision, resume submission, credential redemption and actual tool outcome remain separate. Opening or completing a stream does not prove the tool succeeded.
  • SendMessage has no modeled idempotency token. Persist stream fragments and unknown outcomes; do not blindly resend on disconnect.

Interpretation and recovery

  • An ACCEPTED decision version is insufficient even if the command’s current head later succeeds.
  • SendMessage has no modeled native idempotency token. A disconnected stream is not permission to resend blindly.
  • The caller cannot substitute tool or interrupt IDs, and stream completion does not prove tool success.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

GetScenario

#
READCONTRACT_ONLYP2_READ_AND_INGEST

Read a Scenario’s draft, published or archived representation through one exact-version contract.

Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Review the published program used by a completed Run

Actor. Workflow reviewer

Context. A Run pins published Scenario version 2 while version 3 is a draft. The reviewer needs the compiled program and locks used by that Run.

When to use. When inspecting current authoring state or resolving an exact execution definition.

Intended result. The executed program remains unambiguous despite subsequent editing.

  1. Pass the scenarioId and the Run’s exact scenario version.
  2. Inspect state, definition, publication facts and trusted operation locks retained on that representation.

Preconditions

  • The Scenario and its retained artifacts must be currently authorized and available.

Request · GetScenarioRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
scenarioIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
versionOptionalVersion

Immutable representation number. In a getter request, omission selects the current head once.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · GetScenarioResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
scenarioRequiredScenarioUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Omitting version may return a DRAFT head; that is not the program selected by a historical Run.
  • A native operation registry is not exposed here. A published Scenario shows its resolved locks, not every executable adapter alias.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Choose a published exercise for a new run

Actor. Workflow operator

Context. The operator wants to find scenarios whose current heads are published before choosing a specific program version.

When to use. When navigating the scenario catalog or separating draft authoring from published offerings.

Intended result. The catalog supports discovery while execution remains tied to an exact publication.

  1. List scenarios with the desired state filter.
  2. Inspect the selected Scenario and explicitly pin the intended PUBLISHED version before admission.

Preconditions

  • The caller must have current access to each returned scenario and any required retained content.

Request · ListScenariosRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
stateOptional"DRAFT" · "PUBLISHED" · "ARCHIVED"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
maxResultsOptionalinteger

Requested page bound; default 20, maximum 100. A response may contain fewer rows.

Minimum: 1
Maximum: 100
nextTokenOptionalstring

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · ListScenariosResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
itemsRequiredArray of Scenario

The operation's typed result collection. Parent/version and ordering semantics are specified below.

Minimum items: 0
Maximum items: 100
pageRequiredPage

Publication metadata for the selected traversal; it is not a domain Snapshot.

nextTokenOptionalstring

Opaque continuation for the same fixed traversal and query. Absence ends traversal.

Minimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.

Interpretation and recovery

  • state filters the selected current head, not every historical representation.
  • A later DRAFT head can coexist with an earlier executable PUBLISHED version; use history for that deliberate selection.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, PaginationTokenExpiredException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Revise a criterion without changing an already admitted run

Actor. Workflow author

Context. The error threshold in a published checkout exercise needs review. Existing runs must keep their original program.

When to use. When editing a draft or deliberately reopening a published/archived scenario for authoring.

Intended result. A new DRAFT version is created under the same scenarioId while prior publications remain retained.

  1. Read the current Scenario and prepare the authoring definition.
  2. Submit expectedVersion and the intended edits; reopening a PUBLISHED or ARCHIVED head requires an explicit definition.

Preconditions

  • expectedVersion must match the current head; a reopened non-draft needs an explicit authoring definition.

commandRequiredCommand

scenarioRequiredScenarioUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Publishes the next ordinary Scenario version in DRAFT state, under the current entity expectedVersion. Previously published versions and admitted Runs remain unchanged.
  • Omitted fields preserve draft values. Reopening a PUBLISHED or ARCHIVED head requires an explicit authoring definition; the server never treats locked published content as an editable draft implicitly.
  • Editing an ARCHIVED head is a deliberate guarded reopening. The newly created DRAFT version does not make itself executable; StartRun still requires an exact PUBLISHED version.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The new draft is not executable and cannot retarget existing Runs.
  • Omitted draft fields preserve values, but locked published content is not implicitly treated as an editable definition.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

Use case

Publish a reviewed resilience exercise

Actor. Workflow publisher

Context. The draft’s criteria, dependencies and finalizers have been reviewed, and the team wants an exact program that can be admitted reproducibly.

When to use. After authoring is complete and before starting runs from the definition.

Intended result. Publication fixes the validated program and its implementation references under one Scenario version.

  1. Read the current DRAFT and submit its expectedVersion with a clientToken.
  2. Inspect the PUBLISHED result, including resolved operation/schema locks and digest, before using its exact reference.

Preconditions

  • Compilation must validate DAGs, typed bindings, capability checks, required criteria, finalizers and fixed language/reducer semantics.

Request · PublishScenarioRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
scenarioIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.

scenarioRequiredScenarioUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Compiles the exact current DRAFT representation, resolves immutable implementation/schema locks and creates the next PUBLISHED version of the same Scenario identity.
  • Publication validates DAGs, dependency-scoped references, typed bindings, capability checks, required criteria, finalizers and fixed language/reducer semantics before any external work.
  • The caller cannot submit a trusted lock or digest. A later alias change cannot alter a published version. Missing/revoked pinned artifacts reject future admission rather than substituting another implementation.
  • GetScenario with version retrieves any retained representation; ListEntityVersions enumerates history. There is no ScenarioRevision resource or default revision pointer.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The caller cannot supply trusted locks or a chosen digest.
  • Later alias changes cannot modify this publication; unavailable or revoked pinned artifacts must reject future admission rather than substitute another implementation.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

ArchiveScenario

#
LOCAL_COMMANDCONTRACT_ONLYP3_DURABLE_COMMANDS

Create an ARCHIVED Scenario head that blocks new run admissions while preserving prior publications.

Effect

Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Withdraw an exercise pending review

Actor. Workflow owner

Context. A scenario should no longer admit new executions until its assumptions are reviewed, but its past runs and publications must remain readable.

When to use. When intentionally withdrawing the whole Scenario from new admission.

Intended result. All versions of this Scenario are blocked for new admissions while history and admitted runs remain intact.

  1. Read the current head and submit ArchiveScenario with its expectedVersion.
  2. Inspect the archived result; review existing Runs separately if they need a cancellation decision.

Preconditions

  • The caller needs archive authority and expectedVersion must match the current head.

Request · ArchiveScenarioRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
scenarioIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
clientTokenRequiredstring

Minimum length: 16
Maximum length: 128
Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$
expectedVersionRequiredVersion

Optimistic precondition on the named entity head; never a nested value's own clock.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · ArchiveScenarioResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

scenarioRequiredScenarioUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Creates the next Scenario version in ARCHIVED state, retaining the prior definition and publication facts.
  • A current ARCHIVED head blocks new Run admissions for every version of that Scenario. It does not redirect, cancel or change previously admitted Runs, and exact admission replay still returns its original receipt.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Archiving does not cancel or redirect already admitted Runs.
  • Exact replay of a prior successful StartRun still returns its original receipt after reauthorization; archival must not change that admission history.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

StartRun

#
EXECUTION_COMMANDCONTRACT_ONLYP4_WORKFLOW_RUNTIME

Atomically admit one Run with an exact published program, exact subjects/bindings, StepRuns and a closed input Snapshot.

Wire target

X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.StartRun
Media type
application/x-amz-json-1.1

Effect
Mutating intent; a durable Command receipt is returned.
Provider dispatch

Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Execute a reviewed checkout exercise

Actor. Workflow operator

Context. An operator has chosen a published exercise and authorized test scope, and now wants one auditable execution intent.

When to use. When starting a new execution from an explicit PUBLISHED Scenario version.

Intended result. Admission fixes the program, input evidence, enabled steps and criterion denominator before dispatch.

  1. Select exact Scenario, subject and Connection versions, then provide inputs matching the pinned closed schema.
  2. Submit a new clientToken for the new intent and inspect the returned Command, Run, Snapshot and StepRuns.

Preconditions

  • For a new admission, the current Scenario head must not be ARCHIVED; an intervening DRAFT does not replace the explicitly chosen publication. Subjects and bindings must satisfy current admission authority.

Request · StartRunRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
scenarioRequiredEntityRef kind = "Scenario"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
subjectRequiredEntityRefUses the declared type and containing contract.
inputsRequiredMap<string, JsonValue>Maximum properties: 100
bindingsRequiredMap<string, EntityRef kind = "Connection">Maximum properties: 100
Map keys: Minimum length: 1; Maximum length: 64; Pattern: ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$
clientTokenRequiredstring

Opaque mutation-intent token. Exact replay requires the same operation, payload and preconditions.

Minimum length: 16
Maximum length: 128
Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · StartRunResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

runRequiredRunUses the declared type and containing contract.
snapshotRequiredSnapshotUses the declared type and containing contract.
stepsRequiredArray of StepRunMinimum items: 0
Maximum items: 100

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Durably admits one Run at version 1, its StepRuns and a closed RUN_INPUT snapshot atomically; no claim that an AWS call has started.
  • scenario pins an exact PUBLISHED Scenario version. The current Scenario head is checked separately: ARCHIVED blocks new admission; a newer DRAFT does not replace the explicitly selected published program.
  • subject and connection bindings pin exact versions. Admission requires the subject and binding versions still meet the current admission preconditions; current authorization and material provider preconditions are rechecked at dispatch.
  • inputs must pass the published version's pinned closed input schema; unknown binding names, raw secrets, undeclared operations or unauthorized scope are rejected.
  • Admission fixes enabled steps and the required-criterion denominator. Runtime skips/cancellation cannot shrink it; inapplicable admission criteria remain recorded.
  • A new execution intent uses a new clientToken. Neither a latest selector nor a mutable default pointer may select the executed program.

Interpretation and recovery

  • HTTP 200 and Run phase ADMITTED do not mean an AWS call has started.
  • Runtime skips or cancellation cannot shrink the admitted required-criterion denominator.
  • Retrying the same semantic request uses the same token; a genuinely new execution intent uses a new token.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Explain a run whose workflow ended but cleanup remains uncertain

Actor. Workflow reviewer

Context. The main workflow has ended, yet an external effect has unresolved reconciliation. The reviewer needs more than one success flag.

When to use. When monitoring an admitted run or reading an exact historical representation.

Intended result. The run’s operational progress and workload conclusion remain independently explainable.

  1. Read the current Run head for monitoring, or a cited version for historical review.
  2. Inspect phase, executionOutcome, assessmentVerdict/finality, finalizationState and effectState separately; follow exact input and step references.

Preconditions

  • The Run and its retained evidence closure must be currently authorized.

Request · GetRunRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
runIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
versionOptionalVersion

Immutable representation number. In a getter request, omission selects the current head once.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · GetRunResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
runRequiredRunUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.

Interpretation and recovery

  • A successful HTTP read is not a successful run; successful execution is not automatically a passing workload criterion.
  • A later understanding belongs in new evidence or an evaluation projection and does not rewrite a sealed Run.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

Actor. Workflow reviewer

When to use. When locating run identities before inspecting their captured inputs and outcomes.

Intended result. The reviewer can compare executions without losing the program version that each used.

  1. Filter by the exact Scenario reference or phase as appropriate and traverse the fixed publication.
  2. Open selected Runs and compare their exact admission evidence and independent result dimensions.

Preconditions

  • Scenario filters and returned Run closures must be authorized; the query must remain unchanged during pagination.

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.

  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.

Interpretation and recovery

  • The list selects one head per Run identity within its traversal, not every historical Run version.
  • Shared Scenario identity alone does not prove identical program, subject, inputs or provider targets.

RequestRunCancellation

#
EXECUTION_COMMANDCONTRACT_ONLYP4_WORKFLOW_RUNTIME

Record monotonic cancellation intent under the current Run version and fence new main dispatch.

Wire target

X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.RequestRunCancellation
Media type

Effect
Mutating intent; a durable Command receipt is returned.
Provider dispatch
No direct native dispatch declared by this operation.
Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Cancel an exercise after an uncertain provider start

Actor. Workflow operator

Context. An exercise is no longer desired, but a provider start response was lost and the external effect may already exist.

When to use. When the operator intends to stop further main execution and enter bounded reconciliation/finalization.

Intended result. The first accepted cancellation intent becomes part of Run history without fabricating a remote stop result.

  1. Read the Run head and submit the cancellation reason, expectedVersion and clientToken.
  2. Inspect the returned Run/Command, then monitor effect reconciliation and finalization separately.

Preconditions

  • expectedVersion must match after replay resolution. A new intent against a matching sealed Run returns accepted=false without changing it.

Request · RequestRunCancellationRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
runIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
reasonOptionalstringMinimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096
clientTokenRequiredstring

Opaque mutation-intent token. Exact replay requires the same operation, payload and preconditions.

Minimum length: 16
Maximum length: 128
Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$
expectedVersionRequiredVersion

Optimistic precondition on the named entity head; never a nested value's own clock.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · RequestRunCancellationResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

acceptedRequiredbooleanUses the declared type and containing contract.
runRequiredRunUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Under the supplied current Run.version, atomically records monotonic cancellation intent in the next version and fences new main dispatch. It does not set a remote effect to stopped.
  • Exact replay is resolved before current-version checks. If the expectedVersion still matches an already sealed Run, the command returns accepted=false and that unchanged terminal representation.
  • Finalizers reconcile active/unknown effects, including a lost Start response with no handle. A creating Start must never be reissued after cancellation just to discover its result.
  • Concurrent cancellation intents converge on the first accepted intent after version/replay resolution. Cleanup, execution result and workload verdict remain independently visible.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Cancellation does not declare provider effects stopped or workload recovery complete.
  • A creating Start must never be reissued after cancellation merely to discover a lost handle; unresolved effects retain their protection/hold.
  • A stale new intent conflicts; exact replay returns the original receipt before current-version checks.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

    }

  "notes": [

    "The listed exact representation is the current head at this illustration's admission; later fixture versions belong to another point in history."
  ]
}

Use case

Reconstruct the step view of a past Run representation

Actor. Workflow reviewer

Context. The Run head has advanced since an incident review. The reviewer needs the StepRun versions that belonged to the earlier Run state.

When to use. When displaying or auditing a Run’s immutable step selection.

Intended result. The parent’s historical step view cannot acquire later child state.

  1. Pass runId and the chosen runVersion; omission deliberately selects the Run head once.
  2. Follow returned exact StepRun versions in retained compiled order, including skipped zero-attempt steps.

Preconditions

  • Current authorization applies to the selected Run and each referenced child; missing exact child versions fail the read.

Use case

Review an uncertain native operation attempt

Actor. Workflow analyst

Context. A fault-injection step dispatched a native operation but could not establish its result. The analyst needs the exact attempt facts and external-operation evidence.

When to use. When inspecting why a step selected an attempt or why an effect remains unresolved.

Intended result. The attempt’s recorded execution facts remain independently reviewable.

  1. Supply the complete parent chain and exact StepAttempt version referenced by the StepRun.
  2. Inspect outcome, checkResult, externalOperations and evidenceRefs without inventing a later success.

Preconditions

  • The attempt must belong to the given StepRun and Run, and its evidence must be authorized.

Actor. Workflow reviewer

#
READCONTRACT_ONLYP2_READ_AND_INGEST

Read a native FIS experiment independently from any application workflow Run.

Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Inspect what a fault experiment actually affected

Actor. Fault-experiment operator

Context. A workflow links a native experiment. The operator needs its native state, named action states, selected targets, effect evidence and report readiness.

When to use. When following an external-operation link or reviewing an imported experiment.

Intended result. The native experiment can be understood on its own terms while retaining any verified workflow relationship.

  1. Read the exact Experiment version referenced by evidence, or its current head for monitoring.
  2. Inspect named actions, target memberships, resolution coverage and report facts separately from the workflow’s assessment verdict.

Preconditions

  • The experiment and retained observation must be authorized within its provider scope.

Request · GetExperimentRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
experimentIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
versionOptionalVersion

Immutable representation number. In a getter request, omission selects the current head once.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · GetExperimentResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
experimentRequiredExperimentUses the declared type and containing contract.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Returns retained canonical data with its provenance; does not fetch AWS synchronously.
  • An explicit version selects that exact immutable representation. Omission selects the current head once. An absent/unavailable version never falls back to another version.
  • Every supplied parent must agree with the stored record; a mismatch is not a cross-scope search.
  • Native actions are keyed by experiment + actionName; their catalog actionId is not an execution identity.
  • Selected memberships, applied effects, workload criteria and report readiness are separate evidence dimensions.

Interpretation and recovery

  • An action’s catalog actionId identifies an action type; execution identity is experiment plus actionName.
  • Selected targets, applied effects, workload criteria and report completion are separate evidence dimensions.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, EvidenceUnavailableException.

Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Find the experiment associated with an exercise

Actor. Workflow operator

Context. A Run may have a reconciled native experiment, and the operator wants to locate that experiment without confusing it with unrelated imported experiments.

When to use. When navigating native experiments after provider evidence has been retained.

Intended result. Native experiments remain discoverable whether or not they were created by a product Run.

  1. Use connectionId or runId filters as appropriate.
  2. Inspect each returned experiment and verify the retained external-operation link before attributing it to the workflow.

Preconditions

  • The caller must have current experiment-read authority and the run filter must use verified ExternalOperationRef links.

Request · ListExperimentsRequest

Operation semantics

  • Stable local snapshot traversal returns one selected head per logical identity, pinned to the traversal's publication; nextToken is absent only at the end.
  • Each returned entity carries version, createdAt and updatedAt. ListEntityVersions enumerates the retained versions of one identity separately.
  • A completed local traversal does not establish complete upstream collection or claim coverage.
  • runId filters only verified ExternalOperationRef links; imported experiments can have no product workflow Run.

Interpretation and recovery

  • An imported experiment can validly have no Run.
  • A similar name, template or timestamp does not prove workflow membership.

StopExperiment

#
PROVIDER_COMMANDCONTRACT_ONLYP3_DURABLE_COMMANDS

Admit a provider request to stop one whole native FIS experiment.

Wire target
POST /
X-Amz-Target: ConsolidatedOperationsConsole_20261105V2.StopExperiment
Media type
application/x-amz-json-1.1
Permission
console:StopExperiment · proposed application capability
Entity scope
Experiment, Command
Scope members
experimentId, connection, expectedSource
Effect
Mutating intent; a durable Command receipt is returned.
Provider dispatch
StopExperiment · adapter target, not a wire-compatible console alias
Contract source
Operation metadata · Request / response schemas

Use case

Stop a fault experiment whose effects need reconciliation

Actor. Fault-experiment operator

Context. The operator has verified the target experiment and wants the native stop request tracked separately from its final state and cleanup.

When to use. When intentionally requesting a whole-experiment stop through an authorized connection.

Intended result. The stop request has a durable receipt while final native state and recovery are established through evidence.

  1. Read the Experiment head and its suitable exact Source precondition.
  2. Submit expectedVersion, expectedSource and an exact Connection with the stop intent, then follow the Command and experiment observations.

Preconditions

  • The source must belong to the same native experiment; connection scope and current dispatch authority must be valid.

Request · StopExperimentRequest

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
experimentIdRequiredIdUses the declared type and containing contract.
connectionRequiredEntityRef kind = "Connection"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
expectedSourceRequiredEntityRef kind = "Source"Uses the declared type and containing contract.
clientTokenRequiredstring

Opaque mutation-intent token. Exact replay requires the same operation, payload and preconditions.

Minimum length: 16
Maximum length: 128
Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$
expectedVersionRequiredVersion

Optimistic precondition on the named entity head; never a nested value's own clock.

reasonOptionalstringMinimum length: 1
Maximum length: 4096

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Response · StopExperimentResponse

FieldPresenceType / allowed valuesMeaning and constraints
commandRequiredCommand

Durable intent receipt. An accepted external command is not proof of provider completion.

Closed object: undeclared members are rejected by this schema. Required means present; a permitted null remains a value.

Operation semantics

  • Admits a durable command and returns its receipt. Provider dispatch and authoritative observation reconciliation occur later.
  • expectedVersion guards the named entity head. expectedSource pins the exact source evidence for the native precondition; neither creates an AWS compare-and-swap guarantee.
  • The adapter resolves verified native aliases and enforces connection scope. An ambiguous provider response becomes OUTCOME_UNKNOWN until safe reconciliation.
  • The source precondition must belong to this exact native object and an appropriate configuration/detail representation. A different object's version or a stale unrelated summary is rejected even in the same workspace.
  • The exact Connection version is recorded at admission; current permissions, revocation and material provider preconditions are checked again at dispatch.
  • Requests native StopExperiment for the whole experiment; no individual native action stop/retry/pause command is fabricated.
  • Stop acceptance, final native state, post-action cleanup, workload recovery and report completion remain separate.
  • Starting new fault experiments is available only through an explicitly authorized pinned workflow adapter in this initial facade.

Interpretation and recovery

  • Stop acceptance does not prove final state, post-action cleanup, workload recovery or report completion.
  • No individual native action stop, pause or retry API is invented.
  • This request does not replace Run cancellation; workflow intent and native effect handling remain separately explicit.

Declared errors. ValidationException, UnauthenticatedException, AccessDeniedException, ResourceNotFoundException, ThrottlingException, InternalServerException, ServiceUnavailableException, IdempotencyConflictException, CommandInProgressException, InvalidStateException, VersionConflictException.

Transport rejection also uses the shared size and media-type errors. The error reference describes HTTP status, retryability and recovery.

08 · Error reference

Recover without changing the intent accidentally

Clients parse the typed exception, stable code and structured field paths. Human messages are explanatory. A retryable console error does not authorize reissuing an uncertain provider mutation; Command state and adapter reconciliation govern that decision.

ExceptionHTTPRetryableMeaningRecovery
ValidationException400NoInvalid syntax, field, union, scalar or semantic input; no accepted mutation.Correct the fields, union, precision or reference scope before retrying.
UnauthenticatedException401NoNo verified caller identity.Establish a current verified caller identity.
AccessDeniedException403NoCaller or connection lacks permission for the complete subject/evidence scope.Restore valid current authority if appropriate; denial is not an empty result.
ResourceNotFoundException404NoIdentity is absent or invisible in its trusted workspace and required parent scope.Verify the exact visible identity/version and required parents. Do not substitute a current head.
VersionConflictException409NoThe named entity head no longer has expectedVersion; no mutation was admitted.Read and review the changed head. A deliberate new intent requires a new token and chosen precondition.
IdempotencyConflictException409NoThe same operation/clientToken was used with different intent or precondition.Keep the original payload for replay, or use a new token for a genuinely new intent.
CommandInProgressException409YesA matching durable token reservation is in flight; reconcile the returned command and retry the exact request.Inspect the returned command; retry the identical token and payload after the supplied delay.
InvalidStateException409NoState, scope, binding, source precondition or cross-record invariant prevents this command.Reconcile the relevant state, source context, bindings and invariants before a deliberate new intent.
PaginationTokenExpiredException410NoThe traversal snapshot expired; explicitly begin a new traversal.Explicitly restart traversal; do not merge a new publication into an expired one.
EvidenceUnavailableException410NoRetained content is expired, redacted or unavailable; its identity and known history remain.Surface the retention/unavailability outcome; do not infer absence, success or a fallback version.
RequestTooLargeException413NoThe request exceeds the declared byte or collection bound.Reduce the body or use the declared managed artifact path; obey both byte and collection bounds.
UnsupportedMediaTypeException415NoThe request is not application/x-amz-json-1.1.Use application/x-amz-json-1.1.
ThrottlingException429YesAdmission capacity is limited; honor retryAfterSeconds and keep the original token.Honor retryAfterSeconds with bounded backoff and retain the same mutation intent token.
InternalServerException500YesAn internal failure prevented a complete response; outcome requires receipt reconciliation.Reconcile the durable receipt; a missing response does not establish that no effect occurred.
ServiceUnavailableException503YesTemporarily unavailable; retry the exact intent only within the recorded replay contract.Retry the exact intent within its replay guarantee; reconcile uncertain effects first.

Error body fields are specified by RpcError and FieldViolation.

  "requestId": "req-token-demo",
  "retryable": false
}

09 · Adapter profiles

Keep the native source inspectable

The 65 registered profiles describe native identity, payload field hints, read operations and unknown-provider-output retention. A profile is not automatically a new CRUD entity. Its observedFields are descriptive hints, not executable native SDK schemas. A normalized binding is credited only where the coverage audit establishes a typed owner/profile representation. The listed native operations describe provider coverage; only the operation catalog above defines the console facade.

Trace the model back to the earlier work

History is linked to exact repository commits. “Introduced by consolidation” identifies an application abstraction, not a previously existing AWS resource. Names retained as aliases are crosswalk evidence, not additional current entities.

Earlier analysisFrozen inventoryContribution
DevOps Agent58 filesTasks, executions, journal evidence, observed membership, approvals and investigation UI contracts.
FIS and general workflow55 filesNative experiments, targets/actions/reports, plus generalized scenario/run/step/attempt and adapter contracts.
Health26 filesEvent/context/impact, communication, delivery, lifecycle catalog, exposure and local work.
Resilience Hub87 filesSystem/journey/service structure, dependency topology, assessment context, findings, recommendations and the earlier 44-operation facade.

The frozen inventory contains 226 active files across the four service directories, with generalized workflow and resilience RPC work nested inside them. Complete previous-work inventory · Paths, sizes, hashes and history.

All 174 mapping rows and 340 recorded aliases are retained here, including owned values, projections and deferred native breadth.

Representation labels describe the earlier consolidation decision. The verified audit status alongside each reviewed source concept qualifies that claim; several owned-value labels currently resolve only to retained native content. Coverage counts and gaps · Representation decision rules.

Canonical source register

  1. Current model, identity and versioning — model/schema.json
  2. Model explanations and invariants — MODEL.md
  3. Typed RPC input/output contract — api/rpc.schema.json
  4. Operation metadata and predecessor mappings — api/operations.json
  5. Protocol, concurrency, replay and coverage — api/PROTOCOL.md
  6. Historical concept mappings and adapter profiles — model/adapter-profiles.json
  7. Synthetic entity representations — model/examples.json
  8. Synthetic operation examples — api/examples.json
  9. Editable diagrams and reviewed export manifest — diagrams/model.drawio
  10. Review findings and correction decisions — REVIEW.md
  11. Validation evidence and runtime limits — VALIDATION.md

The HTML is generated from those checked contracts and the editorial notes in reference/entity-notes.json and reference/operation-notes.json. It intentionally preserves the source baseline while adding a complete navigable explanation. Generation inputs and coverage checks are recorded in reference/build-report.json.

The audit identifies 63 substantive source entity concepts in the four original AWS solution catalogs: 29 provider-owned and 34 application-defined. The consolidated model represents them through 36 versioned target entities, owned values and retained profiles. The mapping is many-to-many.

Name coverage is complete; semantic normalization is qualified.

All 130 diagram symbols resolve to registry aliases. For the four AWS solutions, 74 of 119 (62.2%) have normalized core representations. The remaining statuses identify concrete limitations. ExperimentMetricBinding has no accountable experiment → exact binding/query/window relationship in the current target model.

Coverage levelRequired evidence
NORMALIZEDThe source construct's essential application meaning has a bound typed representation. Optional provider details may remain retained evidence; complete SDK validation is a separate question.
PARTIALA typed core exists but a required distinction, relationship, binding or invariant is missing or ambiguous.
RETAINED ONLYConcrete Source/profile retention preserves inspectable content without complete typed application normalization. This can be an intentional scope choice.
UNMAPPEDNo concrete representation sufficient to preserve the construct's essential meaning was established. A name or generic JSON storage is insufficient.
