Findings and next decisions

FindingEvidence-backed issueRecommended decision
COV-HR-01
Localized EventDescription is declared but unbound

health:EventDescription

Bind the existing value to the correct contextual owner/profile if normalized description access is required; otherwise classify it explicitly as retained-only. Do not add a description entity.
COV-HR-02
Health failedSet item scope is absent from normalized errors

health:CollectionItemError

Represent per-item event/account failure and partial-success outcome through a typed owned collection or registered response shape; keep transport failures separate.
COV-HR-03
OrganizationHealthAccess registry targets omit its actual owner

health:OrganizationHealthAccess

Correct registry target metadata to include Workspace and the OrganizationAccess binding. The model already has the appropriate owned value.
COV-HR-04
Match confidence and lifecycle candidate semantics need an explicit disposition

health:EntityResourceMatch, health:LifecycleExposure

Decide and document whether candidate maps to UNKNOWN and whether confidence is resolved from the rule/evidence or exposed as a small owned value. Avoid claiming exact semantic parity until that rule is explicit.
COV-HR-05
Effective target values remain retained rather than normalized

resilience-hub:EffectiveTarget, resilience-hub:EffectivePolicyEvidence

Keep the already normalized service-scoped observation envelope and exact PolicyContext references. Add a typed owned eight-metric value contract, with units and source-policy provenance, bound through the existing Source/profile or capture where normalized target-value access is required. Reconcile policyType versus ownership-source naming; do not infer a policy ARN or inheritance from a label.
COV-HR-06
Policy component read-shape validation can be tightened

resilience-hub:PolicyComponent

Retain the existing normalized PolicyComponent owner binding. Document or enforce allowed known metric keys, numeric/integer semantics and unit rules per component family; RPC ResiliencePolicyChanges and RecoveryTargetsInput already provide narrower native edit shapes. This is a validation-completeness finding, not a missing component representation or a reason to create another entity.
COV-HR-07
Finding capture assessment correlation lacks a typed basis

resilience-hub:FindingCapture

Preserve optional same-service related-assessment reference and correlation basis as a small owned capture/query-context value, or explicitly defer this former facade capability.
COV-HR-08
Recommendation identity is normalized but its content is arbitrary JSON

resilience-hub:RecommendationEntity

Bind ordered suggestedChanges/category content to a typed value when normalized comparison/rendering is required. Retain raw provider evidence for extension and do not create native recommendation IDs.
COV-HR-09
Native topology edge property collections are not normalized

resilience-hub:TopologyEdge, resilience-hub:EdgeProperty

Define lossless property expansion/grouping or an owned properties collection carrying native type and optional inferred label. Preserve source grouping and same-snapshot endpoints.
COV-HR-10
Operational event subject linkage remains untyped

resilience-hub:EventSubject

Bind typed event subjects with role, scoped identity and linkage evidence if the timeline/subject use case is in scope. Native envelope resources alone do not establish those application relationships.
COV-HR-11
Source reference tombstone semantics have no explicit target field

resilience-hub:EntityRef

Define the minimal deletion/visibility observation and how historical references resolve it; do not add a version-only or tombstone-only entity by default.
COV-HR-12
Runtime-health and component-posture evidence are retained profiles

resilience-hub:HealthObservation, resilience-hub:PostureObservation

Keep retained evidence coverage separate from typed measurement/component-outcome coverage. Select concrete owned observation schemas from product use cases before claiming normalized signal or component parity.
COV-HR-13
Native administration and auxiliary configuration are intentional retention boundaries

health:EventType, health:AggregateSnapshot, resilience-hub:DependencyDiscoveryConfig, resilience-hub:PermissionModel, resilience-hub:InputSourceEntity, resilience-hub:ServiceResource, resilience-hub:ServiceFunction, resilience-hub:ResourceDiscovery, resilience-hub:DNS queryRange

Retain these registered native profiles and declare their product normalization/command deferrals explicitly. They do not each justify a new first-class entity.
DEVOPS-COV-01
Registry rows and aliases do not count independent entities		The registry groups Task/Investigation and generic/journal-specific revisions as aliases, while the source assigns them different native/application or specialization roles. The 52 SDK shapes additionally contain many nested values and wrappers.

devops-agent:Task, devops-agent:Investigation, devops-agent:SourceRevision, devops-agent:JournalRecordRevision

Count the 34 independently extracted class/ER symbols as a fixed declaration benchmark, retain a separate semantic concept catalog, and show native resources, values and wrappers in separate subtotals.
DEVOPS-COV-02
Timeline and richer investigation assertions are retained, not normalized projections		Named source profiles exist, but each has descriptive typedContent text, not a normalized result schema. Projection.profile is closed to five profiles and only INVESTIGATION_RESULT covers a dedicated DevOps result shape.

devops-agent:TimelineItem, devops-agent:Finding, devops-agent:EvidenceItem, devops-agent:Hypothesis, devops-agent:RootCauseAssessment, devops-agent:MitigationProposal, devops-agent:ReviewResult, devops-agent:ActionObservation

Keep retention explicit in the coverage total. Promote a concrete supported use case through an owned typed result and registered Projection profile with exact provenance; do not introduce one new entity or revision entity per assertion kind.
DEVOPS-COV-03
Native journal attribution is not an ActorRef binding		The crosswalk labels UserReference as an owned ActorReference, but JournalRecord has no attribution member and ActorRef is the trusted command actor {issuer,subject,kind}. Native userId/userType survives only in raw journal payload.

devops-agent:UserReference

Correct the crosswalk to retained-only until a distinct owned native-attribution value or explicit reviewed identity mapping is defined. Do not infer an actor when native attribution is absent.
DEVOPS-COV-04
Graph structure exists but required graph meaning and provenance are incomplete		The model preserves owned endpoint keys, relationKind and evidence, but lacks an explicit node kind, assertion origin and unresolved-placeholder state. The source also distinguishes more graph-view meanings and provenance/validity facts than the current closed graphKind/claimKind fields.

devops-agent:GraphSnapshot, devops-agent:GraphNode, devops-agent:GraphEdge

Add only the owned graph fields needed by supported graph views and retain exact evidence, rather than treating every graph node as a new canonical entity. Test an unresolved placeholder and an operator-asserted causal edge as semantic cases.
DEVOPS-COV-05
Approval context is pinned but invocation and scope values remain raw		ApprovalRequest pins source/digest and nativeApprovalId, but interruptId, toolUseId, tool and argumentPins are only described by a source profile. No ApprovalPattern/ApprovalAction owned model value exists. The original source itself warns that approval request content is not a universal native typed entity.

devops-agent:ApprovalRequest, devops-agent:ApprovalPattern, devops-agent:ApprovalAction

Define and validate the particular observed request profile before dispatch. If typed normalized access is needed, add an owned invocation/scope value with field-presence semantics; preserve request source/digest and keep decision, resume and effect separate.
DEVOPS-COV-06
Collector and coverage-policy identity are not retained as typed metadata		The source CollectionPass contract includes collector version/selection policy and CoverageClaim retains evaluation policy. Current Collection/CollectionQuery/Coverage capture query, window, attempts, dimensions and rationale but no explicit versioned collector/policy binding.

devops-agent:CollectionPass, devops-agent:CoverageClaim

Represent collector/evaluation policy identity as a small owned binding on the appropriate collection/coverage owner, or explicitly defer it. Do not treat free-text rationale as an exact policy version or add policy-version entities.
DEVOPS-COV-07
Generic artifact storage descriptors do not fully normalize cross-channel artifact references		Managed artifact locators, asset files and exact evidence locators are typed, but the original ArtifactReference carries channel/record/block/native-ID/optional-asset-resolution semantics and finer unavailability reasons that are not a single current owned value.

devops-agent:ArtifactReference

Keep the source reference inspectable and state this as partial normalization. Add a channel-aware owned reference only when a concrete inline, A2A or native Asset use case requires it; never equate those identifiers.
DEVOPS-COV-08
The decision Command receipt does not expose a reconstructable decision input		The prior decision-attempt entity records action/finalized-pattern hash. The console has a typed DecideApproval request, but its readable Command record exposes only operation/requestDigest/subjects and lifecycle; it has no retained request source or typed decision value.

devops-agent:DecisionAttempt

Specify how an authorized historical audit resolves the exact submitted decision input from the Command. A typed owned intent value or exact request-source reference is sufficient; a standalone version entity is not required.
DEVOPS-COV-09
Peripheral native resources are represented only by retained source profiles		Each native resource has an explicit source profile and preserves identity/lifecycle vocabulary, but none has a normalized dedicated model or complete product capability. Homonyms are correctly kept separate from workload Service, resilience Recommendation, console Scenario and Connection.

devops-agent:RegisteredService, devops-agent:Goal, devops-agent:Recommendation, devops-agent:Trigger, devops-agent:PrivateConnection

Count these as retained resource representations, not normalized entity coverage or implemented AWS integration. Promote a resource only after its domain use case and lifecycle authority justify that model/API surface.
DEVOPS-COV-10
SnapshotProjection crosswalk wording uses obsolete target field names		The preservation note still says imported legacy renditions are pinned in sourceRevisionIds, although the current Snapshot contract uses members of exact EntityRef(kind,id,version).

devops-agent:SnapshotProjection

Use sourceRevisionIds/projectionRevisionId only when naming old source vocabulary; describe current bindings as Snapshot.members with exact Source or Projection versions.
DEVOPS-COV-11
Native Task normalization selects one task discriminator		The pinned native Task catalog includes INVESTIGATION, EVALUATION, RELEASE_READINESS_REVIEW and RELEASE_TESTING. The normalized Investigation contract deliberately describes the INVESTIGATION facet only; other types are retained native task documents.

devops-agent:Task, devops-agent:Investigation

Keep the Investigation concept normalized and report the broader native Task family as partial. Add another domain facet only for a supported use case, rather than pretending all task types are Investigations.
COV-FIS-01
Retained provider configuration is mislabeled as normalized owned values		The mapping calls these ownedValue representations, but their named typed classes/properties do not exist. Complete payloads have deliberate Source retention paths. This is not data loss, but it is not normalized contract coverage.

fis:TargetSelection, fis:ExperimentTargetAccount, fis:StopCondition, fis:ActionParameterDefinition, fis:ActionTargetSlot, fis:TemplateAction, fis:TemplateTarget, fis:TemplateBinding, fis:TemplateDependency, fis:TemplateTargetAccount

Mark retention-only explicitly with exact profile and JSON member paths. Promote only the small owned values required by current queries; native template/account/lever management can remain deferred.
COV-FIS-02
Resolved memberships lack a typed selector join		Action bindings name selectors, but memberships provide only selectionKey, whose fixture value combines selector and resource. No documented typed selector field or canonical encoding makes that relation safely queryable. Empty selectors also have no normalized record.

fis:ResolvedTargetMembership, fis:TargetSelection, fis:ActionTargetBinding

Use a small Experiment-owned selector value/key and an explicit selector reference/key on TargetMembership. Keep opaque membership identity separate; retain the complete raw selector and targetInformation in Source. No new entity is needed.
COV-FIS-03
Telemetry binding and experiment-assessment linkage are not concretely mapped		MetricBinding/MetricBindingReference/CheckDefinition names in the crosswalk do not resolve to concrete value shapes or bound input schemas. ExperimentMetricBinding has no property/relation at all. The metric profile documents fields but does not bind typed samples or query/window/unit semantics. Evaluation can target an Experiment without a Run, so a Run-only generic input is insufficient.

fis:MetricBinding, fis:ExperimentMetricBinding, fis:MetricObservation, fis:AssessmentCriterion

Define narrow versioned profile/input schemas for telemetry queries, samples and criterion parameters; bind them to Source/Scenario or captured evaluation contents. Represent the experiment-to-exact-binding/window association as an owned reference value in captured evaluation context, preserving no-Run assessments.
COV-FW-01
Attempt recovery facts have no declared value contract		The source specifies once-evaluated/sealed inputs, typed durable checkpoints and structured technical errors. The current attempt tracks identity, status, evidence and external effects but has no checkpoint/resolved-input contract or workflow error value. ReadError belongs to collection and is not a substitute.

workflow:StepAttempt, workflow:ExecutionError

Add only the durable owned facts required for exact resume/input/error interpretation, or explicitly defer their normalization and identify their retained typed profile. Keep transient lease/queue implementation details outside the domain model.
COV-FW-02
Evidence ownership and production/import roles need an explicit consolidation rule		Shared Source/Observation and exact references are appropriate, but they do not explicitly preserve the earlier run-owned evidence manifest, producer/import role, or the complete typed adapter Observation result. The mapping prose currently claims those roles remain explicit.

workflow:Evidence, workflow:Observation

State how run evidence closure is selected and represent producer/consumer/import provenance as an owned citation value where required. Define registered adapter-result schemas for value/collection/coverage/scope/window. Do not add a duplicate Evidence or Version entity.
COV-FW-03
A normalized profile advertises fields absent from its bound value		The profile and predecessor describe actual/expected summaries, but the bound CheckResult schema has neither. Core check outcome, evidence and cutoff are normalized, so this does not remove CheckResult concept coverage.

workflow:CheckResult

Say which details remain in retained Source and which are normalized, or add a narrow optional explanatory value if a reviewed use case requires it.
COV-FW-04
Evaluation profile identity wording retains removed revision-resource names		identityBasis still says projectionRevisionId and inputSnapshotId even though V2 uses a stable Projection identity/version and exact Snapshot reference.

fis:ResilienceAssessment

Update the profile wording to the current common entity/version/reference contract; do not reintroduce revision entities.

Correct the coverage claims first, then bind existing types or add narrow owner-local values for required use cases. Preserve intentional retained-only administration breadth. No finding requires a version-only entity; the audit does not change the model or API contracts.

12 · Mapping rule catalog

A consistent decision for each AWS construct

Use these rules to map a new AWS construct or revise an existing mapping. Establish identity and ownership first; preserve versions, evidence and state meaning; then record the exact representation and its coverage level. An entity is introduced for a substantive lifecycle, and every entity uses the common version contract.

MAP-01 · Count source concepts, aliases and target entities separatelyMAP-02 · Promote a concept to an entity for identity and lifecycleMAP-03 · Keep versions on the substantive entityMAP-04 · Use owned values for details with one lifecycle ownerMAP-05 · Preserve full provider identity independently of accessMAP-06 · Give relationships one owner and explicit provenanceMAP-07 · Keep retained content, receipt and interpretation distinctMAP-08 · Retain native DTO breadth without claiming normalizationMAP-09 · Use typed projections for conclusions and viewsMAP-10 · Separate historical captures from ordinary version historyMAP-11 · Model collection coverage and per-item failures explicitlyMAP-12 · Preserve independent state dimensions and meaningsMAP-13 · Give local work and mixed authority explicit ownersMAP-14 · Separate API DTOs and commands from entity readsMAP-15 · Treat admission, replay and external outcome as separate factsMAP-16 · Preserve metric and evaluation meaning in typed contractsMAP-17 · Keep presence, future provider values and units losslessMAP-18 · Keep external identity and administration at their real boundaryMAP-19 · Require a concrete proof for each coverage claimMAP-20 · Close gaps with the smallest coherent extension

MAP-01 · Count source concepts, aliases and target entities separately

Use a declared source population and retain source-service scope. Count a diagram symbol once per source service; collapse naming aliases only when the source establishes that they mean the same concept. Never treat mapping rows, native DTO names or spelling aliases as entity totals.

Required evidence

  • A pinned source file and exact declaration or dictionary entry
  • An explicit alias decision and source semantic kind
  • An independently extracted denominator and per-population counts

Example. The source Task and application Investigation aggregate remain two source constructs even when both contribute to consolidated Investigation. HealthEvent and HEALTH_EVENT can be spelling aliases of one concept.

Failure to avoid. Reporting 340 aliases or 174 mapping rows as 340 or 174 represented entities.

Acceptance. Every declared source symbol resolves to exactly one audited construct; source and target totals are reported as a many-to-many mapping.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/MAPPING.md
consolidated-operations-console/model/adapter-profiles.json

MAP-02 · Promote a concept to an entity for identity and lifecycle

Use a first-class entity when the application needs to identify, authorize, retrieve, relate or retain the concept independently through its lifecycle. A native resource can supply that identity, but a native DTO or a screen section alone does not justify a new root. A scoped child may still be an entity when it has meaningful identity and lifecycle.

Required evidence

  • Stable or explicitly provisional identity with full scope
  • A lifecycle and authoritative publisher
  • A concrete cross-module use case requiring independent references or reads

Example. Experiment, Finding and Execution have substantive identities and lifecycle. An experiment action remains an owned FISAction when its control and interpretation belong to the Experiment.

Failure to avoid. Creating one console CRUD entity for every AWS response structure, action parameter or configuration block.

Acceptance. The proposed entity has one owner/version contract and an explicit use case that cannot be represented clearly as an owned value or retained source profile.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Experiment; #/$defs/Finding; #/$defs/Execution; #/$defs/FISAction.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md
aws/fis/analysis/report.md

MAP-03 · Keep versions on the substantive entity

Every entity has stable identity plus version, createdAt and updatedAt. An old revision/history class maps to a version of its substantive owner or to exact evidence of that owner. Do not introduce an entity whose only purpose is to hold a version. Provider versions, schema versions and attempt numbers remain separate domain values.

Required evidence

  • A documented logical key independent of content digest
  • A source-ID/version migration rule
  • Exact references to retained representations

Example. ScenarioRevision maps to a PUBLISHED Scenario version. AssetVersion maps to an Asset representation with nativeVersion/source/files. SourceRevision maps to Source identity plus version.

Failure to avoid. Reintroducing ScenarioRevision, SourceRevision or separate governance/enrichment version counters.

Acceptance. All target entities require the common metadata; owned values have no competing entity clock and historical reads never fall back to latest.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Scenario; #/$defs/Asset; #/$defs/Source; #/$defs/EntityRef.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/MODEL.md
consolidated-operations-console/api/PROTOCOL.md

MAP-04 · Use owned values for details with one lifecycle owner

Represent parameters, policy components, action details, files and configuration values inside their owning entity when they have no independent application lifecycle. Their local keys can identify members, but their changes advance the owner's version. A standalone value definition is insufficient unless an owner actually binds it.

Required evidence

  • A reachable typed owner property or a discriminator-enforced binding
  • Collection semantics, member keys and relevant cardinality
  • Owner-level concurrency and publication rules

Example. Asset.files contains AssetFile values and Scenario.definition contains StepDefinition values. A declared EventDescription type with no owner binding does not establish normalized description coverage.

Failure to avoid. Pointing a crosswalk to a value name that is absent, unbound, or reachable only through untyped JSON.

Acceptance. The typed value is reachable from the named owner under the correct discriminator, and the source concept's essential semantics can be expressed there.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Asset/properties/files; #/$defs/Scenario/properties/definition; #/$defs/StepDefinition; #/$defs/EventDescription.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/model/schema.json
aws/fis/analysis/workflow/model.md

MAP-05 · Preserve full provider identity independently of access

Retain provider/service, partition, account, region, parent keys and native identity where applicable. A Connection records the authorized access path; it does not determine native object identity. Friendly names, unqualified IDs and digests cannot establish cross-source identity.

Required evidence

  • A source-specific identity tuple and stability statement
  • Verified provider bindings or explicit unresolved identity
  • The parent ownership required for reads and mutations

Example. Health event context qualifies impacts by event/account context. FIS pod identity includes cluster and namespace. Switching the reader connection does not create a new native object.

Failure to avoid. Joining different native objects by name, or duplicating an object for every credential/connection that observes it.

Acceptance. Identity is scoped and stable where supported; ambiguity remains explicit and no reference itself grants authority.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/SourceIdentity; #/$defs/OwningScope; #/$defs/Connection; #/$defs/ProviderBinding; #/$defs/ResourceMatch.

Sources.
aws/health/analysis/report.md
aws/fis/analysis/report.md
consolidated-operations-console/api/PROTOCOL.md

MAP-06 · Give relationships one owner and explicit provenance

Represent membership and association facts as owned values or qualified references unless they need an independent lifecycle. Specify the authoritative writer, parent consistency, direction and observation evidence. Derive inverse indexes instead of introducing a second mutable authority.

Required evidence

  • Owner and member identity
  • Parent consistency and inverse-view rules
  • Evidence for imported or inferred association claims

Example. Service owns System/UserJourney memberships. Execution task memberships are observed relations; one mandatory Investigation parent must not be invented.

Failure to avoid. Two editable service lists, fabricated parentage, or an unqualified inferred relationship presented as a provider fact.

Acceptance. A relationship's owner, key and evidence are explicit, and a historical relationship does not join current parent content silently.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Service/properties/memberships; #/$defs/ServiceMembership; #/$defs/TaskExecutionMembership; #/$defs/Execution.

Sources.
aws/resilience-hub/analysis/report.md
aws/devops-agent/analysis/annexes/Investigation_Data_Model.md

MAP-07 · Keep retained content, receipt and interpretation distinct

Map native content to Source, its observation occurrence to Observation, and a computed interpretation to Projection. A repeated poll can observe the same Source version. Changed content advances the Source; receipt order is not provider event order.

Required evidence

  • Stable source identity and representation/profile/operation key
  • Exact Source reference on each observation
  • Provider, transport, observation and local publication time meanings

Example. EventRevision and EntityRevision contribute retained Source versions and observations without creating new event or impact identities for every poll. A→B→A content yields successive versions, not a return to version 1.

Failure to avoid. Counting repeated receipts as new domain objects, conflating observation time with provider time, or refreshing evidence freshness by recomputing a view.

Acceptance. Source identity, observation occurrence and interpretation identity are independently explainable and use the same entity-version mechanism.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Source; #/$defs/Observation; #/$defs/Projection.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/MODEL.md
aws/devops-agent/analysis/annexes/Investigation_Data_Model.md

MAP-08 · Retain native DTO breadth without claiming normalization

Keep native summaries, detail documents, streams, nested values and deferred administration shapes in registered Source profiles with their unknown fields and provider values. State explicitly when the representation remains raw retention. A profile's observedFields hints do not constitute an enforced normalized model or implemented adapter.

Required evidence

  • Registered profile and complete source identity
  • Known field hints plus unknown-field/value retention policy
  • Named normalization and mutation deferrals

Example. A native FIS template or DevOps Trigger can remain inspectable through Source without becoming a console CRUD root. A retained target selector is not a typed Experiment target-selection collection.

Failure to avoid. Calling an arbitrary Source.payload or an existing profile ID complete normalized coverage.

Acceptance. Retention coverage and typed model coverage have separate statuses; no unsupported product capability is inferred from a retained payload.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Source/properties/payload; #/$defs/Source/properties/profile; #/$defs/FieldPresence.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/model/adapter-profiles.json
consolidated-operations-console/CONTEXT_AND_SCOPE.md

MAP-09 · Use typed projections for conclusions and views

Represent a computed result with a declared Projection profile, a typed result shape, exact inputs, rule identity, cutoff and coverage. A UI view, timeline or graph name alone does not prove that a corresponding normalized profile exists. Preserve uncertainty and candidate selection rules.

Required evidence

  • A registered discriminator that binds to a schema
  • Exact subject and input references
  • Selection/reducer meaning and coverage requirements

Example. LIFECYCLE_EXPOSURE, INVESTIGATION_RESULT and EVALUATION are typed profiles. A retained TimelineItem profile must not be counted as a typed Projection profile unless its result contract is actually added.

Failure to avoid. Inventing an unavailable profile, presenting an inferred hypothesis as native truth, or dropping the rationale behind a current status.

Acceptance. The schema/profile combination can encode the source view's essential semantics, and later interpretation creates another representation without rewriting old evidence.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Projection; #/$defs/LifecycleExposure; #/$defs/InvestigationResult; #/$defs/Evaluation.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/model/schema.json
consolidated-operations-console/model/adapter-profiles.json

MAP-10 · Separate historical captures from ordinary version history

Use Snapshot for a deliberate closed historical capture over exact entity representations and evidence. Use ordinary entity history for successive versions of one identity. Structural parent IDs and raw JSON must not become implicit joins to current state.

Required evidence

  • Exact retained members and closure rules
  • Capture interval/cutoff and coverage
  • Typed contents binding where normalized capture semantics are claimed

Example. A topology capture owns GraphContents; a policy-context capture owns PolicyContext. Snapshot.members pins entity versions instead of embedding competing authoritative entity copies.

Failure to avoid. Treating Snapshot as a universal untyped replacement for every missing model, or reconstructing an old assessment from today's policy/configuration.

Acceptance. Historical captures are reproducible from their exact members, and typed capture contents preserve the relevant source semantics.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Snapshot; #/$defs/GraphContents; #/$defs/PolicyContext; #/$defs/EntityRef.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/api/PROTOCOL.md
aws/resilience-hub/analysis/report.md

MAP-11 · Model collection coverage and per-item failures explicitly

Represent bounded queries and reads with Collection and ReadAttempt, retaining empty successes and failures. Qualify pagination, detail, identity and claim coverage independently. A batch's failed item must retain its subject/context; HTTP success or a completed page chain does not prove a complete claim.

Required evidence

  • Fixed query, authorization and parent scope
  • Request/response evidence including empty and partial success
  • Error subject identity and independent coverage dimensions

Example. AWS Health failedSet entries need event/account attribution. A general transport ReadError alone cannot serve as a normalized item-error collection.

Failure to avoid. Treating HTTP 200 as complete success or mapping a collection of contextual item failures to one undifferentiated error.

Acceptance. The model can explain precisely what was requested, what returned, which subjects failed and what claims the evidence supports.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Collection; #/$defs/ReadAttempt; #/$defs/ReadError; #/$defs/Coverage.

Sources.
aws/health/analysis/report.md
aws/fis/analysis/report.md
consolidated-operations-console/api/PROTOCOL.md

MAP-12 · Preserve independent state dimensions and meanings

Map provider state, technical execution, acceptance, cleanup, artifact readiness, local disposition and work verification separately. Preserve the original vocabulary and qualification. Similar labels from different AWS products are not interchangeable states or entity kinds.

Required evidence

  • Each state dimension's owner and evidence
  • Unknown/unavailable semantics
  • A documented mapping for every normalized interpretation

Example. The FIS report's local RESILIENCE_ASSESSMENT is an EVALUATION projection, not the native ResilienceAssessment entity. An approved tool action is not proof of resumed execution or success.

Failure to avoid. Merging distinct assessments because names match, or interpreting completed execution as successful acceptance or remediation.

Acceptance. Independent dimensions can disagree without losing information; source and target meanings are explicit in the crosswalk.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Run; #/$defs/ServiceStatus; #/$defs/ResilienceAssessment; #/$defs/Evaluation; #/$defs/ApprovalRequest.

Sources.
aws/fis/analysis/report.md

MAP-13 · Give local work and mixed authority explicit owners

Keep assignment, completion and verification in WorkItem. Keep recommendation estimates/notes and dependency governance in their owning entity as values with narrow write authority. All fields of a given entity still serialize through its one version boundary.

Required evidence

  • Field authority and command owner
  • Exact verification evidence
  • One expectedVersion guard for each changed entity

Example. Recommendation.enrichment has no independent workState or version. Dependency.governance has application authority while observed fields retain collector authority, using the same Dependency version.

Failure to avoid. Separate overlay clocks, duplicated task ownership, or local completion changing provider impact/finding state.

Acceptance. There is one owner for each editable value and no hidden mutation under an unchanged entity version.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/WorkItem; #/$defs/Recommendation/properties/enrichment; #/$defs/Dependency/properties/governance.

MAP-14 · Separate API DTOs and commands from entity reads

Map request/response wrappers as transport shapes, not domain entities. Expose deliberate operations with closed writable inputs. Distinguish a local catalog edit from native dispatch; a provider action is only present when an explicit command contract and authority exist.

Required evidence

  • Operation effect, permission and input/output schemas
  • Named target entity and expected-version/source preconditions
  • Native operation binding or explicit deferral

Example. UpdateService edits local catalog metadata; UpdateResilienceServiceConfiguration is an explicit provider command. A native SendMessage event union remains a stream DTO rather than another entity per event variant.

Failure to avoid. Generating CRUD from a native response shape or claiming a deferred AWS write exists because its payload is retained.

Acceptance. Read models and write DTOs are separate and every external effect has a named durable command boundary.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Command; #/$defs/Service.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/api/operations.json
consolidated-operations-console/api/PROTOCOL.md

MAP-15 · Treat admission, replay and external outcome as separate facts

Map intent to Command and later outcome to authoritative observations and entity versions. Use immutable receipts, intent tokens and current authorization. A retryable console response cannot authorize blindly repeating an uncertain creating provider call.

Required evidence

  • Exact admitted intent and returned version references
  • Replay identity and expiry guarantees
  • Native effect identity and non-creating reconciliation

Example. A decision Command can be accepted before provider approval is definitive. ResumeExecution requires the exact successful decision version and approval context. Cancellation does not establish remote cessation or cleanup.

Failure to avoid. Replaying latest results instead of the original receipt, or conflating accepted stop/cancel with completed cleanup.

Acceptance. The application can distinguish requested, admitted, dispatched, observed, failed and uncertain effects without rewriting prior records.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Command; #/$defs/ExternalOperationRef; #/$defs/CancellationIntent.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/api/PROTOCOL.md
aws/fis/analysis/workflow/model.md

MAP-16 · Preserve metric and evaluation meaning in typed contracts

When a metric, criterion or evaluation is normalized, retain query identity, dimensions, units, aggregation/window rules, missing-data semantics, threshold/evaluator identity and denominator. A generic binding or arbitrary inputs map is insufficient proof that those contracts exist.

Required evidence

  • Typed metric/query and criterion definitions or an explicitly pinned operation schema
  • Exact evidence and evaluation cutoff
  • Fixed required-criterion denominator and units/absence policy

Example. The admitted workflow criteria must not shrink when a step is skipped. A named MetricBinding crosswalk requires a real typed value/profile binding before it can be counted as normalized.

Failure to avoid. Treating a missing sample as zero, a JSON inputs bag as a metric model, or skipped checks as a higher pass rate.

Acceptance. A retained evaluation can be interpreted from its exact definition, evidence, denominator and evaluator contract; unknown inputs remain unknown.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/StepDefinition; #/$defs/CheckResult; #/$defs/Admission; #/$defs/Evaluation.

Sources.
aws/fis/analysis/report.md
aws/fis/analysis/workflow/model.md

MAP-17 · Keep presence, future provider values and units lossless

Preserve unknown native fields/enums and distinguish omitted, null, empty, zero, unavailable and not requested. State units and time precision explicitly. Writable normalized inputs remain closed and strict; read tolerance must not manufacture success.

Required evidence

  • Source field-presence and raw-payload retention
  • Units, time and normalization rules
  • Output-tolerance and input-validation boundaries

Example. An omitted Health aggregate account breakdown is not zero affected accounts. Unknown FIS runtime state is retained instead of mapped to success. Native timestamp precision remains in source evidence if normalized precision differs.

Failure to avoid. Defaulting unfamiliar provider values to healthy/completed, or deleting richer detail because a later summary omits it.

Acceptance. A consumer can distinguish unavailable or unrequested information from a known value and inspect the original source when normalization is incomplete.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/FieldPresence; #/$defs/Source; #/$defs/Timestamp; #/$defs/StateDimension.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/api/PROTOCOL.md
aws/health/analysis/report.md

MAP-18 · Keep external identity and administration at their real boundary

Reference accounts, organizations, credentials, external resources and integration configuration without inventing duplicate ownership. Retain administrative breadth through named profiles until a concrete use case requires normalized management. Historical configuration is evidence, never a surviving permission grant.

Required evidence

  • Actual external owner and identity scope
  • Current access checks independent of retained versions
  • Explicit managed-versus-referenced responsibility

Example. Workspace is the application scope; AgentSpace is a native DevOps object. Account and organization references do not become new console tenancy entities, and a captured credential reference cannot restore revoked access.

Failure to avoid. Conflating provider account/AgentSpace with application tenancy or treating stored configuration as authorization.

Acceptance. The console owns only its stated domain and preserves the external identifiers and current authorization boundaries needed for its use cases.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Workspace; #/$defs/AgentSpace; #/$defs/Connection; #/$defs/OrganizationMembership; #/$defs/OrganizationAccess.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/CONTEXT_AND_SCOPE.md
consolidated-operations-console/api/PROTOCOL.md

MAP-19 · Require a concrete proof for each coverage claim

Record source evidence, semantic kind, owner, exact schema paths, profile bindings and preserved invariants per construct. Distinguish NORMALIZED, RETAINED_ONLY, PARTIAL and UNMAPPED. A pointer's existence is structural evidence; semantic completeness still needs source-to-target review.

Required evidence

  • Source declaration and prior use
  • Resolvable target schema pointers and registered profile IDs
  • Essential semantic checks and any limitations

Example. A GraphEdge type proves typed endpoints and relationKind; it does not by itself prove preservation of every native edge relation/property grouping. A named but unbound EventDescription is not complete normalized coverage.

Failure to avoid. A green alias-existence check being reported as complete model or adapter coverage.

Acceptance. Every status is inspectable, denominators are reproducible, gaps have clear remedies, and runtime conformance is reported separately.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/GraphEdge; #/$defs/EventDescription.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/tools/validate.py
consolidated-operations-console/model/adapter-profiles.json

MAP-20 · Close gaps with the smallest coherent extension

First bind an existing typed value correctly, then add a narrow owned value/profile if the use case requires it. Introduce a new entity only if identity, lifecycle and authority justify it under MAP-02. Keep consciously retained-only capabilities explicit and avoid generic mutable extension bags.

Required evidence

  • The user-facing use case affected by the gap
  • The smallest typed owner/profile change and migration impact
  • Validation examples and a deliberate API decision where writes are involved

Example. A missing Experiment selector collection or contextual batch-error collection usually calls for typed owned values, not ExperimentSelectorVersion or CollectionItemErrorVersion entities. Deferred native administration can stay retained-only.

Failure to avoid. Repairing coverage by adding a class for every source name, or claiming completeness by placing everything in generic JSON.

Acceptance. The correction restores required meaning while preserving a simple owner/version contract and explicit scope; entity count increases only when justified.

Current contract evidence. #/$defs/Experiment; #/$defs/ReadAttempt; #/$defs/Source.

Sources.
consolidated-operations-console/DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md
consolidated-operations-console/CONSOLIDATION_PLAN.md

Generated from the reviewed model and API contracts. All examples are synthetic; no service, provider mutation or production runtime is represented as implemented.
